items.body: Happy golden anniversary to the International Computer Music Conference! This special album honors founder David Wessel (1942–2014). The full title of the 2025 theme: Curiosity, Play, Innovation—A 50th Anniversary Celebration of Creativity in Music, Science and Technology. This generous collection showcases electro-acoustic music from around the world. Each piece is intricate and unique, while many touch upon contemporary themes, starting with Jiajing Zhao‘s “Glitchopolis,” a commentary on information overload. The very first sound is that of an alarm, doubled and then tripled, set against London traffic, which begins to fracture, stutter and glitch. Garbled human voices emerge from a processed vat; construction and technology intertwine. A bee – real and metaphoric – buzzes by, followed by a flock of birds, fireworks and a police siren. How many inputs can one brain handle? “Pardon me, ‘scuse me, sorry,” a commuter apologizes at the end. By refusing to mute the signals, the composer imitates the feeling of being overwhelmed, not only aural, but emotionally. “Rumors, approximated” by Shane Turner with Simone Pitot (Delorca) uses algorithms to translate sound into data. The textures are the key, but as patterns emerge, questions of value arise: are these patterns authentic or unintentional? And how much of the human remains after technology has had its say? While Pitot purposely subjected her vocals to this process, other parts of life are unwittingly fed to the whims of the machine. Zeo Lin‘s Escape, whose opening minutes flirt with the dance floor, is filled with glass crashes and computer beeps, percussion and synth, piano and breath, representing a clash between the organic and the electronic, its movements marked by the click of a cassette. At the end a church bell tolls, only to by subsumed by static. Daniele Valenti‘s “CAN you hear them?” is particularly clever, derived almost entirely from the timbres of cans. Without knowing this, one might only guess at the nature of these sounds. The knowledge allows one to lean in,, to cherish the sounds made by the humble object that one often kicks down the road or discards without any attention to its aural qualities. Can a can sound like traffic, or rain? Yes, it CAN. In contrast, “Hammerklavier” uses the piano as its acoustic source, with Antonio Argentieri doing pretty much everything but playing the keys. Think of Matmos’ Ultimate Care II, which performed a similar feat with a washing machine. Few would ever guess that this is a piano piece, which exponentially increases its appeal. How does it feel to be “an international student with limited English proficiency” in London? Hongquan Yang and Fan Zu attempt to translate the experience in “Rambling,” starting with a traditional classroom speech about sound, then feeding it through echo, loop and reverb, injecting their own language to return the favor. Soon everyone is confused, yet finds common ground in the tempo and the playful approach. Passing grade! The chimes and choral tones of the beautifully titled “A Poem for Little Things” turn out to have been taken from children’s toys; as the mother of twins, Chung Eun Kim‘s aural environment has been altered, and she has responded by altering it right back, finding rhythm and melody, wonder and awe, in a castanet, maraca or toy xylophone. “Decorate beauty” is the concept behind Peter Dickson Lopez and Ensemble MISE-EN. “Mise En Series I” begins as a pure chamber piece before the electro-acoustic elements enter; the timbre approaches drone, as the instruments swell with sound, underpinned by pensive electronics. As if coming full cycle, Liu Yurai‘s “The Shackle” is inspired by a visit to the thousand-year-old Daci Temple, an oasis of peace located in the heart of Chengdu. The contrast between peace and overload (as first addressed in “Glitchopolis”) is palpable. Tapping and texting sounds overlap and threaten to undo all calm; a train clacks by; passengers chatter. Soon the bicycle bells are replaced by temple bells, the incoherent conversations with chants, the traffic with birdsong, and a sense of balance is restored. Unfortunately, albeit realistically, the outside world keeps rushing back in. “Seascape Serenity” readjusts the scene. Yu Chia Kuo and SinYu Deng pack the soundscape with hydrophone recordings that reflect the ecosystems of Taiwan. Just as one wished for the serenity of the temple in “The Shackle,” one wishes for humans to stop polluting the biophony of this piece. And yet, this is part of the lesson: that marine life is at least as stressed as we are and that we have caused both. While the piece attempts a happy ending, increasing the number of species calls, one wonders how realistic this might be; the title becomes less a reflection of the piece than an elegy. Taken as a whole, Best of the Listening Rooms demonstrates incredible range while managing to flow beautifully as a whole. The collection is sociologically enlightening yet retains a sense of fun, honoring the theme. Most couples are winding down by their golden anniversary, but we have a feeling that the International Computer Music Conference is just getting started. (Richard Allen)
items._genre: electroacoustic / experimental / glitch / algorithmic composition / field recording
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑为国际计算机音乐会议五十周年纪念专辑，收录全球电子声学音乐作品。赵嘉靖的《Glitchopolis》以警报声、伦敦交通噪音与失真人声模拟信息过载的感官体验。Shane Turner与Simone Pitot合作的《Rumors, approximated》通过算法将声音转化为数据纹理，引发关于人类与机器关系本质的反思。林泽的《Escape》融合有机与电子元素，玻璃碎裂声与合成器、钢琴、呼吸声交织，磁带咔哒声标记结构转换。Daniele Valenti的《CAN you hear them?》几乎完全以罐头声响为素材，展现日常物品被忽视的声音美学。Argentieri的《Hammerklavier》将钢琴作为非传统声源，探索乐器的非常规演奏方式。杨鸿全与范祖的《Rambling》通过回声、循环与混响处理课堂录音，呈现国际学生在语言障碍下的生活体验。整体作品在声音设计、算法作曲与跨文化视角上展现出高度的实验性与创新性。

items.body: For all its stunning virtuosity, the tumbling fingerstyle guitar of Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo is always in service to a set of brilliant compositional ideas Digging through the various improvised solo and duo recordings Swedish guitarist Finn Loxbo has made over the last decade is like witnessing a slow-motion creative winnowing, observing how a feverish pile of ideas and experiments has gradually coalesced into something inscrutable. His third solo album Lummernikt is a work of astonishing focus and originality forged from familiar notions, a free improvisation practice patiently chiseled into compositional rigour. Across eight riveting acoustic pieces played live without overdubs, Loxbo melds extended technique, fingerstyle fluency and self-devised preparations to deliver one of the year’s most beguiling, detailed and beautiful... The post Not the How But the What: Lummernikt by Finn Loxbo appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: free improvisation / fingerstyle guitar / experimental composition / contemporary acoustic
items._cn_summary: 瑞典吉他手Finn Loxbo的第三张个人专辑《Lummernikt》收录了八首现场录制的原声作品，全程无叠加录音。他在指弹吉他技法中融入了扩展演奏技巧与自制的吉他准备物，将近十年间积累的自由即兴实验逐步凝练为严密的作曲结构。评论指出，这些作品的高难度炫技始终服务于精妙的作曲构思，展现出从大量即兴素材中提炼成型、形成独特声响美学的过程。专辑既保留了即兴的鲜活感，又具备作曲层面的内在逻辑，在熟悉的原声吉他框架内开拓出原创而细腻的表达空间。

items.excerpt: Shadowlands, a new international music festival at the Gulbenkian Arts Centre in Canterbury, England, has added 16 acts to its debut edition running 1-4 July 2027, bringing the final line-up to 35 names across the alternative, electronic, avant-garde and experimental fields. The additions, announced 10 September, include These New Puritans, Matmos, Årabrot, Hula, Barry Adamson, Sunroof, JG Thirlwell (solo), Negativland, Globo, The Soft Pink Truth, Carl Stone, 2nd Gen, Mischievous Misappropriator
items.body: Shadowlands, a new international music festival at the Gulbenkian Arts Centre in Canterbury, England, has added 16 acts to its debut edition running 1-4 July 2027, bringing the final line-up to 35 names across the alternative, electronic, avant-garde and experimental fields. The additions, announced 10 September, include These New Puritans, Matmos, Årabrot, Hula, Barry Adamson, Sunroof, JG Thirlwell (solo), Negativland, Globo, The Soft Pink Truth, Carl Stone, 2nd Gen, Mischievous Misappropriators, Monosum, M.C. Schmidt and Obel Feldi, and Rangelova as DJ. The festival launched on 2 July with 19 acts already confirmed, among them Foetus performing as a 20-piece chamber orchestra, Lustmord, Test Dept., Clock DVA, The Wolfgang Press, Portion Control, :Zoviet*France, Warrington-Runcorn New Town Development Plan, Regis (with Liam Andrews) and People Like Us. The event spans three performance spaces on the University of Kent campus, alongside a programme of talks, Q&As and film screenings. Several of the new additions mark returns or firsts. Sheffield industrial funk band Hula are reforming for their first live show in almost four decades. Barry Adamson is premiering a new solo show, “Gone Undercover.” JG Thirlwell performs his solo soundtrack to the 1962 Harry Smith film “Heaven and Earth Magic” in the UK for the first time. Negativland play the UK for the first time in eight years, and 2nd Gen for the first time anywhere since 2009. The Soft Pink Truth, a Matmos offshoot, makes its first UK appearance since 2008, while M.C. Schmidt and Obel Feldi, another Matmos-related project, make their UK debut. Sunroof, the duo of Mute Records founder Daniel Miller and producer Gareth Jones, add a rare live outing to the bill. Githead – Colin Newman of Wire, Malka Spiegel of Minimal Compact and Robin Rimbaud aka Scanner – reunite after a 13-year hiatus, with Newman and Spiegel also performing separately as Immersion. Rimbaud joins Vicki Bennett of People Like Us and Carl Stone for a rare live outing of their trio project Mischievous Misappropriators. As previously announced, JG Thirlwell’s Foetus set is a European exclusive drawing on his 2026 album “HALT” and earlier material, presented as a large orchestral format for only the second time and his first UK appearance as Foetus in over 25 years. Lustmord plays the UK for the first time in almost a decade. Shadowlands is co-founded by David Sefton, former Head of Artistic Development at the Royal Festival Hall/Southbank Centre in London, who originated the Meltdown festival in 1993. Co-founder Gerard Myers stated the festival’s line-up was built around artists he and Sefton wanted to see together rather than genre or era, adding that some acts agreed to reform once approached. Sefton described the goal as identifying “the most exciting line-up of the most adventurous music ever made” and then booking it. The festival has 450 tickets available, including a three-monthly-payment option, with on-site accommodation bookable now via the official site. Canterbury’s proximity to London, mainland Europe and major airports is positioned as part of the event’s appeal. Shadowlands 2027 full line-up Foetus (20-piece chamber orchestra), Lustmord, Test Dept., Clock DVA, The Wolfgang Press, Portion Control, :Zoviet*France, Warrington-Runcorn New Town Development Plan, Regis (feat. Liam Andrews), People Like Us, These New Puritans, Matmos, Årabrot, Hula, Barry Adamson, Sunroof, JG Thirlwell (solo), Negativland, Globo, The Soft Pink Truth, Carl Stone, 2nd Gen, Mischievous Misappropriators, Monosum, M.C. Schmidt and Obel Feldi, Githead, Immersion, and Rangelova (DJ). About Shadowlands Shadowlands is a new boutique international festival taking place across four days at the Gulbenkian Arts Centre on the University of Kent campus in Canterbury, England, from 1 to 4 July 2027. It was co-founded by David Sefton, former Head of Artistic Development at the Royal Festival Hall/Southbank Centre in London and originator of the Meltdown festival, together with Gerard Myers. The festival describes itself as “The Outside Of Everything,” positioning its programme around artists spanning industrial, electronic, avant-garde and experimental music rather than a single genre or era. Beyond concerts, the festival includes talks, Q&As and film screenings across three venues. Several headline acts connect to Side-Line’s own coverage history: Clock DVA issued a remastered “Sensorium” single ahead of its “Thirst” 45th-anniversary reissue earlier in 2026, and its member Adi Newton also performs at Shadowlands as T.A.G.C. The Canterbury debut follows a first-wave announcement of 19 acts on 2 July, expanded to 35 with the additions confirmed on 10 September.
items._cn_summary: Shadowlands 是2027年7月将在英格兰坎特伯雷Gulbenkian艺术中心首演的国际音乐节，横跨实验、前卫、电子、另类及先锋领域，最终阵容达到35组艺人。新增名单包括These New Puritans、Matmos、Årabrot、Hula、Barry Adamson、Negativland等，多个项目的演出具有特殊意义：Hula重组近四十年后的首场现场，Barry Adamson首演新独奏项目，JG Thirlwell在英国首次呈现其1962年Harry Smith电影配乐独奏版，Negativland八年来首次赴英演出。Githead在中断13年后重组，Wire成员Colin Newman与Minimal Compact成员Malka Spiegel同时以Immersion名义分头演出。Foetus将以20人室内乐团编制呈现2026年专辑《HALT》素材，作为欧洲独家。音乐节联合创始人David Sefton曾于1993年创立Meltdown音乐节，策展理念聚焦冒险与实验性。

items.body: The title gives it away. ]ex(s)it(u)[ is a “concept album.” The cover photograph might initially suggest a bucolic collection of field recordings, but Leonardo Barbierato has other ideas. Birdsong is indeed one of the first sounds we hear, accompanied by delicate guitar plucking and live processing. From the outset, the surrounding environment enters into the performance alongside instrumental gestures, electronics and the acoustic properties of each location. Each of the seven Patchwork pieces functions as an individual study within a larger trajectory. Their subtitles — “margine” [margin], “l’ora di punta” [peak hour], “la mania del controllo” [control freakery], “frammenti di frizione eco-tonale” [fragments of ecotonal friction], “infestazione” [infestation], “condizionamento” [conditioning] and “hauntology” — provide a loose conceptual map. As Barbierato explains in the accompanying interview, the recordings grew out of five years of site-specific performances, with the characteristics of each location feeding directly into the music. The album only came into focus retrospectively, when excerpts from those performances were edited into a coherent sequence. Throughout ]ex(s)it(u)[, electronics, acoustic gestures and environmental recordings continually interact, their respective roles shifting from one piece to the next. Barbierato calls this condition “eco-tonality”, describing the intertwining of ecosystemic and performative sounds and the fluid identities that result. “l’ora di punta” allows guitar melodies to emerge from and disappear back into circuitry; “la mania del controllo” frustrates attempts to impose stable order through heightened sound levels; “frammenti di frizione eco-tonale” places different sonic ecologies within a rarefied environment; while the textures of “infestazione” proliferate across the acoustic field. The extended “condizionamento” reintroduces birdsong, which grows increasingly synthetic before giving way to a slow accumulation of density and abrasion and a roughening of texture. “hauntology” turns towards the residue left by sound, retrieving voices that seem to belong to another timeframe. For all the variety of its source material, ]ex(s)it(u)[ holds together remarkably well. Guitar, electronics, birds, voices, resonance and the acoustics of individual sites move in and out of focus across the seven pieces. Barbierato’s “eco-tonality” ultimately describes something quite practical here: a way of performing in which the sounds already present in a place can alter the direction of the music as it happens. photo by Devadatta “Sk!” Valmiki, 2025 To help us piece things together, we reached out directly to Leonardo Barbierato. Throughout ]ex(s)it(u)[, the seven Patchwork pieces seem to form a conceptual progression: from “margine”, where different sonic worlds first come into contact, through “l’ora di punta”, “la mania del controllo”, “frammenti di frizione eco-tonale”, “infestazione” and “condizionamento”, before arriving at “hauntology”, where what remains is no longer the sound itself but its residue in memory. Were these seven pieces conceived as successive stages of a single compositional journey, or did that overarching narrative emerge only retrospectively? At what point did you realise they belonged together as one work rather than as independent electroacoustic studies? The seven pieces belong to a single performative and compositional process that unfolded over the course of five years. At the beginning, I was interested in exploring the ecosystems in which I performed through improvisation. This led me to develop a series of site-specific performances entitled [in situ], where the aim was to engage with the place to the point that it could actively shape the performance itself, avoiding to treat the place as a backdrop. Initially, I had no intention of releasing this material. In a sense, doing so seemed to contradict the very idea of site-specificity on which [in situ] was based. Those performances were conceived as experiences in which listening was inseparable from the materiality of the place: its light, its physical presence, and the network of relationships and perceptions that define a particular environment. However, when I listened back to the recordings, I realised that publishing selected excerpts could open up another layer of meaning. I became interested both in the sonic interactions that had emerged during the performances and in the idea that these recordings would be heard in places completely different from those in which they were created. I was curious about how this displacement might reshape the listening experience. So, to answer your question more directly: although all seven pieces originate from the same artistic process, the overall narrative of ]ex(s)it(u)[ only emerged retrospectively, during the editing and listening phase. It was then that I recognised the trajectory connecting the excerpts, a trajectory that, to some extent, also follows the chronology of the original performances. Your background combines jazz improvisation with artistic research in ecology, and your current doctoral work explores the relationship between improvisation and cultural and environmental ecology. Listening to ]ex(s)it(u)[, I was struck by how the field recordings — birdsong, environmental ambiences and site-specific sounds — never function simply as documentary material. They seem to interact with instrumental and electronic sounds until their identities become almost indistinguishable. How do you approach this dialogue between recorded environments and composed material? Are you trying to preserve the identity of a place, or are you more interested in allowing those places to be transformed through the compositional process? While working on my PhD at the Conservatory of Rome, which I recently completed, I became increasingly aware of how environmental sounds and what we conventionally call “musical” sounds gradually overlapped and entered into dialogue. Interestingly, this was also something noticed by people attending the performances. In my research, I describe this quality as eco-tonality: a condition in which ecosystemic and performative elements become intertwined. In most of the pieces on ]ex(s)it(u)[, the environmental sounds are not field recordings added afterwards. They are the actual sounds that were present during the performances and were processed in real time through an electroacoustic setup. Only in a couple of pieces (“frammenti di frizione eco-tonale” and “hauntology”) I used dedicated field recordings, which were nevertheless recorded in the same environments where the performances took place. My intention was to place all these elements into dialogue without establishing a clear hierarchy between them. Ultimately, the project has both an ecological and a political dimension. It seeks to encourage a more attentive mode of listening and a deeper engagement with the ecosystems we inhabit. I believe that composition can function as a device that subtly transforms the way we perceive and experience the places we live in. In that sense, I am less interested in preserving the “identity” of a place than in exploring its transformative potential through listening. One of the most remarkable aspects of the album is its treatment of listening itself. By the time “condizionamento” unfolds, the music seems to have subtly altered the listener’s expectations: instead of following individual events, one begins listening to relationships, resonances and the spaces between sounds. Was this gradual transformation of perception something you consciously composed? More broadly, do you think of ]ex(s)it(u)[ as a work that conditions the listener’s way of hearing as much as it presents a sequence of sounds? I’m really pleased to read your observation, because it touches on something that was central to the project. Yes, the gradual transformation of perception you describe is something I consciously sought during the performances over the years, and later tried to recreate through the selection, editing and sequencing of the material that became ]ex(s)it(u)[. As I mentioned earlier, the album aims to influence the way we listen. This intention is rooted in the belief that aesthetics, ethics and politics are deeply interconnected. I believe that changing the way we listen can also open up different ways of thinking, relating to others and inhabiting the environments around us. However, I don’t think there is a “correct” way of listening or a predetermined ethical outcome. What interests me is the possibility that listening differently may enable each person to inhabit and relate to the world in their own way, according to their experiences, memories and ways of making sense of them. In times of social and ecological crisis, I believe that the possibility of listening and acting differently can become particularly meaningful. For me, this is where the political dimension of the work lies: in creating the conditions for a different mode of attention. Whether that change lasts for a few minutes or extends beyond the listening experience is, of course, something each listener will discover in their own way. The album artwork quietly maps the Patchwork pieces onto a series of specific locations — from Morra’s Studio in Asti to the Parco Nazionale della Maremma, the Mattatoio di Testaccio and other sites — suggesting that geography itself forms part of the composition. Combined with the recurring use of field recordings, this gives the impression that ]ex(s)it(u)[ is almost a cartography of listening rather than simply an electroacoustic album. How important was the notion of site in shaping the project? Do you see these places as sources of sound, as collaborators in the creative process, or as traces that continue to resonate long after the recordings themselves have been transformed? At the beginning of the project, I spent a long time questioning what it means to act in a site-specific way and, more fundamentally, what a place actually is. Each piece on ]ex(s)it(u)[ is an excerpt from a specific performance of [in situ], connected to a specific location. The geography of these places is mapped in the artwork, allowing the listener to associate each track with its original context while listening. I really enjoy the expression “cartography of listening” that you used, as it captures an important aspect of the project. Throughout this process, I always tried to avoid treating places as soundscapes from which to extract material to manipulate freely. When I used field recordings, they emerged from encounters with the ecosystems themselves: for example, through conversations and interviews with the communities I encountered in different locations, who often pointed me towards sounds, events or relationships that were meaningful to them. In most cases, however, these sounds emerged directly during the performances: the movements of participants, objects being touched or activated, birdsong, cicadas, wind, my playing and all the other sonic events that became part of the situation. This is central to my understanding of site-specific practice: a place is an entanglement of personal, human and other-than-human stories, relationships and forms of agency that actively shape the compositional and performative process. For me, a place is a kind of patchwork, where each patch (each element that contributes to its identity) follows its own trajectory and interacts with others, sometimes in harmony, sometimes in conflict, and sometimes with indifference. Through this work, I try to make these relationships perceptible on a sonic level and to reflect on them actively. In this sense, the place collaborates with and co-produces ]ex(s)it(u)[. It remains beyond the production of the work itself, continuing to resonate and transform through each new listening experience. (Gianmarco Del Re)

items._cn_summary: Leonardo Barbierato的专辑以七首"Patchwork"系列作品构成，素材源自五年间在多个特定地点进行的现场表演。每一首作品都将环境录音、电子处理与原声乐器演奏融为一体，三者在不同曲目中轮流占据主导地位。"eco-tonality"（生态音调性）是贯穿全作的核心概念，强调生态系统声音与表演性声音之间的互相渗透与身份流动——吉他在电路中浮现又消隐，鸟鸣逐渐被合成质感侵蚀，最终在"hauntology"一曲中回溯声音的残留。整张专辑以回顾性方式剪辑成形，呈现出一种由声音、空间与演奏共同塑造的创作逻辑，关注的是声音如何因场所本身而改变方向。

items.body: Poladroïd packs eight lean, muscular tracks with throbbing bass, fat drum-machine punch and just enough EBM grit to keep the whole thing moving. Lean, mean and mechanical Roentgenizdat by Poladroïd   Poladroïd drops this lean eight-tracker of electro industriana, fusing lino-friendly aesthetics with European body-music gloss and a distinctly modern tech-funk sensibility. The moods are taut and tensile, the bottom end throbbing in post-Moroder blasts while the drums come in big and fat, all Roger Linn punch and TR-909 muscle. The result is an album that understands restraint but never sounds restrained. “Norilsk” opens proceedings with clean-air funk and a diabolically wiry synth topline that cascades like digital waterfalls. Warm pads gradually move into the frame, adding color and perspective as the track develops into a convincing soul-and-machine coalescence. “Lyuberi” follows with straight-up EBM propulsion, its hard pulse surrounded by huge string synths that give the track a cinematic glow without softening its physical impact. “Leningrad” reveals Mr Droid as someone not inclined to follow the routines of the pack, bending familiar electro and industrial grammar into something more individual and elusive. “Sochi” twists and turns through helter-skelter synth melodies, constantly changing direction while maintaining its​ muscular rhythmic center. We are now only halfway through as Roentgenizdat—The Soviet-era practice of copying banned Western and émigré music onto discarded X-ray film to evade state censorship—begins its closing moments “Girls From Omsk” digs deepest into the groove, riding a simple, infectious refrain that becomes increasingly impossible to shake. “White Boy Funk” steps forward on a clipped rhythm and wiry bassline, its fogged-out strings creating a sense of pressure and anticipation. “Doomer” brings the industrial vocal miasma, gruff and ominous, with proto-paranoia steadily gathering behind the beat. Closer “Escape To Tbilisi” finally lets everything off the leash: a stomping, skewed belter that sends the album out at full mechanical tilt. Roentgenizdat is available on Roulette Rekordz. [Bandcamp] Roentgenizdat by PoladroïdThe post Poladroïd :: Roentgenizdat (Roulette Rekordz) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张以苏联时代'X光片盗版磁带'概念命名的电子工业专辑，共八首紧凑有力的作品。低频合成器bass线扎实饱满，鼓机节奏兼具Roger Linn与TR-909的硬朗触感，整体呈现出冷峻机械却不失律动感的声音面貌。曲目编排从开场曲的清冽funk质感逐步推进至EBM直给的脉冲驱动，再过渡到工业嗓音营造的阴沉氛围，最终以失序的全速机械轰鸣收束。制作者并非简单复制类型模板，而是将经典电子语法拆解重组，在熟悉的工业/电子框架内注入更具个性的节奏变化与旋律走向。专辑在克制与爆发之间找到平衡，节拍始终维持肌肉感与推进力。对暗潮与电子工业场景的听众而言，这张作品提供了足够的类型纵深与执行精度。

items.body: “Mood Starters” is the result of a collaboration between Belgian artists Pedro Maras (BedouinDrone) and Marc Ceulemans (Brainquake). They share a common vision of music and the atmosphere surrounding it, which has resulted in this 11-track album, released on the Bulgarian label Mahorka. “Mood Starters” is all about atmosphere—a dark and unsettling mood that evokes a sense of mental anguish. Intense, sometimes overwhelming dark sounds alternately blast you away and carry you along on an imaginary deathbed. The album sits somewhere between Dark-Ambient and Cinematic music, while being spiced up with other Electronic music elements, including a brilliant closing track that opens a window onto IDM. Add a few highly Experimental tracks to the mix, and you get a pretty clear picture of what “Mood Starters” is all about. At times, the music feels almost improvised, which I find to be the album’s weakest aspect. For the most part, however, the tracks sound carefully considered, crafted with a vast arsenal of sounds, effects, and even field recordings. BedouinDrone and Brainquake seem unconcerned with genre boundaries, preferring instead to experiment freely. The result is a collection of strong tracks that conjure up powerful visual imagery. I can only hope the duo will repeat this experience, as this album demonstrates enormous potential. (Rating:8). Listen to “Cages”: Cages by BedouinDrone + Brainquake About BedouinDrone & Brainquake BedouinDrone is the dark ambient and illbient project of Belgian artist Pedro Maras, built around dense atmospheres, layered drones and a cinematic sense of storytelling shaped by themes of loneliness, memory and collapsing emotional landscapes. Brainquake is the industrial project of Belgian artist Marc Ceulemans, working with mechanical repetition, distorted textures, fragmented rhythms and psychological pressure rooted in classic industrial traditions. The two artists had never met in person before recording together for the Bulgarian label Mahorka, which released their collaboration album “Mood Starters” on June 5, 2026.
items._genre: dark ambient / cinematic / industrial / experimental electronic / IDM
items._cn_summary: 比利时艺术家Pedro Maras与Marc Ceulemans从未谋面便通过远程合作完成了这张十一曲专辑。二人各自拥有暗氛围与工业项目的创作背景，作品中大量使用密集的音墙、分层drone、失真纹理与田野录音，构建出黑暗不安、带有精神痛感与临终意象的氛围空间。专辑跨越暗氛围与电影音乐边界，并融入IDM与高度实验性的电子元素，结尾曲目尤其突出。评论指出部分曲目带有即兴感、结构稍显松散，但整体经过精细打磨，创作者不拘泥于类型界限自由实验，画面感强烈，展现出两位艺术家相当大的合作潜力。

items.body: Synapscape The Future Ant-Zen Synapscape have nothing to prove to anyone other than themselves at this juncture. Thirty years and fourteen LPs deep into their career, the German duo of Philipp Münch and Tim Kniep have earned the right to either reprise the scraping, break-ish power noise they pioneered in their early years or, as is the case with new LP The Future, give themselves license to drift from that brutal and uncompromising remit. Carrying on from 2022’s The Stable Mind, Synapscape’s detours from ‘power noise for power noise’s sake’ finds them revisiting many of the genres and periods which preceded the style. There’s the dubbish echo and squall of “Five Four”, while “Pick” and “Valley” both feature foreboding synth stabs and rubbery bass taken from vintage dark electro and reframed in Synapscape’s far more skitterish rhythms. It’s tempting to try to trace the origins of these fluctuations, but as was the case for many years with another German duo in Haujobb, one member’s constant stream of side and solo releases concurrent with mainline projects, in comparison to the other’s relative silence out of the duo itself, makes this a tricky proposition. Münch’s recent spate of work as neat_less, for instance, is not so far from the serpentine, funky lope of “Disappear”, but there’s unquestionably something in those tracks which in unquestionably Synapscape and nothing else. Is that je ne sais quois the result of Kniep’s quiet but firm hand, or just the natural result of the pair’s chemistry? Such questions are effectively academic at this point. Synapscape’s legacy has long since been established, and for those who’ve spent any amount of time with the records which built it, there’s an easy pleasure in listening to them rework and rethink the sounds upon which it sits. Buy it. the future by synapscape The post Synapscape, “The Future” appeared first on I Die: You Die.

items._cn_summary: Synapscape 由德国二人组 Philipp Münch 与 Tim Kniep 组成，已活跃三十余年并发行十四张专辑。这张《The Future》延续 2022 年《The Stable Mind》的路线，从他们早期标志性的极端暴力噪音框架中出走，转而回溯更广泛的电子音乐谱系。作品中可见 dub 回响与嘈杂音墙、复古暗色电子合成器的低频推进以及蛇形律动线条，节奏更碎裂灵活。评论指出两位成员在主项目之外的独立活动为创作带来复杂影响，但最终成品仍保留不可复制的二人组化学特质。对于长期追随的听众而言，这张专辑的价值在于二人对自身根基的重新审视与拆解重组。

items.body: Acclimation, or acclimatisation as it is more commonly termed, is a process by which an individual organism adjusts to a change in its environment. This could be the response of an animal or plant to a change of season; the adaptation of a mountaineer to a high-altitude atmosphere; or, perhaps more obliquely, the ‘becoming natural’ of certain introduced objects or processes (consider how, for many observers of the British landscape, treeless fields and dry stone walls have ‘acclimated’ to their environment and thus become ‘natural’, while wind turbines have yet to do so). The latter example may be somewhat spurious, but it is relevant to the themes and processes behind Jake Muir’s new album. The Seattle-based artist was inspired by the invitation to perform at the century-old Georgetown Steam Plant to create a live set based on industrial and aqueous field recordings, and this set became the basis of “Acclimation”. Without knowing this context, however, it would be difficult to link the album’s two tracks back to any kind of industrial activity; on the contrary, Muir has arranged and processed his sounds such that they come to resemble a more general enveloping environment. Mechanical, electronic, and ecological effects overrun their respective boundaries and blur the perceptual and conceptual lines between them. What does this sound like in practice? ‘Cold Seeps’ presents a dense, humid tropical atmosphere, with damp gleaming and splish-splashes of water, the brushing of leaves and snapping of twigs. None of these things are heard, exactly; rather, a rich field of abstract sound suggests or gestures towards such things. Later on in the piece, a faint ringing glimmer builds into an emphatic high-pitched stutter, and gleaming winds race over low bass throb, evoking more a weather system on another planet, or a moon such as Titan or Enceladus, than anywhere on Earth. Towards the end, however, bright, undulating tones recall sharp sunlight and the rolling of the sea, a postcard from the Pacific coast reduced to smudged outlines and splotches of colour. A similar approach to rhythm informs ‘Black Smokers’, the vague tossing and turning of which has more in common with outdoor environments than the strictly regulated pulse of most Western music. A faint crackle recalls quiet, hesitant footsteps on gravel or sand, and tones soar like the cries of distant birds. Things rattle and echo as if on the floor of a vast canyon, or tap intermittently like a moored boat’s rigging against a mast. Harmony is sometimes present, though somewhat effaced, or rather transformed: glistening tones gather in what sometimes resemble chords, but also gusts, flocks, streams. Perhaps it’s just my own idiosyncratic way of listening to it, but to me it seems that with “Acclimation” Muir has succeeded in bringing the ‘industrial’ and the ‘natural’ together in ways that sound like neither, but somehow lean decidedly towards the latter; I’d be interested in hearing what impressions it forms on other listening ears. Acclimation by Jake Muir Jake Muir Dragon’s Eye Recordings
items._genre: ambient / field recording / experimental electronic / drone
items._cn_summary: Jake Muir以在西雅图百年Georgetown Steam Plant演出的现场录音为基础，将工业与自然环境录音通过处理和编排转化为两首长篇作品。'Cold Seeps'呈现潮湿的热带氛围，水声与叶片摩擦以抽象声场暗示存在，随后高频闪烁逐渐累积，唤起外星天气系统的感官印象。'Black Smokers'以不规则的节奏运动模糊了自然声响与机械脉冲的边界，碎石脚步声、远处鸟鸣、峡谷回响与船帆碰撞的节奏交织在一起。和谐音被弱化或转化为气流、鸟群、溪流般的集合体，使工业录音'驯化'为某种非地球的自然环境。整体手法模糊了感知与概念上的分类边界，呈现工业与生态声响融合的实验性听觉体验。

items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.
items.label: Cool Waters
items._genre: folktronica / world music / experimental electronic / global fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是内罗毕新厂牌Cool Waters的首发作品，核心是一组跨国组合：德国出生的肯尼亚驻地打击乐手Sven Kacirek与搭档Olith Ratengo组成Odd Okoddo二重奏，并邀请83岁的传统肯尼亚dodo流派歌手Ogoya Nengo加入。Kacirek以Buchla合成器、手打打击乐和套鼓构建声音骨架，与两位歌手的嗓音形成层次丰富的对话。合成器多声部节奏层层叠加，低频与木琴音色穿插其间，电子纹理始终克制，不喧宾夺主。歌曲从简洁的节奏短句逐步生长，最终呈现为浑然一体的有机声音。专辑涉及代际、地域与流派的交汇：传统东肯尼亚歌唱与当代电子实验并置，老年歌手的全球首秀与白人电子音乐家的非洲节律框架共存，是全球化背景下非洲根源音乐与前卫电子美学相互渗透的一个样本。

items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 联合作曲家 Francesco Paolo Paladino 与诗人 Luca Chino Ferrari，以 United States of Alchemy 之名发表专辑《Songs of Compassion》，收录十一首作品。专辑核心挑战在于音乐层面：以钢琴为主导，搭配弦乐、木管、合成器泛音与金属质感音色，构成非线性的模态结构，打破西方和声进行的惯常逻辑，向更古老、更遥远的音乐叙事致敬，风格更接近 Steve Reich 与 Philip Glass 而非民谣摇滚。歌词同样具有强烈的当代政治色彩，《Pale Wanderer》探讨威权主义的帮凶机制，《Charlottesville》直指新纳粹集会的种族主义口号，同时延续六十年代抗议歌曲传统，对死亡与人类在宇宙中的位置进行哲学沉思。Moskowitz 的嗓音苍老而充满智慧，如同训练有素的方法派演员演绎歌词，旋律如意识流般起伏，不拘泥于自然音阶和声，钢琴则扮演另一重声音与希腊式合唱队的角色，对叙事作出呼应与评论。整体呈现为政治意识鲜明、音乐语言高度实验化的当代创作。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 的第二张专辑以自制乐器为核心亮点——所有演奏器材均由废弃物和零碎材料手工打造，包括低音管、厨房号角等多种非标准乐器，音准与音色在录音中展现出出乎意料的专业水准。乐队将克莱兹默、昆比亚、桑巴、阿弗罗贝等全球音乐语汇与即兴手法巧妙交织：单簧管奏出犹太东欧旋律，笛声游走于拉美与中东曲调之间，颤音琴点缀非洲节奏框架。评论特别强调乐手在器乐即兴段落中展现出的娴熟技巧与跨文化理解。专辑整体洋溢着发明家的童趣与音乐学者的严谨，提醒人们旋律、节奏与和声的表达并不依赖乐器的光鲜外表，而在于演奏者如何让材料发声。这一切使作品在民俗融合的亲切感之上叠加了一层实验性的手工声响美学。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自2021年新冠封锁期间，钢琴家奥马尔·索萨在意大利法奇奥利音乐厅进行的两小时独奏即兴录音，后经后期混音加入稀疏的人声采样、打击乐、循环音轨、田野录音和环境音效。他在访谈中阐述其创作理念：拒绝被风格标签束缚，主张融合所有影响于新的形式中，强调"无错音"的自然首录哲学，追求与听众共同踏上自由即兴的精神之旅。专辑深植古巴音乐传统，融合爵士即兴与实验手法，以钢琴为核心探索声学共振的内在精神维度，是一位跨越四十年创作生涯的艺术家对全球化音乐工业分类体系的反思之作。

items.body: Laho is a Finnish project that originated in 2006. After releasing a few records during its early years, the project went quiet for a long time before being reactivated a few years ago. “Death Machines”—which feels more like a seven-track mini-album—was inspired by today’s dystopian world, as well as by self-reflection and other dark themes. The music is indeed quite dark, but that is not the whole story. This record reveals two sides: on the one hand, a powerful production featuring menacing yet brilliant basslines topped with razor-sharp sequences; on the other, a completely different style with a Cinematic feel, including one entirely instrumental track. Personally, I prefer Laho’s harder side, which occasionally reminds me of early Combichrist, albeit with a certain polished touch. This is also evident in the vocal production, which is powerful yet has something of a ‘Power-Pop’ quality. It comes as no surprise, then, that the album concludes with a remarkable cover of Depeche Mode‘s “Behind the Wheel,” delivered in a dark and intense style. I think it’s a great track, by the way. Laho seems to be a sort of Janus—a two-faced project, with its powerful side completely winning me over. (Rating:7½). Listen to “The Great Collapse”: The Great Collapse by Laho About Laho Laho is a Finnish dark electronic project led by musician and recording engineer Konsta Vehkala, who is based in Jyväskylä and is responsible for all composition, programming and production. The project is an outlet for solo works by Vehkala and blends industrial, EBM, futurepop and darkwave. The project began in 2006 under the name Lahonnut Konkelo as a series of electronic and industrial experiments. The name was shortened to Laho shortly afterwards. The first EP, “The Other Side”, appeared in 2007 as an independently issued CDr, combining instrumental industrial metal with a slightly experimental edge. It was later re-released by Italian netlabel Ekleipsi, which also issued the first full-length album “Escape from the Dying Star” in 2009. “Escape from the Dying Star” was recorded between 2007 and 2008 at the Cable_Hell studio and released digitally in April 2009, offering a mix of electro-industrial, cybernetic synth work and distorted guitar. The album held ten tracks including “Program”, “Dead End” and a remix by Technomancer. Later in 2009 Laho issued “The World in Flames” as a standalone digital release, followed by the single “Mechanigod” in 2011 and a one-off digital track “Walking in the Air (1984 mix)” in December 2021. After these early EP and album releases, the project entered a 13-year hiatus as Vehkala focused on other bands and production work. Writing for Laho resumed in 2024, leading to a new series of songs, this time including vocals. Parallel to Laho, Vehkala maintains an active role in the Finnish metal scene. He plays drums for the melodic metal band Psychework and has performed and recorded with groups including Gian, Vipermilk and Lojohh, as well as contributing recording, mixing and mastering work to a wide range of Finnish underground acts. “Death Machines” is Laho’s first release since writing resumed in 2024, and its first EP built around vocals throughout.
items._cn_summary: 芬兰暗潮/工业电子单人项目 Laho 沉寂十三年后携全新数字 EP《Death Machines》回归，七首作品围绕当代反乌托邦语境与自我审视展开。制作层面呈现双重特质：一方面以锋利序列与压迫性贝斯线构建猛烈的工业舞曲架构，融合了类似早期 Combichrist 的强硬质地；另一方面则融入电影化氛围与纯器乐段落，形成叙事性张力。人声处理偏重力量感与流行可听性的平衡。专辑以重新诠释 Depeche Mode《Behind the Wheel》收尾，将经典曲目转化为暗色高强度版本。整体在传统 EBM 框架内加入了音色打磨与结构层次，虽未突破类型边界，但执行力扎实，兼具舞曲驱动力与暗潮情绪深度，适合工业电子场景的循环聆听。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — "Universo rojo"s social media accounts have been dead since 2021, the band, located in Vi�a delMar, apparently has no plans of coming back together in the near future, I must admit, that just asthere's a mystery around this LP (I will later tell you why!), it remains a mystery why they justdissapeared from social media for 5 years now!The band hands us this record in a silver platter, claiming that it is a conceptual record, indeed Icould see where they are going, the way the album sounds is overall telling of the nature of therecord itself, yet, and now I'll tell you the mystery, there's almost no lyrics! It's a semi fullyinstrumental album, with the only spoken sections being some indigenous like chants on the secondtrack "Visi�n planetaria de los tiempos", which seem to be in a native American language, I'd say itmost likely is Mapudungun, however, these chants and lyrics have no subtitles available on thedescription of the track (at least on platforms such as Spotify), and the singer seems to beuncredited, ladies and gentlemen this is the mystery I told you about! What do these lyrics meanexactly, and who sang them? It's captivating how a detail so simple can imply so many things!Musically wise, the music delivers an interesting experience which mixes krautrock with psychedelicrock and some elements of Zeuhl. Speaking of Zeuhl, it seems to be one of the main genres the bandlooks up to, as their publicly available playlist is dominated by bands such as Magma and Weidorje,as well as kasutrock acts like Popol Vuh and Amon D��l II, interestingly enough, we find some ratherodd influences that stand out in their playlist, like the extreme doom metal band Sunnata. Beinghighly influenced by classic experimental genres characterized by their use of symphonicinstrumentation, tape effects, spiritual topics and repetitiveness, "Impermanencia" is full ofsynthetizers, tape loops, repetitions of bass lines and riffs and a very hypotonic, spiral like windof textures and noises, all contributing to the creation of pieces which feel less like music andmore akin to a state of trance and meditation, albeit a very chaotic one. Each composition feelsvery much like the previous one, with little variation in the state it indices on the listener, thisoverall calmer and more meditative approach to music, will appeal to those invested in ambient andkraut, but won't satisfy those who prefer Zeuhl or more expressive, grandiose symphonic rock. The album has a lot of influences, although most can't be felt, but when it shows the signs, itsounds great! I'd like to point out that I was fairly dissapointed, as I was promised a magnum opus,a masterclass for the genre and most of the times, the record feels like an experiment halfway doneor a very relaxing jamming session.The musicianship is good enough, you can feel that each instrument was recorded separately and thenpieced together with the others, they are talented players but you can't really feel much chemistrybetween the parts that make the music, if you add this to what I previously stated, you get the fullpicture : this record is much more like something "Stars of the lid" would do if they went a littlemore experimental and not something that comes out of the chaotic mess of Zeuhl or the mathematicsof krautrock.My biggest issue with this record is the production, which is straight up unbearable...this recordsounds muddy, grainy, blurry and inconsistent, because yes, some tracks have good production and theother an awful one, and the difference is so noticeable it makes it uncomfortable to listen to. Thedrums can't even be heard most of the time, a record so inspired by krautrock should have a veryclear rhythmic direction and presence, which can't be heard through at least half of the record.I give it 2 stars because it's an interesting record to dig into and because of how hypnotic anduseful for meditation it is, but musically itself, I don't really see much to highlight...it'salmost as if it were an experiment that was never properly finished, this is sad because thisproject had so much potential.

items._cn_summary: 这张2018年专辑由智利乐队UNIVERSO ROJO录制，整体走向半器乐化概念作品。评论者指出专辑几乎无歌词，仅在第二轨出现类似马普切语的原住民吟唱，歌手身份未标注，这种留白构成了专辑神秘感的核心。音乐融合了Krautrock的循环律动与Zeuhl的爆发张力，合成器、磁带循环、贝斯线重复层层叠加，营造出恍惚冥想式的听感。每首曲目之间变化有限，偏向ambient式的绵延而非戏剧性推进。乐手技术扎实，录音呈现分层拼贴质感。评论者最终略显失望，认为作品更像半完成实验或放松即兴，未达预期杰作水准。拉丁美洲小厂背景与原住民语言元素为专辑增添了独特地域色彩。

items.body: Nightshop for September 2026, starting with 2 songs of the day via Colombia & Galicia. Our albums of the month start with American artist Megiapa and her spiritual soul, followed by a sunny compilation of Belgian label WERF Records, Brussels international group Re#encounter and their gnawa & griot jazz, Thai band Khun Narin with their hypnotic phin guitar music, and a collaboration by Mexican Institute Of Sound with Meridian Brothers for energetic electro cumbia. items.body: FOURSCHER Festival returns to Club From Hell in Erfurt, Germany, on 7 and 8 November 2026, with nine acts spanning EBM, dark electro, rhythmic noise and ritual electronics: Snog, Black Lung, Individual Totem, Mildreda, This Morn’ Omina, Heimstatt Yipotash, Polykoptr, KIFOTH and Manipulation. Having attended the festival twice, in 2024 and 2025, what stood out both times was less any single performance than the combination of a carefully selected programme, an open audience and the sense that organisers Danny Hildebrandt and Andreas Schubert were personally invested in how people experienced the weekend. That impression carries into the 2026 edition, where the nine acts are connected less by genre than by a shared refusal to treat the existing vocabulary of industrial and electronic music as sufficient on its own: some dismantle it, some stretch it toward ritual or techno, some return to it after decades, and some use familiar EBM structures to ask questions that have little to do with genre loyalty. The clearest example is the pairing of Snog and Black Lung, both projects of David Thrussell. Snog works through legible structures, songs, hooks, slogans and satire, using the dancefloor to examine consumerism, obedience and political absurdity. Black Lung strips away that accessibility for harder, darker and more experimental electronic forms. Their FOURSCHER appearances are billed as their only European shows of 2026; a new Black Lung album, “Ordo Ab Chao,” is due shortly before the festival. Individual Totem bring an electro industrial catalogue reaching back to the 1990s, including records such as “S.E.T.I.,” “Mothfly,” “Kyria 13” and “Electrostatic,” with live appearances rare enough that the Erfurt date carries weight of its own. Mildreda’s context is more immediate: “Realities,” released 28 August, pushes Jan Dewulf’s work into a space where dark electronic abrasion sits alongside more emotional exposure than the genre typically allows, while retaining the project’s Canadian EBM and Belgian electronic lineage. This Morn’ Omina arrive in their thirtieth year with new release “Vestiges,” which frames three decades as continuity of practice rather than a retrospective; the project’s rhythm-driven material has always worked to alter a listener’s sense of duration and physical orientation rather than simply carry songs. Heimstatt Yipotash’s 2026 album “Abyss” draws on the physical conditions of the deep sea, pressure, isolation, cold and downward movement, as both imagery and compositional logic, moving between aggressive electro, rhythm noise and more cinematic passages. Polykoptr comes from the wider Amnistia orbit and the Leipzig electronic scene, presented here on its own terms rather than as an extension of that name. The Slovak project KIFOTH released “Artificial Territory” in June 2026, reconnecting earlier KIFOTH material with contemporary EBM production. Manipulation return after close to three decades, with “Feel The Same” remembered as a small club hit from the project’s earlier run. Line-up and practical information FOURSCHER Festival 2026 takes place at Club From Hell, Flughafenstraße 41, 99092 Erfurt, Germany, on 7 November (19:00-03:00) and 8 November (13:00-18:00). The line-up: Snog, Black Lung, Individual Totem, Mildreda, This Morn’ Omina, Heimstatt Yipotash, Polykoptr, KIFOTH and Manipulation. Tickets are priced at €70 for the weekend or €40 for a day ticket; electronic tickets are available, with printed tickets held at the box office on request.
items._genre: industrial / EBM / dark electro / rhythmic noise / ritual electronics
items._cn_summary: 本文介绍2026年FOURSCHER音乐节的阵容与策展理念，该节在德国埃尔福特Club From Hell举办两日。九组艺人涵盖电子身体音乐、暗电子、节奏噪音与仪式电子等领域。文章重点阐述策展逻辑：节目编排不以类型层级为依据，而以艺术亲缘性为纽带——这些艺人共同拒绝将工业与电子音乐的现有词汇视为自足体系，有的拆解结构、有的推向仪式或科技舞曲方向、有的在数十年后回归。Snog与Black Lung作为同一创作者的两个项目形成对比；Individual Totem携九十年代曲目回归；Mildreda新专辑拓展情感表达边界；This Morn' Omina三十周年新作强调实践延续；Heimstatt Yipotash以深海物理条件作为创作逻辑。整体呈现独立场景中策展人主导、强调艺术关联而非商业考量的策展思路。

items.body: A short intro on "Sculpting Silence" The nature of art is to make you stop you in your tracks, to stop doing what you're doing and thinking, and to start using your senses, your eyes and ears, sometimes your touch and smell to be surprised, to be confronted with the unexpected, to admire, to see things differently. We will have a short series of music that we describe as "s culpting silence ", music in which sound is used like the black lines of a pen in zen art, a few strokes that capture the essence on a white canvas. And the first album in the series explicitly refers to the Zen concepts of ' Mu ' and ' Shin ' : " The term combines the kanji Mu (nothingness) and Shin (mind or spirit), and is often translated as “no-mind.” It refers to a state of consciousness free from fear, anger, or ego—where action arises naturally and without obstruction. In musical terms, this becomes a space where sound is not forced or premeditated, but emerges with clarity and immediacy ", we read in the liner notes. So the few strokes on a white canvas - on 'nothingness' - are like the ripples on a still pond, the barely visible effect of the slightest breeze. Here are some descriptions I found on the value of the colour 'white' in Zen art, comparable to silence in music. In Zen art, white is not merely a blank background or an empty void. It represents 'ma' (negative space), functioning as living breath, silence, and the infinite potential from which all forms emerge and return. The unpainted white paper or silk is an active, essential presence equal to the black ink strokes. Zen painting uses intentional emptiness, asymmetry, and abbreviated forms to point toward direct seeing rather than decoration. Blank space is not “nothing”; it functions as breath, silence, and the field in which forms appear and dissolve. Common motifs—enso, bamboo, landscapes, and solitary figures—teach non-attachment and ordinary clarity. I also found some sayings about listening. "Listening stops with the ears, the mind stops with recognition, but spirit is empty and waits on all things." "What is this mind? Who is hearing these sounds? ... What is it that hears?" "The quieter you become, the more you can hear." Now about the album. The cover art is bizarre, to say the least: a cigarette-smoking armour seated on a toilet in a hilly landscape. It's in bad taste in my opinion, and not because of the toilet, but also because it does not truly reflect the nature of the music. It's a surreal digital artwork created by Aki Karano (also known as Akis Karanos) a visual artist and experimental musician, based in Greece. In retrospect, it looks familiar when you see the likeness with the traditional Japanese drawings of monks contemplating the world, and also seen from the back. There may be a reference, or it might just be a coincidence. Admitted, the monk is not smoking and not wearing an armour, and he's contemplating a circle and not a square, yet it might be a more modern, more surreal rendition of the same experience. Now really about the album. Both Susana Santos Silva on trumpet and Vasco Trilla on percussion explore the boundaries and sonic potential of their respective instruments, creating ringing tones, whistles, droplets, swooshes, rumbles, gurgles, swishes and many more sounds without name or description. The album begins quietly, with uncommon sounds cautiously flirting with silence—touching it slowly and gently, as if aware of its fragility. The result is a kind of soft intensity, with no obvious path or predetermined concept beyond the simple act of producing small fragments of sound and welcoming their clarity, their unexpectedness, and the ways in which they interact. This is music that has nothing to prove. It does not seek to impress, move, or even necessarily engage a listener or an audience. It exists simply for its own sake: to be savoured, appreciated, and perhaps approached with the same state of mind as the artists themselves—with no attachment and no anticipation. Such an experience can only emerge from going beyond the expected, allowing the music to develop organically and naturally, as if arising from nothingness. Contrary to the liner notes, I would recommend simply listening, rather than reflecting while you listen. Let yourself become part of the experience. Be there in the moment. Both Santos Silva and Trilla are masters of their art. They share a remarkable sensitivity and an innovative ability to draw sounds from their instruments that are rarely heard, while employing a wide range of techniques and tools to sustain the listener’s attention. As with much improvised music, the album may surprise you on a first listen, but it reveals more of itself with each return. Be the music. Listen and download from Bandcamp . Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Susana Santos Silva与Vasco Trilla合作的即兴作品，隶属于Defkaz厂牌的「Sculpting Silence」系列。乐评以大量篇幅阐述禅宗美学对专辑的启发——「无」（Mu）与「心」（Shin）的结合，意指声音不被刻意安排，自然涌现于寂静之中。文中引述禅画中「留白」的概念，将沉默类比为水面涟漪，寥寥音符如同墨笔在白纸上勾画的痕迹。专辑封面的超现实数字艺术引发讨论：一位身穿盔甲的僧侣坐在马桶上抽烟，虽看似与音乐意境不符，但乐评指出其与传统日本僧侣冥想图存在视觉上的呼应关系，可能是有意为之的当代演绎。整体文字注重概念阐释，对音乐本体的技术分析较少，但禅意哲学与即兴演奏的结合展现了独特的艺术视角。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的新专辑延续了她标志性的模糊跨界风格，将民谣、前卫元素与宗教感融为一体。中提琴、簧风琴、击弦古钢琴与钢琴构成核心编制，并加入鼓、贝斯和合成器拓宽音色边界。多数曲目为一次性即兴录制，营造出穿越时空的静谧神秘氛围。专辑同时是一份纪念，献给 Cotton 已故的父亲，曲目《最后的收获》以深沉的庄严感呈现老人最后一次造访他所钟爱的小菜园，情感超越了语言。专辑中光与暗相互渗透，融合中世纪圣咏、民谣旋律与即兴手法，形成难以归类的独立美学，既具挑战性又能触动听众。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 本合辑收录贝宁音乐人Antoine Dougbè与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo de Cotonou在1977至1982年间合作的作品。Dougbè以拍手演绎Cavacha节奏见长，融合巫毒传统音乐元素与刚果流行乐影响，与Poly-Rythmo共同打造出独具西非特色的放克声响。乐评指出，专辑虽扎根七十年代风格，但因录制年代跨越至八十年代，吉他音色带有塑料质感，合成器开始介入，呈现出与乐队以往合辑不同的声音质感。古巴son的影响在开篇曲目中尤为明显，合成器铺垫配合闪亮吉他与紧凑踩镲节奏，构成层次丰富的律动底床；另一首作品则更直接地呈现古巴风味的牛铃、鼻音人声呼应与重复乐段。该合辑展示了Dougbè短暂却高产的创作生涯对贝宁音乐场景的独特贡献，Analog Africa作为专注非洲音乐的独立小厂牌，为其提供了向国际听众呈现的渠道。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是挪威Camilla Hole Trio的最新作品，相比前作融合科幻合成器声效的探索，本作回归更为脚踏实地的表达。主奏乐器为高音萨克斯，融合爵士即兴与挪威西部传统民间音乐素材，体现在为传统春季舞蹈配乐的曲目中。三人组合中角色并非固定，旋律、节奏与色彩在不同乐器间自由流转：低音提琴与萨克斯同步演奏主旋律，模块合成器与颤音琴增添层次感，鼓手则不断拓展节奏空间。整首作品从结构化的陈述逐渐滑向自由的即兴对话，萨克斯在尾声再次回归主题旋律，为开放式探索收束。这种角色互换的演奏方式模糊了主奏与伴奏的边界，使得传统民谣素材在爵士语法中获得新生。
