items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位瑞典小提琴手与两位挪威乐手组成三重奏，以非传统方式重新诠释斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲。乐评将其比作室内乐——三位演奏者沉浸在亲密的音乐对话中，而非适合舞蹈伴奏的表演。唱片试图挖掘舞曲表面之下的隐秘含义与暗流，呼应易卜生戏剧中隐藏在欢愉表象下的不安。开场曲选自挪威塞特斯达尔的传说主题，暗示小提琴曾被视为魔鬼之器。演奏中旋律线条时有碎裂与停滞，节奏被刻意打散，呈现出对传统素材的解构与再探索。独立小厂牌发行，融合民间传统与实验性即兴手法。

items.body: French industrial project HORSKH has released “Connected“, a collaboration with Carpenter Brut, on September 10, 2026, ahead of HORSKH’s forthcoming album “MTNT”. HORSKH’s official Bandcamp credits the track jointly to HORSKH and Carpenter Brut, with mixing and mastering by Thibault Chaumont at Deviant Lab Studio and artwork by Johanna Jaskowska. Connected by HORSKH “Connected” also appears on HORSKH’s forthcoming album “MTNT”, listed as a ten-track release scheduled for September 25, 2026, issued through Wire Control under exclusive licence to Blood Blast Distribution. “Connected” and the earlier single “Glow” are both tied directly to “MTNT”. The lyrics give the collaboration a considerably less comfortable meaning than its title suggests. Images of wires, intravenous connection, fear, chemical illusion and an attachment that persists despite attempts to escape recur throughout the song, placing bodily, technological and psychological attachment close together rather than treating “connection” as straightforward communication. The pairing brings together two French projects that approach heavy electronic music from different but intersecting angles. HORSKH’s recent catalogue has increasingly combined guitars, electronic programming and industrial pressure: “BODY” arrived in January 2024, following “WIRE” in 2021 and “GATE” in 2017. Carpenter Brut, meanwhile, released his latest studio album “Leather Temple” on February 27, 2026. The two releases share a technical link as well: “Leather Temple” was mixed and mastered by Thibault Chaumont at Deviant Lab, the same studio and engineer credited on “Connected”. “MTNT” arrives on September 25, 2026. “Connected” is available now through HORSKH’s official Bandcamp and streaming platforms. About HORSKH HORSKH are based in Besançon, France. Their recorded catalogue dates back to the “DAWN” EP, released in October 2014 and followed by an expanded edition in 2015. Their first full-length album, “GATE”, arrived on April 10, 2017, followed by “WIRE” on January 22, 2021 and “BODY” on January 19, 2024. The credits for “GATE” and “WIRE” list Bastien on programming, keyboards, vocals and guitar, Briou on live drums, and Jordan on guitar and keyboards. “WIRE” was mixed by Sam Munnier and Bastien Hennaut and mastered at Deviant Lab Studio, while “BODY” was mixed and mastered by Thibault Chaumont at Deviant Lab Studio. Ahead of “MTNT”, HORSKH released three other singles during 2026: “BAD GLITCH” on January 22, “Hyperhuman” in March and “Glow” in June. “Connected”, featuring Carpenter Brut, followed on September 10. The band have also been active on the European festival circuit in 2026, with appearances listed at Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig, Castle Party in Bolków and Nocturnal Culture Night in Deutzen, alongside a series of French dates extending into November. The catalogue combines programmed electronics, guitars and live percussion across industrial, EBM and electro-adjacent territory, reflecting the band’s own album credits. About Carpenter Brut Carpenter Brut is the stage name of Franck Hueso, a French darksynth musician from Poitiers active since 2012. He released three EPs, “EP I” (2012), “EP II” (2013) and “EP III” (2015), later compiled as the album “Trilogy” (2015), followed by “Leather Teeth” (2018), the “Blood Machines” soundtrack (2020), “Leather Terror” (2022) and “Leather Temple” (2026). His releases since 2015 have come out through his own label, No Quarter Prod. In live performances, Carpenter Brut is joined by guitarist Adrien Grousset and drummer Florent Marcadet, both also members of the French metal band Hacride.

The track is the third single from Ignea’s upcoming album “Monumental,” due October 23, 2026 via Napalm Records, and pairs Ignea vocalist Helle Bohdanova with LaPlegua on an industrial metal cut built around aggrotech and electro-industrial textures. “Prefab” looks at architecture and collective memory, themes that run through “Monumental,” which
items.body: Ukrainian modern metal band Ignea have released a new single, Prefab, featuring Andy LaPlegua of Combichrist. The track is the third single from Ignea’s upcoming album “Monumental,” due October 23, 2026 via Napalm Records, and pairs Ignea vocalist Helle Bohdanova with LaPlegua on an industrial metal cut built around aggrotech and electro-industrial textures. “Prefab” looks at architecture and collective memory, themes that run through “Monumental,” which the band describes as centered on nostalgia. Bohdanova wrote the lyrics; the music was composed by keyboardist Yevhenii Zhytniuk with additional contributions from Bohdanova. Bohdanova commented on the track: “‘Prefab’ reflects on the darker side of nostalgia – prefabricated socialist buildings, originally meant to give everyone a roof over their heads. But like many socialist ideals, the concept was flawed at its core: uniform, industrial, stripping people of individuality and personal choice, making them feel like ants inside their own homes. Remnants of this architecture still stand across Europe – from Ukraine and Poland, from Germany to France. As Ukrainians from a post-Soviet country, we grew up surrounded by the physical remains of a system that promised a bright future and delivered the opposite. In the ‘Prefab’ video, we wanted to convey the feeling of a confined, uniform space, a cramped room representing a typical Soviet apartment, where only the tenants ever change. When we shaped the demo, we were basically hearing Andy’s vocals in the back of our minds, and we’re so glad he agreed to lend his voice. Having Combichrist as part of the industrial metal track on our upcoming album […]” Andy LaPlegua formed Combichrist in 2003 as a solo studio project, building it into one of the touchstone acts of the aggrotech and industrial metal scenes alongside his other projects Icon of Coil and Panzer AG. Combichrist’s most recent album, “The Venom In The Mouth Of God,” was announced via Out Of Line Music earlier in 2026, following singles including “Demons Wanna Be Summoned” with King 810 and “Feraline.” “Monumental” is Ignea’s second full-length album, following 2023’s “Dreams of Lands Unseen.” Writing and recording took place largely during the winter of 2025-2026, amid icy temperatures and long power outages in Kyiv during the full-scale war in Ukraine. Bohdanova described the record’s concept: “Back in the 17th century, nostalgia was considered a deadly disease – and in many ways, it still is. Much of this album was inspired by modernist architecture – concrete giants built to signal progress and a brighter future, now slowly decaying.” The album spans nine tracks: “Darkness,” “Dreams of Lands Unseen,” “Presence of the Past,” “Prefab” (feat. Combichrist), “What Buildings Dream of,” “I am in Hell,” “Between No Longer and Not Yet,” “Harmony Manufactured” (feat. Hiraes), and “Nadir.” Mixing and mastering were handled by Grammy-nominated producer Jacob Hansen, whose credits include Delain, Amaranthe, Volbeat, Amon Amarth, Arch Enemy and Epica. “Monumental” arrives on translucent dark night blue splatter vinyl with booklet, solid silver vinyl, CD jewelcase, a CD/T-shirt bundle, and digitally, released via Napalm Records. Ignea will support Evergrey’s “Architects Of A New Weave” European tour alongside Stellar Circuits starting in November, taking “Prefab” and the rest of “Monumental” to stages across Scandinavia, the UK and mainland Europe. Ignea tour dates 11 November 2026 – Lund, Sweden – Mejeriet 12 November 2026 – Stockholm, Sweden – Kollektivet Livet 13 November 2026 – Linkoping, Sweden – Paletset 14 November 2026 – Gothenburg, Sweden – Filmstudion 2 15 November 2026 – Oslo, Norway – Salt 17 November 2026 – Hamburg, Germany – Logo 18 November 2026 – Berlin, Germany – Hole44 19 November 2026 – Munich, Germany – Feierwerk 20 November 2026 – Vienna, Austria – Weberknecht 21 November 2026 – Milan, Italy – Slaughter Club 22 November 2026 – Aarau, Switzerland – KiFF 23 November 2026 – Antwerp, Belgium – Zappa 25 November 2026 – Southampton, UK – The Brook 26 November 2026 – Birmingham, UK – Asylum 27 November 2026 – London, UK – The Underworld 28 November 2026 – Leeds, UK – The Key Club 29 November 2026 – Dublin, Ireland – Opium 30 November 2026 – Belfast, UK – Limelight 2 1 December 2026 – Glasgow, UK – G2 2 December 2026 – Newcastle, UK – Anarchy Brew 3 December 2026 – Manchester, UK – Rebellion 4 December 2026 – Bristol, UK – Strange Brew 5 December 2026 – Nottingham, UK – Saltbox 7 December 2026 – Paris, France – Petit Bain 8 December 2026 – Trier, Germany – Mergener Hof 9 December 2026 – Karlsruhe, Germany – Substage 10 December 2026 – Dortmund, Germany – Junkyard 11 December 2026 – Rotterdam, Netherlands – Baroeg 12 December 2026 – Maastricht, Netherlands – Muziekgieterij About Ignea Ignea formed in Ukraine in 2013, releasing the EP “Sputnik” the same year. The band mixes melodic and progressive metal with symphonic, electronic and folk elements, building material around narrative concepts. Ignea’s debut full-length, “The Sign of Faith,” followed in 2017. The band’s early single “Alga,” released as a hymn referencing the Crimean Tatars’ battle cry after the annexation of Crimea, became the first original song by a Ukrainian metal band recorded with a full symphonic orchestra. Ignea’s second album, “The Realms of Fire and Death” (2020), was funded through the band’s Patreon page and was later named Ukraine’s metal album of the year. A split EP with Ersedu, “BESTIA,” followed in 2021. After building an independent following through two albums and two EPs, Ignea signed to Napalm Records and released “Dreams of Lands Unseen” in 2023, an album dedicated to Ukrainian travel writer and photographer Sofia Yablonska. Despite the ongoing war, the band toured extensively, including a 43-date EU/UK run supporting Fear Factory, and has since played festivals including Wacken Open Air, Summer Breeze, Bloodstock and Brutal Assault, alongside club dates with Cradle of Filth, Epica and Butcher Babies. Nine Ignea tracks also feature in the video game “S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl.” The current lineup is Helle Bohdanova (vocals), Yevhenii Zhytniuk (keyboards), Dmytro Vinnichenko (guitars) and Oleksandr Kamyshyn (bass). Ignea’s second full-length, “Monumental,” follows “Dreams of Lands Unseen” on October 23, 2026, led by the singles “Prefab” featuring Andy LaPlegua and its predecessors, and supported by the band’s November-December European tour with Evergrey.

items.body: Tomates En Verano know exactly what a guitar is for: tension, impact, and the occasional act of vandalism. On El color del mar, the Mar del Plata trio turn shoegaze, gothic post-punk, and 1990s alternative rock into a record full of sudden pressure changes, serrated edges, and hooks that keep poking through the distortion. Five albums in, they sound less concerned with refinement than with making every shift in volume count. Pixies are all over this record, and that is meant as praise. You hear it in the sudden changes of pressure, the clipped guitar figures, the way Ignacio Giobellina can leave a song hanging on a few dry notes before dropping something much heavier into the room. There’s some Joey Santiago in that instinct: the understanding that a guitar doesn’t need seventeen pedals and a doctoral thesis to make you nervous. There’s something in the way the guitars and melodies crash against each other that echoes Lush, while the more expansive passages carry the oceanic airiness of Slowdive’s Just for a Day. The Breeders, Liz Phair, and Sonic Youth all rub elbows here, too, without turning the album into a museum tour of shoegaze and alternative rock. Carina Monjeau is the reason much of this works as well as it does. At times, her airy, cool delivery strongly recalls My Bloody Valentine’s Bilinda Butcher, sounding almost effortless while the guitars are busy throwing furniture around behind her. That contrast gives the record much of its personality. She never sounds as though she has to fight the arrangement for space, and Graham Sutton’s production deserves credit for that. Sutton, of Bark Psychosis, gives these songs mass without stuffing every available frequency until the record suffocates. The band’s solid bass lines carry as much character as a guitar hook, and Pedro Moscuzza’s drumming keeps the heavier sections from becoming a shapeless pile of amplification. There is muscle here, but there is also movement. At times, El color del mar feels like something you might have stumbled across on a particularly strange Lilith Fair bill in 1997, right after a band indebted to The Breeders. It would feel equally at home on a Lollapalooza stage, with staff handing out earplugs to anyone braving the volume near the front. Farther back, some listeners might lie in the grass and give themselves over to the music’s reverie, looking up until they feel as though they could fall into the sky. The dayglo decade of the 90s hangs heavily over the album, yet the trio have enough personality to avoid sounding like collectors showing off their favorite records. The title translates as The Color of the Sea, though the band connects it to internal conflict and the sensation of living in a world where everything seems slightly misplaced. That idea fits these songs rather well. They keep shifting their balance: thick guitars give way to cleaner passages, sweetness brushes against abrasion, and quieter sections make the harder moments hit with greater force. Francisco Raccanello Monjeau adds piano to Algo común, while Luana Giobellina Monjeau of Buenos Vampiros plays bass on El color del mar and Todo comienza en casa. Both appearances broaden the arrangements without turning them into showcases. After more than twenty years together, Tomates En Verano sound less interested in proving their credentials than in making a record with big guitars, strong songs, and enough instability to keep the volume knob within reach. El color del mar makes a convincing case that the old alternative-rock machinery still has plenty of dangerous moving parts. Listen to El Color del Mar below, out now via Casa del Puente Discos. You can order the album here. items._cn_summary: 阿根廷三人乐队Tomates En Verano的第五张专辑将shoegaze、哥特后朋克与90年代另类摇滚融合，吉他使用强调张力与冲击感而非精致修饰。乐队在安静的干音段落与厚重的失真墙之间反复切换，制造骤然的音量落差与压迫感。女主唱Carina Monjeau冷静飘忽的声线与躁动的吉他层形成鲜明反差，让人联想到My Bloody Valentine的Bilinda Butcher。Graham Sutton的混音保留了高频空间，避免了音墙过于窒息。贝斯线条与鼓组同样具有表现力，使作品在沉重与流动之间保持平衡。专辑深受90年代影响，但乐队本身的性格避免了单纯的致敬感。标题虽指向海洋的色彩，实则隐喻内心的失衡感——歌曲不断在甜美与粗粝、清澈与厚浊之间摇摆，构成这张充满张力与对比的作品。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — One of Radiohead's founding guitarists (and still member) Ed O'Brien releases his second studio album as a solo artist. I don't know any of the guest musician/collaborators but you can bet that Ed had his pick of the cr'me de la cr'me!1. "Incantations" (7:41) a single repeating acoustic guitar arpeggio provides the bed for 1:45 of Ed's folk singing. It honestly sounds like something from an early Roy Harper album. Other instruments, hand percussives and electronics, join in to move the music into territory previously traveled by the likes of DONOVAN and BJ'RK. Floating background vocals sound like Bj'rk's Inuit Choir on the Vespero tours. At 5:40 the percussionist(s) are joined by drums, electric bass, electric guitars, and keyboard atmospherics--which play out until slowly being faded out while Dave Okumu's bass and Ed's reverberating guitar notes continue to the song's end. Cool song! (13.875/15)2. "Blue Morpho" (6:18) another really cool atmospheric sonosphere created by guitars, wordless vocals, bass, synth washes, and, this time, full symphony strings. It's quite lovely--even moving: chords and multiple melody lines floating, flowing, shifting, morphing, and melding into one gorgeous textural feast. And the whole time I'm feel quite a little debt owed (or homage given) to George Martin and The Beatles. (Think of songs like "Blackbird" and "I Am the Walrus" as well as albums like Magical Mystery Tour.) Brilliant and beautiful! (9.75/10)3. "Sweet Spot" (4:10) double lines of picked acoustic guitar chords woven into one though coming from both sides of the stage starts out this beautiful, atmospheric and kind of eerie (like GRAVENHURST) music over/within which Ed sings both lead and backing vocals. I like the way the orchestra strings slowly move to the fore as Ed's lead voice sinks into the instrumental mix. Eventually, the strings (and, I'll assume, keyboard electronics) end up alone, finishing the song after everybody/everything else has left. Not as memorable as the previous songs but rewarded for the creative sound and structural tactics. (9/10)4. "Teachers" (5:18) a funky bass 'n' drum pattern is surrounded and permeated by eerie atmospherics. Ed's heavily-treated ghost-voice enters toward the end of the first minute, singing in a pleasant monotone for a minute or so but then it leaves, whereupon the bass, drums, guitars, and synths all seem to spread out into loose, adventurous swaths away from but still anchored in the main theme. The final minute sees the vocal choir sing, "open wide" before the instruments all stop or fade away, leaving only weird electronic noises to close out the song. (8.875/10)5. "Solfeggio" (2:36) guitar/electronic harpsichord chord perpetuated with sustain and arpeggiation open this before more layers of voice-originating atmospherics enter and steer the with an eerie yet unthreatening kind of melody line, repeated over and over before signing off with a final lower-register three-note sequence, all the while the glitchy electronica effects are increasingly present, even rising to a driver's position, like something from a SyFy Continuum soundtrack experience (think Au4's "Everyone Is Everyone [and Everything Is Everything]"). More genius song/sound making. (4.4375/5)6. "Thin Places" (2:19) flute, wordless voice, synthetics all woven together to create a kind of dream-like out-of-body astral travel experience. (4.4375/5)7. "Obrigado" (9:53) a very cool, almost jazz-lite rhythm track over/within which Ed & Co. deliver some pretty awesome atmospherics (as well as vocals). The reverse-delay guitar effects for Ed's guitar solo in the seventh and eighth minutes are only surpassed by the dreamy psychedelic soundscape floating and morphing beneath it (and, later, by the amazing wordless vocal tracks raging in the background--which I think one must attribute to Clare Torey-inspired Awsa Berstrom). Ed's ultra-cool voice reminds me of both George Harrison, Gadi Caplan, Donovan, and Harry Nilsson as well as, you know, Radiohead. Really a cool, amazing, and powerful song. A pleasure to listen to every single time I do. (19.5/20)Total Time 38:15It's weird how much/how often I hear core/key Radiohead sounds in Ed's music here. This leads me to feel strongly how important and integral he was/is to the Radiohead sound--to their music.A/five stars; a brilliant display of creative/innovative sound and song crafting that stands out as a masterpiece of extrapolated future music (as if Ed's projecting himself into the 22nd Century or beyond--or even another dimension). A modern musical masterpiece. Highly recommended. One of the best albums I've heard from 2026.
items._cn_summary: Radiohead成员Ed O'Brien第二张个人专辑延续了乐队后期的氛围化探索，以木吉他分解和弦为基底，叠加电子音效、人声层次、交响弦乐与实验打击乐，构建出流动且不断变形的音景。多首歌采用循环动机逐步展开的方式，声音层层叠加又缓慢消散，制造出冥想般的氛围感。部分作品带有民谣根源，向早期Roy Harper、Donovan致敬，同时融入Björk式的人声处理与电子质感。弦乐编排暗示对Beatles及George Martin制作美学的继承。整体偏向氛围化艺术流行，融合民谣根基与电子实验，介于独立流行和前卫摇滚之间，跨界融合度较好但在实验性与独特性上仍较为温和。

items.body: Review by higgins — There are debuts that sound like debuts, with that mixture of timidity and overreach so typical of someone still searching for their place, and there are debuts that arrive already carrying the astonishing confidence of people who've been playing together for half a lifetime without anyone quite noticing. Datura Lodge decidedly belongs to this second lineage. And it's no coincidence: Nicky B and W. have known each other and played together since their teens, something that comes through in every breath of this self-titled album, a chemistry that can't be improvised or bought in any studio, however good it may be.I listened to this record thanks to a promo copy the label was kind enough to send me, and I'm deeply grateful for it, because Datura Lodge is one of those works you'd rather have stumbled upon yourself, tripping over it in a record shop, and yet here we are, with the good fortune of having had it in hand ahead of time.The New Jersey duo doesn't hide its sources, nor should it. There's a melodic streak that leads straight back to Genesis, especially in those moments when the vocal reaches for the hook without giving up harmonic complexity. And there's something else too, something of our own era: that way of organizing the chaos, of metering out the tension and releasing it at exactly the right moment, which inevitably brings to mind a more restrained Steven Wilson, or his band Porcupine Tree on the days it decides to smile.Tracks like "Stone" or "Can" show that technique serves emotion rather than the other way around, with an instrumental display (Adam Holzman is in there on keys, contributing a great deal) that never tips into gratuitous showmanship. But it's in the fragility of "Hole" or the almost uncomfortable honesty of "Them" where Datura Lodge reveals its true nature: an album that knows how to laugh at itself while talking about rootlessness, generational disillusionment, and the strange task of staying human amid a full digital shipwreck.Datura Lodge doesn't reinvent progressive rock, but it inhabits it with a naturalness and a joy of playing that are sorely missed in so many current releases, more concerned with orthodoxy than with life.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自新泽西二人组的同名首作，延续了Genesis的旋律骨架与Porcupine Tree式的张力编排。两位乐手自少年时代便共同演奏，长期磨合赋予作品天然的默契感，编曲中可见Adam Holzman的键盘贡献。专辑并不试图重塑前卫摇滚，而是以一种从容的演奏状态栖居其中，作品如"Stone""Can"侧重器乐技法服务于情感表达，而"Hole""Them"则呈现出脆弱与自省的质地，涉及漂泊感、世代幻灭与数字化时代的生存命题。整体定位更偏向传统prog脉络内的成熟表达，与极端实验或电子融合方向距离较远，但其内敛的气质与诚恳的创作态度为当下过度关注正统性的前卫摇滚场景带来了一种少见的松弛与愉悦。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The affirmation often has a psychological value that operates at an unconscious level; it begins from the outside and ends up taking hold internally. The Yes Album was a new beginning for many reasons: the first to feature Steve Howe, the first in which the compositions of Anderson, Chris Squire, and soon Howe would acquire that classic status and the first where rock, jazz, and a distinctive balance between acoustic and electric elements would find their signature style and a home within the progressive universe.There are many classic Yes lineups, and although the subsequent era might be considered the "classic of classics," the 1971 period is already worthy of that title. Gathering at Langley Farm, they recorded a handful of songs that would become enduring favorites, not only for that lineup but for those that followed, and have been performed live ever since.I'm a fan of the Peter Banks era, but Steve Howe, while retaining that affinity for rock 'n' roll, jazz, and classical music, brought a rhythm, a groove, and a fingering style, along with a cosmic dimension, that set the band apart right from "Yours Is No Disgrace." The vocal harmonies, often bordering on a cappella, were just one of many hallmarks that emerged with this album. The band also gained a warmth and an intimacy it hadn't possessed before; tracks like "Yours Is No Disgrace" featured not only instrumental sections but also intimate moments that made for a complete experience."Clap" is the first of many acoustic tracks by Steve Howe; composed of several sections, some with a pastoral, rustic feel and others with a distinct rock-and-roll vibe, the version that made the final cut was recorded live at London's Lyceum Theatre and would forever define one of the facets of this new Yes."Starship Trooper" must be one of the first tracks that made me fall in love with the band. Jon was gradually reaching the peak of his expressive potential, conveying a genuine emotion that was reinforced by Chris Squire on bass, Bill Bruford on drums, and, son, Steve Howe on guitar (who already seemed like a full-fledged member, even though Peter Banks still appeared on the album cover!). There was a palpable sense of communion as they focused on conveying their musical vision. Tony Kaye was solid, too, though he would later be succeeded by someone with such a massive aura that it would elevate "Starship Trooper" to even greater heights. Once again, the vocal harmonies and Jon's voice stood out... and just as the emotion reached its peak, "W�rm", the third section, would kick in. Steve would start off solo, with the rest of the band gradually joining him, creating a soundscape that felt like the prelude to a space voyage and the actual liftoff. And the first of many memorable riffs with an electrifying personality.The emotional momentum didn't let up, as a powerful new surge of feeling arrived with "I've Seen All Good People", a track that is 100% Yes. The band always drew sustenance from both the technical/virtuosic side and the spiritual/emotional one; neither works without the other, and it was their combination that gave birth to their best songs and albums. The track is neatly divided into two parts: the acoustic first section, "Your Move", which carries an almost Andean feel, and the rock-driven second half, "All Good People." The two work in tandem, creating the song's magical contrast."A Venture" is an atypical and unusual track within the context of the �lbum, and a very beautiful one. It features very interesting breaks and syncopated drum and guitar work from Howe and Bruford; towards the end, Chris's bass and Tony Kaye's distinctly jazzy solo leave you wishing they would keep playing like that for even longer."Perpetual Change" is the final track, and Bill Bruford's presence is as notable as it is significant; the format, an elaborate introduction leading into a fully developed song, set a precedent for what was to come. Hints of a country feel followed by a jazz-inflected progression, along with the polyrhythms and counterpoint in the finale, exemplified the band's high level of technical proficiency. Meanwhile, the vocal interplay between Jon and Chris offered a different facet, helping to create an album that holds a unique place in history. There are many layers to consider: while the band's subsequent work was undoubtedly more complex and elaborate, and is rightly regarded as some of their best, this album possesses its own distinct value. It stands as an equally great record, not for the same reasons as the later material, but for others; after all, as we have seen, Yes is a multi-dimensional band.
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑标志着乐队的转型起点：新吉他手Steve Howe的加入带来了融合摇滚、爵士与古典元素的演奏风格，其标志性的节奏律动与宇宙感贯穿全作。专辑在声学与电声之间取得独特平衡，多首作品以多段落结构展开，从田园质朴的吉他独奏到渐进构建的声景空间感，体现了渐进摇滚的叙事性与器乐展开逻辑。Jon Anderson的人声表现力在此达到新高度，与Chris Squire的贝斯线及多声部和声形成乐队标志特征。作品融合摇滚的爆发力与爵士的即兴感，同时保持整体结构的统一与情感弧线。评论指出这些作品在后续现场演出中被反复演绎，成为该乐队曲库中历久弥新的核心。作为1970年代英国渐进摇滚的代表作，其艺术性与结构复杂度契合前卫音乐审美，但相对偏向传统渐进摇滚范式，未深入更极端的实验领域。

items.body: Naples dark folk act Corde Oblique released the single “Emma” on September 11, 2026, the first track from their tenth studio album, “All’ombra dei fanciulli in fiore” (In the Shadow of Young Girls in Flower), due November 27 on German label Dark Vinyl Records. The title references Marcel Proust and centers on parenthood. Emma by Corde Oblique ‘Emma’ previews a 12-track album recorded in Naples and mastered at Abbey Road Corde Oblique, led by composer and art historian Riccardo Prencipe, recorded “All’ombra dei fanciulli in fiore” between Peppino di Capri’s Splash Studios in Naples and London, where it was mastered at Abbey Road Studios by Alex Wharton. The album runs 12 tracks plus a bonus track, mixed by Massimo Aluzzi, and moves across metal, prog rock, folk songwriting and dark wave elements. The band’s core lineup on the record is Prencipe on classical and electric guitar, Alfredo Notarloberti on violin, Alessio Sica on drums, Umberto Lepore on bass and Rita Saviano on vocals. Guest contributors include singer-songwriter Andrea Chimenti, a voice of the Italian New Wave scene, on three tracks, and actress Maddalena Crippa, who provides a spoken-word performance. The digipak and booklet use vintage 1980s photographs of Pozzuoli and the Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields), tying the album to the region where it was recorded. Corde Oblique open a promotional tour on October 24 at the Schwarzer Herbst Festival in Löbau, Germany, followed by Italian dates at Teatro Bolivar in Naples on November 20 and at Improve in Castelfranco Veneto on November 21. About Corde Oblique Corde Oblique is an Italian dark folk project founded and led by Naples-based composer and art historian Riccardo Prencipe. Side-Line has followed the band’s output since at least 2018, and covered their 2020 album “The Moon Is a Dry Bone.” “Emma” and the accompanying album “All’ombra dei fanciulli in fiore” mark the band’s tenth full-length and its first new release on Dark Vinyl Records, continuing a catalog built on the intersection of classical guitar, folk songwriting and darker, heavier textures.
items._genre: dark folk / neoclassical / progressive rock / darkwave
items._cn_summary: 意大利那不勒斯暗潮民谣乐队Corde Oblique发行第十张录音室专辑，以普鲁斯特《追忆似水年华》第二卷命名，围绕父母身份主题展开。专辑在Peppino di Capri的Splash Studios录制，于伦敦Abbey Road Studios完成母带处理，融合古典吉他、小提琴、民谣创作与黑暗氛围等元素，横跨金属、前卫摇滚、民谣写作与暗潮多种风格。阵容以主创Riccardo Prencipe为核心，客座嘉宾包括意大利新浪潮歌手Andrea Chimenti与演员Maddalena Crippa的念白表演。唱片包装采用1980年代 Pozzuoli与Campi Flegrei地区的复古照片，与录音所在地建立文化联系。德国独立厂牌Dark Vinyl Records发行，将于十月开启欧洲巡演。

items._cn_summary: 这是中岛元广暌违五年的新作，以环境破坏与资本主义终结为概念主题，音乐上模拟深海与意识深层的沉浸感。他本人以指弹吉他为核心，叠加微弱噪声、柔和管弦乐器音色，邀请多位客座乐手参与，营造出有机氛围与近乎冥想式的寂静。整体呈现学院派与现代古典交织的气质，结构上偏向氛围化处理而非传统作曲逻辑，吉他与器乐层次之间的留白与纹理变化是核心聆听点。对于偏好实验性氛围、冥想音乐与跨界合作的听众有较高契合度，但商业化痕迹较弱，更适合小众场景聆听。

items.body: The Wind is a peaceful retreat, a meditation on the natural world, and a call to act on the threat of climate change when inactivity and tepid response has become a disturbing norm. The Wind also details the ancient tale of a saint who carried the wind to an airless French valley, and in a similar way, Balmorhea’s debut release on Deutsche Grammophon (which releases April 9 on CD, vinyl, and digitally), is swept up in the air, too. It’s music for the planet, and a timely reminder of Earth’s fragility. People all over the world are reconnecting with nature and finding solace, rest, and peace in her arms. But The Wind also contains the sounds of Earth. Prayer flags can be heard flapping in a breeze, and piano, pipe organ, harmonium, double bass, wind chimes, and guitar are all a part of its gentle-but-stirring sound. Guitars remain light and airy, and a swooping vocal pulls the music to all four corners of the globe. The Texas-based duo of Rob Lowe and Michael A. Muller have created protective and quiet music, and the protection of the environment and the opportunity for renewal slips into the title tracks, too. ‘La Vagabonde’ is named after the catamaran that Greta Thunberg travelled on while crossing the Atlantic. Towards the end of the record’s completion, Lowe discovered a translation of the Otia Imperialia, a thirteenth-century compendium containing descriptions of marvels and miracles. Lowe was drawn to the tale of ‘The wind which St Caesarius shut up in a glove’, wherein the archbishop of Arles carries the sea breeze to a desolate valley and releases it to make the area fruitful and healthy. The same ethos can be felt in The Wind, with its life-renewing and reaffirming philosophies attaching themselves to its ambient music. www.balmorheamusic.com www.deutschegrammophon.com
items._cn_summary: Balmorhea 由 Rob Lowe 和 Michael Muller 组成，德州双人组首张发行于 Deutsche Grammophon 厂牌的作品以风为核心意象。专辑概念源自十三世纪文献 Otia Imperialia 中圣 Caesarius 将海风封入手套并带至荒凉山谷使其重获生机的故事，同时呼应 Greta Thunberg 跨大西洋航行所乘双体船。乐器编制涵盖钢琴、管风琴、簧风琴、低音提琴、风铃与吉他，辅以飘扬的祈祷旗声效与人声采样，营造出轻柔而具呼吸感的氛围纹理。乐评将其定位为面向地球的冥想之作，强调环境保护与自然重生的哲学主题，介于当代古典、环境音乐与轻量后摇之间，情感基调偏向内省与宁静。

items._cn_summary: 这张作品由David Dzubinski作曲，Prism Quartet（普里斯姆四重奏）联合人声Ursula Rucker、打击乐Tyshawn Sorey及小提琴Carlos Santiago共同呈现，作为该组合"Unlocking Your Inner Composer"系列合作计划的一部分，于2025年11月在费城自由图书馆演出录制。全曲时长不足四分钟，却在原始粗粝与抒情诗意之间快速切换，既展现了作曲家的结构控制力，也体现出多位演奏家在即兴与协作层面的灵活度。作为面向团体新作，由四大件乐器——四支萨克斯、打击乐、小提琴与人声——编织而成的音色层次较为丰富，融合了当代室内乐、实验爵士与跨界即兴的元素。乐评来自RootsWorld主编Cliff Furnald的简短推荐，短文中虽提及"genre-blurring"（类型融合）作为该组合一贯特色，但未对和声语言、空间处理或具体演奏技法做深入分析，信息密度有限。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统音乐素材，乐手各自带来不同的演奏视角。开场曲以粗犷奔腾的节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的声线；另一首唯一原创曲目中，口簧琴与风笛提供了持续向前的推进力。扬琴为传统民谣增添了精致的背景层次，口簧琴的柔和音色在终曲中与笛子和弦乐交织，呈现出一种令人兴奋的失衡感。整体营造出古老而略带粗粝的氛围，展现了乐队成熟的音乐素养。作为引介之作令人期待后续完整专辑。

items.body: “Caminando Por La Playa” means walking along the beach, yet Aldo Zolev wrote it about a happy day marching through Bogotá, a city more than 2,600 metres up in the Andes and hundreds of kilometres from the sea. The percussion sets a brisk marching step through the instrumental, with Sandro Londoño on cymbals. Sandra Duque plays the melody on bassoon over Zolev’s double bass. Zolev describes the piece as energetic and lively, built on a memory of Colombian rhythms, and says the walk stands for a way through life, urging his friends to walk “por la vida hoy y siempre“, through life today and always, and to be happy. Zolev comes from Pamplona, a small Andean city in north-eastern Colombia near the Venezuelan border, where his grandfather, a professional double bassist, started him on the instrument. He moved to Bogotá to study double bass at the conservatory of the Universidad Nacional de Colombia and took jazz and harmony lessons with saxophonist Antonio Arnedo. He formed the world-jazz group Dos Aguas and later played in Bereket, an ensemble devoted to Turkish and Middle Eastern music. In 2007 he set up EnnO, the independent Bogotá label and studio that has since produced 25 albums and runs its own world music festival. Three years later he launched UVA Sexteto, bringing the oud in alongside his double bass. He has also recorded with MARIAZÚ, whose album Eau de Vie – Agua Ardiente was cut outdoors in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, with birdsong and running water around acoustic instruments and indigenous percussion. In 2025 Zolev relaunched Sensaciones Bajo La Lluvia, the album that carries “Caminando Por La Playa”, and he has just come back from a summer tour of Europe. Listen to “Caminando Por La Playa” and the full Sensaciones Bajo La Lluvia album HERE The post Daily Discovery: Aldo Zolev – Caminando Por La Playa appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于哥伦比亚低音提琴演奏家 Aldo Zolev 及其作品《Caminando Por La Playa》的介绍性乐评。曲目以打击乐节奏铺陈行进感，巴松管在低音提琴上方演奏旋律线，融合了哥伦比亚传统节奏元素。Zolev 来自哥伦比亚安第斯山区潘普洛纳，在波哥大国立大学音乐学院学习低音提琴，后涉猎爵士与和声课程。他组建过世界爵士团体 Dos Aguas，也参与演奏土耳其与中东音乐的 Bereket 乐团，并创办了独立厂牌与工作室 EnnO。他还将乌德琴引入爵士编制，组建 UVA Sexteto，展现了跨文化器乐对话的探索。整体内容偏向人物背景与作品介绍，缺乏对声音质感、编曲结构或艺术价值的深度评析，更接近新闻推介而非深度评论。

items.body: Argentine post-punk project Zudpöl releases the single Disciple: In Control on 11 September 2026, through the Buenos Aires label Catálogo Negro / No Me Escucho Records (NMER). The two-track release pairs the title song “Disciple” with the B-side “In Control”, sitting between dark post-punk and the club sound of the late 1980s and early 1990s. Both tracks were built on a vintage drum machine, a mini analog synthesizer, a pocket sampler, guitar and bass, with software used only for the final edit. No Me Escucho Records describes the approach as “simple hardware and no virtual instruments”, the same method Zudpöl has used on its earlier releases. The Bandcamp page embeds the single below. Disciple: In Control by Zudpöl Zudpöl on Catálogo Negro since its 2022 debut “Disciple: In Control” is issued under the Catálogo Negro imprint of No Me Escucho Records, the label that has released Zudpöl’s catalog since 2022. NMER previously put out the free covers compilation “NMER C-01 2024”, on which Zudpöl contributed a version of Death In June’s “Fall Apart”. About Zudpöl Zudpöl is a post-punk, darkwave and coldwave project released through No Me Escucho Records, the independent label founded in Buenos Aires, Argentina by Darío Martinez and Diego Centurión, joined in 2021 by Ferran Pont Vergés. Zudpöl debuted on NMER in 2022 with the album “A Weaker Sun”, followed in June 2023 by the single “In Fear” and, on 24 November 2023, by the six-track album “Last Lights”, which extended the project’s coldwave core with ethereal and dream-pop textures. In January 2025, Zudpöl contributed a cover of Death In June’s “Fall Apart” to NMER’s free “NMER C-01 2024” covers compilation. All of these releases share the same production method: hardware synthesizers, samplers and drum machines, without virtual instruments. “Disciple: In Control” is Zudpöl’s first single since “Last Lights”, continuing that hardware-based approach on Catálogo Negro.
items._cn_summary: 阿根廷后朋克/暗潮项目Zudpöl在布宜诺斯艾利斯独立厂牌Catálogo Negro旗下发行双曲单曲《Disciple: In Control》，标题曲与B面曲分别呈现，介于暗黑后朋克与八十年代末至九十年代初俱乐部声响之间。制作方式延续项目一贯的硬件路线：复古鼓机、小型模拟合成器、口袋采样器、吉他与贝斯构成主体，软件仅用于最终剪辑，不使用任何虚拟乐器。这一方法自2022年首张专辑《A Weaker Sun》以来保持一致，此前作品《Last Lights》曾在冷波核心里融入梦幻流行的空灵质感。文中提及Zudpöl曾在厂牌免费翻唱合辑中演绎Death In June的《Fall Apart》，显示出与欧洲暗潮传统的关联。整体为信息性新闻稿式乐评，缺少具体声响描述与音乐分析。

items.body: New York darkwave duo Ghostbells released “The Silence” on September 17, 2026 through Out Of Line Music, as a digital single with an accompanying music video. It is the second piece of original material Jessica Perry and Jim Finley have put out since their debut EP “Catacouture” arrived in February, following “Curses” in August. The Silence by ghostbells The track returns to the confessional side of the duo’s sound: 80s and new wave melody laid over a 90s EBM pulse, pushed forward by the kind of driving, dancefloor-ready arrangement that keeps its darker moments moving rather than static. The lyric follows someone consumed by sadness and reaching for a version of life that used to feel joyful, with a plea that goes nowhere: Can someone save me / I hear nothing / it’s the silence that takes me. Ghostbells described the writing behind the song directly. “The Silence is about being consumed by sadness and longing for times before, when there used to be a joy for life. There is a cry for help but it seems useless when it goes unanswered.” Jessica Perry named the source more specifically: “Struggles that I have personally endured and some of the lowest times in life.” Ghostbells follow Dark Summer Open Air with ‘The Silence’ “The Silence” lands right after one of the duo’s largest shows to date. On September 12, Ghostbells played Dark Summer Open Air Vol. 2 at Wasserschloss Klaffenbach in Chemnitz, Germany, alongside Blutengel and Chrom, in front of roughly 3,000 people. In just over a year since signing to Out Of Line, the pair have built a run of remix work alongside their own releases, reworking Blutengel’s “Schwarzer Engel”, Cemetery Skyline’s “Torn Away” and Blitz Union’s “Evolution”. The single carries that momentum into a run of US club dates and a full Latin American tour supporting label-mates Hocico, followed by European festival dates into next year. Tour dates for Ghostbells in 2026 and 2027 September 19, 2026 – Los Angeles, CA, USA – Bar Sinister September 23 – October 4, 2026 – Hocico “Unseen Horror Scenes” tour support October 29, 2026 – Fort Worth, TX, USA – Haltom Theatre October 30, 2026 – Houston, TX, USA – Scout Bar November 13, 2026 – Tampa, FL, USA – New World Tampa November 14, 2026 – Miami, FL, USA – Las Rosas November 20-21, 2026 – Wangels, Germany – Plage Noire Festival November 28, 2026 – Essen, Germany – Obsidian Echoes Festival July 24-25, 2027 – Cologne, Germany – Amphi Festival About Ghostbells Ghostbells are a duo from New York City: Jessica Perry on vocals, guitar, bass and synth, and Jim Finley on production, vocals, bass, guitar and synth. The project signed to Berlin label Out Of Line Music in 2025 and released its first single, “Darkness Saves“, that August. Three digital EPs followed before year’s end, and the duo’s debut EP proper, “Catacouture”, arrived on Out Of Line on February 5, 2026, collecting six tracks including “Darkness Saves”, “Ghosts”, “Wrath” and “Cry4Her” and giving the band its first CD pressing. Since then, Ghostbells have kept up a steady release and touring pace: a run of remixes for Blutengel, Cemetery Skyline and Blitz Union, the “Curses” single and video in August, and festival and club dates across the UK, Europe and the US. “The Silence” is their second original track since “Catacouture”, released as the band works toward its debut full-length album, and it opens a touring stretch that runs from Los Angeles through Latin America to the Amphi Festival in Germany next summer.

items.body: London-based queer alt-metal artist Ray Noir released “Gothstar” on September 17th 2026, a six-track EP that mixes metalcore guitars with rave and electronic club production. Ray Noir’s “Gothstar” EP is out digitally and on vinyl and CD. The EP collects the four singles issued since April 2026 and adds two new recordings. It opens with “Label Whxre” and continues with “Black”, “Boys”, and “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu, the New York artist and former Echo Black frontman. The new track “Crush” follows, and “Gothstar (Alternative Version)”, a solo version of the title track, closes the record. Ray Noir wrote the material with Jon Cass and Tom Saint, who are also the EP’s producers. The track credits for “Black” and “Crush” list Cass as producer and Saint for additional production, mixing and mastering, with Saint also singing backing vocals on “Crush”. Cass, a member of UK post-hardcore band As Everything Unfolds, previously produced Ray Noir’s 2025 EP “Against The Machine”. The release material describes the EP as dealing with identity, confidence and sexuality, with “Gothstar” as both a character and an attitude at its centre. Ray Noir commented: “Growing up in the Norwegian metal scene, I didn’t really see anyone like me. With Gothstar, I wanted to create the world I wish I’d had back then. It’s gay, it’s heavy, it’s sweaty, it’s camp and it doesn’t take itself too seriously. Basically, if Berghain had a mosh pit, I’d like to think this would be playing.” “Crush” is the focus track of the EP. Ray Noir based it on his own experience of growing up in Norway’s metal scene and on “Heated Rivalry”, Rachel Reid’s gay ice hockey romance novel, which was adapted for television in 2025. The lyrics name the story’s lead couple, Ilya and Shane, and include lines in Norwegian. Four singles ahead of the EP “Label Whxre” opened the “Gothstar” campaign on 2 April 2026. “Black” followed on 14 May 2026 with a video directed by Ray Noir, and “Boys” arrived in June 2026 with a video filmed at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store in Islington, north London. The title track “Gothstar” featuring Danny Blu came out on 13 August 2026 together with an official music video. ‘Gothstar'”‘ release party in London Ray Noir marks the release with a party at Slim Jim’s Liquor Store on Saturday 19 September 2026, the venue where the “Boys” video was filmed. Tom Saint is listed as special guest. Entry is free, with tickets via Ray Noir – Gothstar EP Release Party on DICE. Get the EP as vinyl or CD here! About Ray Noir Ray Noir is a queer alternative artist based in London. His official biography places his background in Oslo’s black-metal underground, and his sound combines metal guitars with electronic club production. He released his first single, “Double Trouble”, in 2014. In October 2023 he issued “Pity Party“, the lead single from the mixtape “Scorpio”, followed on 1 November 2023 by “Latency“. The seven-track “Scorpio” arrived in 2024, and his official biography lists a top-five placement in the German Alternative Charts. A deluxe edition of “Scorpio” followed in July 2024, adding “All Alone” featuring Mariann Rosa of Surferosa, a “Double Trouble” remix by TOVA, remixes by Gothminister, Corlyx and Tension Control, and “You, Me & The Devil” featuring Tom Saint. That August he supported Combichrist at the Underworld in London and played the Electro Night in Oslo at Revolver with Piston Damp on 31 August 2024. On 14 February 2025 he released “Razorblade Romance“, written with Steve Stevens and Madeleine Wood, featuring Stevens on guitar and produced and mixed by Jon Cass. A cover of Tears for Fears’ “Shout” followed in May 2025, with guitar by Arno Von Detritus and backing vocals by Ben Christo of The Sisters of Mercy. “Dead Valentine” came out on 3 July 2025 and announced the EP “Against The Machine”, released on 18 September 2025 with “Razorblade Romance”, “Dead Valentine”, “Mad World” and an alternative version of “YMATD”. A deluxe edition followed in December 2025 with remixes by Tension Control, Verona On Venus, Junkie Kut and Ays Kura, alongside vinyl and CD editions. Ray Noir opened 2026 with the singles “Temptation” in January and “Breathe” in February. “Gothstar” is his second EP after “Against The Machine” and continues his work with Jon Cass, who produced both EPs, and Tom Saint, who also featured on the 2024 “Scorpio” deluxe edition.
items._cn_summary: 伦敦酷儿另类金属艺人Ray Noir于2026年9月发行六首曲目EP《Gothstar》，将metalcore吉他与锐舞俱乐部电子制作相融合。由Jon Cass与Tom Saint共同担任制作人，后者来自英国后硬核乐队As Everything Unfolds。EP收录此前四首单曲并加入两首新作，其中与前Echo Black主唱Danny Blu合作的标题曲为核心曲目之一。EP聚焦身份、自信与性取向议题，Ray Noir以自己在挪威金属场景中的成长经历为素材，新曲《Crush》灵感源自瑞秋·里德2025年改编为电视剧的冰球题材小说《Heated Rivalry》，歌词中直接引用主角名字并夹杂挪威语。整体概念将Berghain式锐舞美学与金属pit结合，呈现出兼具沉重感、戏剧性与自嘲气质的酷儿金属姿态。

items.body: Boston publisher SIGNALS Press launched a Kickstarter campaign on 10 September 2026 for “Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement“, a 320-page survey of the graphic design that grew up alongside industrial music. The campaign runs through 2 October 2026, with books shipping spring 2027. The book traces the movement’s visual language from post-punk Britain and Cold War Europe through Reagan-era America, across album covers, logos, posters, type studies and ephemera. It documents the graphic identities of bands and labels including Throbbing Gristle and Industrial Records, Cabaret Voltaire, Mute Records, Nettwerk, wax trax!, Einstürzende Neubauten, Skinny Puppy, Front 242, Ministry, KMFDM and Nine Inch Nails. Designers contributing directly to the book include Neville Brody, Rob Sheridan, Richard Borge, Rick Valicenti, Patrick Codenys, Steven R. Gilmore, Simon Granger, Simone Grant, Brian Shanley and Martin Atkins. The Kickstarter’s reward tiers include a pin designed by Simon Granger of Nitzer Ebb Produkt and two shirts by Steven R. Gilmore. “Industrial music didn’t just change how music sounded, it changed how music looked,” said coauthor Chris Grimley. “Designers were sampling medical imagery, military documents, brutalist architecture, and early computer graphics into something coherent and international, and that history has never been collected. It sits in aftermarket bins and collectors’ stacks. This book brings it together.” The book is authored by GR—APP, the shared pseudonym of Chris Grimley and Alan Rapp. Grimley is founder and creative director of SIGNALS Press and has authored, coauthored and designed numerous books; Rapp is editorial director of SIGNALS Press and a former college DJ and music critic. “Industrial Music/Graphics” is produced as a physical object in its own right: 8 x 10.25 inches, 320 pages, Otabind layflat binding, four-color interior and a six-color foil-stamped, offset-printed cover. The Kickstarter campaign carries a Kickstarter “Project We Love” designation. About SIGNALS Press SIGNALS Press is a Boston-based publisher founded and led by Chris Grimley, who has authored, coauthored and designed multiple books and began making music after covering Skinny Puppy in high school. Alan Rapp, the press’s editorial director, is a former college DJ and music critic. Together the pair write as GR—APP, a pseudonym paying homage to the artistic aliases adopted by figures within the industrial scene the book documents. “Industrial Music/Graphics: A Visual History of a Movement” is SIGNALS Press’s Kickstarter campaign running through 2 October 2026, with fulfillment planned for spring 2027.

items.body: Infacted Recordings launches the Zoth Ommog Classix series, a vinyl-only reissue line reviving catalog from the German EBM and electro-industrial label Zoth Ommog. The first release is a limited grey-vinyl pressing of Lights Of Euphoria’s 1995 debut album “Brainstorm“, out 16 October 2026, followed on 23 October by Menschdefekt’s fifth studio album “Into the Void” on CD. Zoth Ommog was founded by Talla 2XLC after he left Techno Drome International. Its first release was Italian electro act Pankow’s “Kunst & Wahnsinn” EP. Talla continued T.D.I.’s early program with artists including Bigod 20, Aircrash Bureau, Leæther Strip, X Marks the Pedwalk and Armageddon Dildos. Torben Schmidt, founder of Infacted Recordings, worked as Zoth Ommog’s label manager from 1995 to 1998. He and Talla launched the Zoth Ommog Classix series together. “Brainstorm” track listing: This Is the Point, Brainstorm, Give Me You, Reaching Out, Energy & Consciousness, Misery, Sacred, Ice Machine (vox version), Serenade (splitter), Subjection (violated), No Tears, Face of a God, Dead Bodies. Menschdefekt’s “Into the Void” arrives 23 October on CD (catalog FACT3483, EAN 4018939613945) in a clear tray jewel box, its first full-length album with vocalist Alex Erbacher. The 14-track, roughly 70-minute record moves between synth pop, dark electro and future pop, and includes two tracks reaching CD for the first time: a cover of Bronski Beat’s “Smalltown Boy” and “Day by Day”, a collaboration with Mark Sousa of Voicecoil, who died earlier in 2026. “Into the Void” will also be released digitally via Bandcamp and on streaming platforms. “Into the Void” track listing: Into the Void, Inside the Machine, Black as Black Can Be, Fragile Existence Part I, Losing Fire, The Book of Life, Reality, This World, Scream in Silence, Smalltown Boy, Oblivion, God, Embrace Your Fate, plus bonus track Day by Day (Album Version feat. Mark Sousa). The Zoth Ommog Classix series also keeps in print earlier Lights Of Euphoria releases “Future Unknown” and “True Life” on vinyl, the “Suicidal” MCD and “Traumatized” CD, plus Menschdefekt‘s “Recombination” CD. About Lights Of Euphoria and Menschdefekt Lights Of Euphoria is a German EBM act that released “Brainstorm” on Zoth Ommog in 1995, one of the label’s catalog titles from its run as a driving force in European electronic music through the 1990s. The album’s Zoth Ommog Classix reissue marks its first-ever appearance on vinyl, 31 years after its original CD release. Menschdefekt build a sound bridging synth pop, dark electro and future pop, marked by clean vocals, trance-inspired synthesizer structures and the band’s spoken-word samples. “Into the Void” is the group’s fifth studio album and its first to feature vocalist Alex Erbacher, presenting a more melodic and accessible side of the band while staying rooted in its electronic origins.

items._cn_summary: 本文为Infacted Recordings厂牌推出的Zoth Ommog Classix黑胶再版系列新闻稿，首批发行涵盖Lights Of Euphoria 1995年首张专辑《Brainstorm》灰色限量黑胶首版及Menschdefekt第五张录音室专辑《Into the Void》CD版。《Brainstorm》收录13首曲目，涵盖工业电子与EBM典型结构，是该厂牌推动欧洲电子音乐发展的代表目录之一。《Into the Void》则跨越合成器流行、暗潮电子与未来流行三种风格，包含两首首次以CD形式发行的曲目：Bronski Beat翻唱曲《Smalltown Boy》与已故合作者Mark Sousa参与的《Day by Day》。Menschdefekt以清晰人声搭配迷幻合成器架构和spoken-word采样，形成层次丰富的电子声响。整体内容偏向厂牌资讯与曲目罗列，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论与艺术性分析。

items.body: KN/GHTS, the solo project of James Knights, releases the single “Light The Fuse” on 17 September 2026 via Specchio Uomo. Knights is known as one of the singers of electronic pioneers Boytronic and for his time in Scarlet Soho. “Light The Fuse” combines synth pop, dark disco and Italo-influenced sounds. The track deals with loss, recovery and the moment someone stops looking backward and finds the strength to move forward. The single’s B-side carries a darker remix of “Supernatural Lover” by Berlin-based artist Daniel Knutz, whose own sound draws on darkwave, coldwave, post-punk and minimal electronic music. The official video for “Light The Fuse” was directed and edited by independent filmmaker Dirk Roche. It was filmed during the Supernatural Lover Tour, with additional footage captured at live performances in Germany. “Light The Fuse” follows KN/GHTS’s second studio album, “Supernatural Lover”. Since that release, the project has built momentum internationally, with an audience particularly across Germany, Sweden and Mexico. Its live show has become a central part of the project’s identity, with recent performances alongside Drab Majesty and Andy Bell of Erasure. Light The Fuse by KNIGHT$ “Light The Fuse” is available on Bandcamp and Spotify. About KN/GHTS KN/GHTS is the solo project of James Knights, known for his work across the electronic and alternative music scene as one of the singers of Boytronic and for his time in Scarlet Soho. Under the KN/GHTS name, Knights combines synth pop, dark disco, electronic music and theatrical performance. Following the release of his second studio album, “Supernatural Lover”, KN/GHTS built an international following, particularly across Germany, Sweden and Mexico. Live performances alongside acts including Drab Majesty and Andy Bell of Erasure became a defining part of the project. “Light The Fuse”, released 17 September 2026 via Specchio Uomo, is the project’s newest single, backed with a Daniel Knutz remix of “Supernatural Lover” and an official video shot during and after the Supernatural Lover Tour.

items.body: Mute have shared the newly remastered Coil track “Either His, or Yours”, the third track revealed from “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders),” due on limited-edition vinyl, CD and digitally on 30 October 2026 through Mute and Coil’s own imprint Threshold House. Side-Line covered the reissue’s announcement and its first single, “Cardinal Points,” in July, when Mute and Threshold House confirmed the 30 October release date and the reissue’s catalog number, COIL3. “Either His, or Yours” follows that track and the subsequent “Aqua Regalia” as the reissue’s third pre-release song, and sits at position thirteen on the album’s sixteen-track sequence. “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is the closing album in a trilogy that began with “Scatology” (1984) and “Horse Rotorvator” (1986), drawing on textural and instrumental material sidelined during “Horse Rotorvator’s” sequencing. The reissue restores artwork reconstructed by Stephen Thrower and his partner Ossian Brown (a member of Coil from 1999 to 2004), using archive material that includes artefacts, photographs and personal notes made by the late John Balance, alongside new sleeve notes. It is the first release in a new partnership between Mute and Threshold House that will bring four early Coil albums back into print with restored artwork and previously unseen imagery. Coil’s “Gold is the Metal” release details The album’s full, sixteen-track running order remains “The Last Rites of Spring,” “Paradisiac,” “Thump,” “For Us They Will,” “The Broken Wheel,” “Boy in a Suitcase,” “Golden Hole,” “Cardinal Points,” “Red Slur,” “…Of Free Enterprise,” “Aqua Regalia,” “Metal in the Head,” “Either His, or Yours,” “Chickenskin,” “Soundtrap” and “The First Five Minutes after Violent Death,” all carrying the 2026 remaster. Mute and Threshold House plan to follow “Gold is the Metal” with further early Coil reissues: the soundtrack for Derek Jarman’s “The Angelic Conversation,” the previously unreleased music Coil recorded for Clive Barker’s “Hellraiser,” and the compilation “Unnatural History.” About Coil Coil formed in London in 1982 as a solo project of John Balance (born Geoffrey Burton, 1962-2004), then a member of Psychic TV. The project became a duo when Balance’s partner Peter Christopherson (1955-2010), formerly of Throbbing Gristle, joined him. Coil’s first release, the one-sided 12″ single “How to Destroy Angels,” came out in 1984. Stephen Thrower joined the group during the recording of “Horse Rotorvator” (1986) and remained through “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” (1987), the third and closing album of a trilogy that also included “Scatology” (1984). Coil released music through the 1990s and 2000s that ranged from the industrial dance of “Windowpane” to the ambient “Time Machines” (1998) and the two-volume “Musick to Play in the Dark.” John Balance died in 2004 after a fall at the band’s home, and Coil effectively ended; Peter Christopherson continued to oversee reissues of the group’s catalog until his own death in 2010. In July 2026, Mute and Threshold House announced the “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” reissue for 30 October, along with its first single, “Cardinal Points,” followed by a second track, “Aqua Regalia.” “Either His, or Yours” is the third song to surface ahead of that release date.

items._cn_summary: 本文并非乐评，而是关于Coil专辑《Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)》再版发行的新闻稿。文章介绍了Mute与Threshold House合作重新发行Coil早期四张专辑的计划，该专辑原为1987年作品，作为三联曲的收尾之作，汇集了《Horse Rotorvator》创作期间被搁置的素材。再版由Stephen Thrower与Ossian Brown使用John Balance的档案材料重建封面与内页设计，包含照片与个人笔记等罕见素材。文中还列出了十六首曲目的完整曲目顺序，并预告后续将发行Derek Jarman电影配乐、《Hellraiser》未发表配乐及合辑《Unnatural History》的再版。作为英国工业与暗潮领域的标志性项目，Coil融合仪式音乐、实验电子与后朋克的声响探索对地下音乐影响深远，但本文未提供任何对音乐本身的分析或评价。

The project describes its sound as combining “Industrial
items.body: Aggrotech and dark electro project Subliminal Code released an official video for “Behind the Mask“, the title track from the single issued through Neon Retro Records on July 31, 2026. Side-Line covered the single’s five-track remix package when a People Theatre remix, an Elektroterapi remix, a club version and a Dominator remix were added on August 16; the video now gives the title track its own visual counterpart. The project describes its sound as combining “Industrial, Aggrotech, Dark Electro, EBM and Hard Techno”, and says “Behind the Mask” continues that direction with “a cinematic visual concept inspired by classic psychological horror and 80s slasher cinema.” Behind the Mask by Subliminal Code About Subliminal Code Subliminal Code was founded at the start of 2010 by Raul Jose Padron and Raul Junior Padron, drawing on EBM, industrial, metal and synthpop; the twin brothers trace their roots to Venezuela, with the project now based between Venezuela and Hungary. Side-Line has followed the project’s chronology from the “Malevolencia” single in 2020 through the “The Cancer Of The World Is Human Beings” album in 2021 and on to the “Behind the Mask” single and its remix package this year. “Behind the Mask” is the first Subliminal Code release to carry Neon Retro Records, and the new video is its first official visual.

items._cn_summary: Subliminal Code 由委内瑞拉的双胞胎兄弟于2010年创立，项目现扎根于委内瑞拉与匈牙利两地。他们的作品横跨工业、激进电子、暗潮电子、EBM与硬核 techno 多个领域，风格凶猛且节奏驱动明显。最新单曲《Behind the Mask》延续了这一混合路线，并搭配了五轨混音版本，收录 People Theatre、Elektroterapi、Dominator 等不同制作人的重混音。官方 MV 以经典心理恐怖与八十年代砍杀电影为视觉灵感，营造出影院化的暗黑叙事氛围。这是该组合首度与 Neon Retro Records 合作发行的作品，也是其首支拥有官方影像呈现的曲目。从地域角度看，拉丁美洲与中东欧背景为项目带来一定的跨文化视角，但在声音设计与类型融合上的创新幅度仍有待更多作品验证。

The EP holds “Rezorpt Into The Frequency” and “TR-3B”; ZoZo wrote, performed and produced it, and Beau Thomas mastered it. The video follows the activity of an alleged secret government aircraft rumored to have existed since the 1990s, staging a surreal abduction across shifting experiments and hallucinatory ima
items.body: Electronic duo ZoZo released the two-track EP “TR-3B” on September 15, 2026, together with a music video for the title track directed by John Mannion. The EP holds “Rezorpt Into The Frequency” and “TR-3B”; ZoZo wrote, performed and produced it, and Beau Thomas mastered it. The video follows the activity of an alleged secret government aircraft rumored to have existed since the 1990s, staging a surreal abduction across shifting experiments and hallucinatory imagery that touches on hidden knowledge, extraterrestrial contact and dimensional timeline shifts. The duo describes the EP itself as “a result of many years of research into the realms of the paranormal, metaphysics, unexplained phenomena, and ET contact”, built from fluid passages, splintered rhythms and futuristic imagery. TR-3B by ZoZo About ZoZo ZoZo is the duo of Zoe Wardlaw and John Mannion, who started the project in New York City in 2016 and are now based in the Mojave Desert. Both members have backgrounds as classically trained performers and in the noise and experimental underground, which they carry into a vocal-driven electronic sound built on complex rhythms, processed vocals and unconventional song structures. The project’s debut single “Faceshuttle”, made with Bayley Sweitzer, appeared on December 4, 2020, ahead of the debut EP “Simulations of Self” on January 14, 2021; the single “Blood-Brain Barrier” followed in 2022. ZoZo’s work has been covered by Sermon 3 Recordings, The Wire, Ears to Feed and A Closer Listen. “TR-3B” is the project’s first release since “Simulations of Self”.
items._cn_summary: ZoZo 是由 Zoe Wardlaw 与 John Mannion 组成的电子二人组，2025年9月发行两曲EP《TR-3B》，标题曲同步推出由 Mannion 执导的音乐录影带。EP 以传说中自1990年代起流传的政府秘密飞行器TR-3B为核心视觉意象，通过超现实的外星劫持场景、幻觉画面与维度时间线偏移等概念构建叙事。二人将多年对超自然、形而上学与不明现象的研究融入创作，采用流动性段落、断裂节奏与未来主义音色堆叠，配合经过深度处理的人声与非常规歌曲结构。作品延续了二人古典科班背景与噪音/实验地下场景的交叉脉络，是自2021年EP《Simulations of Self》之后的首度新作。整体呈现出概念驱动的实验电子路径，融合噪音根源与暗潮工业质感，文本层面信息以新闻发布为主，缺乏对声音细节的深入评述。

items.album: Watch Video for “Neighborhood”
items.artist: LA New Wave Artist NYIKO Searches for Meaning and Connection in the Modern World on Second LP “Fate”
items.excerpt: A moment in adulthood arrives, sooner or later, when your childhood neighborhood starts looking like a movie set built from memory: the curb seems smaller, the houses fake, the corner store guilty. items.body: A moment in adulthood arrives, sooner or later, when your childhood neighborhood starts looking like a movie set built from memory: the curb seems smaller, the houses fake, the corner store guilty. NYIKO’s Neighborhood lives in that unnerving dislocation, where leaving home turns out to be less dramatic than realizing another place has become home while life made other plans. The song has the good sense to keep its hands off the panic button, though. Guitars jangle with a tone that brings Echo and the Bunnymen to mind, while NYIKO sings with a wounded restraint that brushes against The Smiths and Choir Boy. The arrangement gives the melody room to wander, lets the bass and drums hold their ground, and trusts the ache in the vocal to do more work than production could. NYIKO has moved through hip hop, piano songwriting, emo, hardcore, and electronic music, and you can hear the benefit of that restlessness in the way Neighborhood sidesteps purity tests. The song feels pop-minded without becoming smug about hooks, emotionally direct without begging for sympathy. Somewhere in its DNA sits the plainspoken intelligence of Magnetic Fields and Divine Comedy, that knack for taking a condition and phrasing it as though you overheard the right sentence at the wrong time. Directed and edited by Sabrina Gimenez, the video for Neighborhood follows people moving separately through a residential area before their bodies begin slipping into rhythmic glitches. A twitch here, a repeated gesture there, then these isolated figures start syncing up, as if the neighborhood itself has found a tempo and decided everybody ought to obey it. At golden hour, they converge in a brief group movement before the pattern breaks apart. Everybody disperses, except one person who keeps going. NYIKO, who produced and choreographed the video, turns belonging into something halfway between comfort and contagion. Community looks beautiful for a second, then faintly sinister once you notice how easily individual behavior can fall into step. Watch Neighborhood below: That idea runs straight into Fate, NYIKO’s sophomore album, released September 16 through Trailing Twelve Records. Across ten songs, he considers desire, identity, attachment, politics, memory, and the unseen systems nudging people toward choices they swear are entirely their own. “I wanted to write an album about the invisible forces that shape our lives,” says NYIKO. “Whether it’s the internet, politics, nostalgia, celebrity culture, or our own attachment patterns, we spend so much time believing we’re making independent choices without realizing how much we’re being pulled by things outside ourselves. Every song asks the same question from a different angle: how much of our lives is fate, and how much is choice?” Opening track O Primate sets chiming synthesizers against jangling guitars, its wavering electronic tones giving the brighter riffs an agreeable instability. Warm bass anchors NYIKO’s phrasing, which has something of The Smiths’ conversational elasticity: a melody that seems to discover its own argument as the sentence unfolds. Beneath that inviting surface sits a consideration of animal rights, human power, and the ease with which cruelty becomes ordinary. When clipped, piano-like keyboard notes enter midway through, they sharpen the arrangement without disturbing its composure. His measured delivery gives the subject room, keeping the listener close enough to sit with an uncomfortable question. On Stay Young, hazy synthesizers and a gentle bass figure make way for a new wave vocal over unhurried drums. Its wish to suspend youth carries the knowledge that adulthood keeps changing the people and places we count on. As the bass grows fuller, guitars broaden into the generous shapes of 1980s pop-rock, with vocal harmonies adding lift. There is an appealing ease to the way these parts gather around the melody, each arrival making the song feel a little more expansive. For a few minutes, NYIKO makes holding on sound effortless, even as the title betrays how much effort might be involved. The piano-led opening of camgirl brings Corey Hart’s earnest new wave balladry to mind, with soft vocals and small harmony accents lending the first stretch an almost private scale. Inspired by the psychological thriller Cam, the song follows a lonely fan who mistakes a sex worker’s paid attention for a romance. NYIKO lets us hear the tenderness that makes the misunderstanding persuasive to the person having it. Midway through, a funkier bass line, firmer drums, and more expressive guitars enlarge the arrangement, carrying his fantasy toward the proportions of a grand declaration. The musical uplift makes his certainty feel alarmingly easy to share. Sugar brings a cooler, more physical tension, somewhere between Mareux’s controlled darkwave and Provoker’s bruised intimacy. Angular guitars interrupt the synth swells, while a substantial bass line gives the track weight and a certain weary grace. The album’s notes place it within the complexities of loving someone who works in the sex industry; desire, emotional distance, and control all bear on the relationship. NYIKO’s delivery catches that difficult balance between wanting another person and recognising how much of yourself you are surrendering to the arrangement. The rhythm keeps moving with an assurance the relationship seems unable to sustain. “To me, Sugar is about temptation and control,” NYIKO confesses. “It’s what happens when lust overrides logic – when something looks sweet on the surface but rots you from the inside.” Rippling synths introduce SUPERFAN, where a wistful vocal gradually acquires momentum from the drums and bass. Its apparent love song exposes the possessiveness that can turn celebrity admiration into entitlement. Chiming synthesizers and changes in pace give the arrangement a restless shape, repeatedly raising its emotional temperature before allowing it to settle. Those returns to relative calm are especially effective: NYIKO gives the melody enough breathing room for its sweetness to register. At each subsequent swell, the voice seems ready to make an enormous promise, leaving us to wonder who has actually agreed to receive it. An extended guitar melody holds Shelter steady while warm bass and drums establish a more welcoming momentum. Here, the search for home settles on the emotional security another person can offer. NYIKO’s pop-rock delivery has room to open up, and the bright, bubbling synthesizer that introduces the chorus supplies a welcome burst of pleasure. The beat becomes easier to dance to as the song expands, giving its optimism a physical expression. After the fraught attachments of the preceding tracks, that sustained guitar line sounds particularly reassuring, carrying the tune through its changes with an unforced sense of continuity. After Neighborhood, the title track Fate draws the album into darker territory. A compressed synthpop beat gradually comes into focus, revealing a wiry rhythm beneath NYIKO’s smooth delivery. Layered vocal harmonies lend the melody a slightly baroque elegance. The song explores an avoidant relationship, with desire repeatedly renewed by a lover’s retreat. Metallic keyboard tones and sighing synth pads enter around the midpoint, followed later by rippling melodic figures that make the arrangement feel increasingly unsettled. There is something rueful about how gracefully the vocals move through all this activity, as though the pleasure of singing could briefly make the uncertainty bearable. Drifting synthesizers give Victim of No Consequence an airy entrance before a buoyant bass line and gently floating drumbeat take over. NYIKO returns to a Smiths-like cadence, surrounded by jangling acoustic guitar and bright electronic accents. It is among the album’s most immediately memorable songs, with a tune that almost supplies its own invitation to sing along. The lyrics follow two young men drawn toward incompatible realities through pandemic misinformation and conspiracy culture. That inviting arrangement becomes an especially pointed setting: a melody capable of bringing voices together accompanies a song about people losing the ability to agree on what is real. Closing track Summer of Outrage opens out around warm bass, acoustic strumming, and a sustained guitar figure whose long, expressive reach recalls The Chameleons. The riff returns between verses, giving the song a recognizable center as NYIKO’s broad radio-pop vocal and bright synthesizers fill the space around it. Written in August 2020, the song holds the urgency of the Black Lives Matter protests alongside the isolation of lockdown and the exhausting churn of social media. Its public concerns eventually give way to a more personal grief over time apart from friends. A late passage of piano and voice brings that feeling into focus before the closing guitar expansion. The generosity of the melody makes a fitting conclusion to Fate: even after ten songs spent examining what draws people together and pulls them apart, NYIKO can still make connection sound possible. Listen to Fate below, and stream the album here. Follow NYIKO: Instagram TikTok YouTube Facebook Bandcamp The post LA New Wave Artist NYIKO Searches for Meaning and Connection in the Modern World on Second LP “Fate” — Watch Video for “Neighborhood” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items._cn_summary: NYIKO的第二张专辑《Fate》收录十首歌曲，探讨欲望、身份、依恋、政治、记忆以及那些将人推向所谓'自主选择'的无形力量。单曲《Neighborhood》以回响吉他与受伤克制的嗓音为基底，编曲为旋律留出游走空间，低音与鼓点稳住骨架。NYIKO横跨嘻哈、钢琴创作、情绪摇滚、硬核与电子的经历使作品规避流派纯净度测试，听感上偏向流行却不卖弄钩子，情感直接而不乞求同情。MV由NYIKO本人编舞并制作，将社区归属感处理成介于舒适与传染之间的暧昧状态。开篇曲《O Primate》以钟鸣合成器与回响吉他交锋，温暖的贝斯支撑人声流动，电子音色的不稳定感为明亮 riff 增添不安底色。

ルツェルン音楽祭が、セバスティアン・ノルドマン新総裁の企画である「序曲」と題した無料公演で、8月13日に開幕した。公開リハーサルの様相で、リッカルド・シャイー以下ルツェルン祝祭管弦楽団の楽団員は普段着だったが、それがまた親近感を抱かせる。 プログラムも、スティーヴ・ライヒ《ニューヨーク・カウンターポイント》のあとはガーシュウィン《キューバ序曲》、バーンスタイン《ウェスト・サイド・ストーリー》から〈マンボ〉と楽しめるプログラムだったのは、今年のテーマが「アメリカン・ドリーム」だからだ。シャイーはこのところ、これらのレパートリーを各地で披露しているといい、彼の新たな顔が見られる。 続いて会場のルツェルン・カルチャー・コングレスセンター（KKL）前に設置された野外ステージで、ハバナ・リセウム・オーケストラとベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団のホルン奏者、サラ・ウィリスがラテン調のモーツァルトや《カルメン》等、キューバ音楽を奏で、踊り出す聴衆も多くいて、熱いオープニングとなった。 15日は今年のアーティスト・エトワール、アウグスティン・ハーデリヒが登場、クラウス・マケラ指揮の祝祭管とバーバー「ヴァイオリン協奏曲」を研ぎ澄まされた音で奏で、まるでおとぎ話の世界のような共演だった。 2年前にアメリカの永住権も取ったというハーデリヒが愛情を込めて紡ぎ出す音に、マケラが応える様子が室内楽のように精緻だ。アンコールもアーヴィン・T・ラウズ《オレンジ・ブロッサム・スペシャル》で、アメリカンな選曲だった。 後半はストラヴィンスキー《火の鳥》を熱演し、マケラは何度も聴衆に呼び戻された。 8月17日はダニエル・バレンボイムが指揮するウェスト=イースタン・ディヴァン管弦楽団が、ヨーヨー・マとドヴォルジャーク「チェロ協奏曲」で匠の共演を聴かせた。後半はシューマン「交響曲第3番《ライン》」で若々しさも見せた。 8月23日にはコンポーザー・セミナーが6人の若手作曲家に委嘱した作品を、6曲一斉に世界初演した。このセミナーはピエール・ブーレーズが始めた現代曲アカデミーを基礎に、2016年にヴォルフガング・リームが立ち上げたもので、今年は4人の若手指揮者も招かれた。 作曲家同席の下、今年も110人が参加するルツェルン祝祭現代管弦楽団と創り上げた音が、歓びに満ちて生まれ出た。今年は日本人の参加者も多く、ヴァイオリンの伊勢宥奈、ヴィオラの布施海里、チェロの蕨野真美、フルートの矢島雄太郎、テューバの山本蒼太、ピアノの船橋佑花らが生き生きと演奏。日本の音楽界を支えていく次世代が、世界の現代音楽の第一線を学ぶ姿に頼もしさを感じた。 チェチーリア・バルトリの、涙を誘う《オルフェオとエウリディーチェ》 観客の拍手に応えるチェチーリア・バルトリ。今年還暦（60歳）を迎えた© Peter Fischli / Lucerne Festival 夜には当音楽祭の人気者、チェチーリア・バルトリがグルック《オルフェオとエウリディーチェ》で聴衆を喜ばせた。このプロダクションは、ザルツブルクからウィーンを回り、以前はチューリヒ・トーンハレでも見たが、その時よりも音楽的により深くなっていた。 暗くなった舞台にエウリディーチェ役のメリッサ・プティ（アモーレ役も兼任）が横たわり、蝋燭のような灯りを持ったモンテカルロ歌劇場合唱団が登場するだけで舞台装置ができあがる。そして彼らの歌により情景が描かれるため、字幕は必須、とバルトリは語る。 今年還暦を迎えた彼女はKKLを満たすほどの声量はないが、代わりに弱声はどんどん研ぎ澄まされ、涙を誘う。それに、ジャンルカ・カプアーノが指揮するピリオド楽器オーケストラ「モナコ公の音楽家たち」がそっと寄り添う。今回は歌詞を歌わずに叫ぶような部分も複数見られ、魂の震えを歌っていると実感させた。 有名なオルフェオのアリア〈エウリディーチェを失って〉は、いつもバルトリは超速で歌うのが残念なのだが、今回は繰り返し部分でしっとりと絶望感を表現したため、ここでも涙が込み上げる。 終演後、楽屋へ行くと、バルトリの御母堂も涙を溜めており、バルトリも「ほんとうに良い音楽」といって、まるでオルフェオとエウリディーチェの葬送に参列した人のようだった。この音楽的共感力が好演の理由だろう。
