items.body: Label: P&M Records, 2026 Personnel - Michael Blake: tenor and soprano saxophone; Gary Versace: piano; Ben Allison: bass; Michael Sarin: drums. Canadian-born, New York-based saxophonist and composer Michael Blake gathers a quartet of longtime collaborators for a slightly unsettling jazz session centered on Halloween, a holiday of imagination and transformation built around costumes, community, and the unexpected. Joining Blake here are pianist Gary Versace, bassist Ben Allison, and drummer Michael Sarin—all of whom have played and recorded with the saxophonist in various musical contexts. All nine compositions on the album are covers associated with Halloween, with the exception of the last track, Blake's " The Creep ", a shape-shifter showing many faces in minor mode with a bluesy feel. The opener, " Halloween ", slides in with mystery-induced suspense, leading to an atmospheric crescendo dreamily texturized by jagged piano chords in the high register. It keeps us engaged and alert as it moves forward in a fluid 5/4 time signature, strengthened by Blake's command of phrase and tone—he offers a haunting improvisation delivered with pure instinct and multiphonic impact. " Stalking Monster " and " Anatomy of a Murder " are Duke Ellington compositions, the former from Night Creature and the latter from Otto Preminger's film of the same name. " Stalking Monster " features tonally contrasting piano playing over hi-hat pulsation, creating eerie undertones before morphing into a 4/4 swing in the best that jazz tradition has to offer. An empowering feeling comes from the soloists: Blake is soulfully articulate while Versace introduces rich motivic ideas. This continuous fluidity, without straining to make a point, carries over to " Anatomy of a Murder ", a blues where bass and piano start in tandem, filling the lower register with gorgeous groove. The gears shift considerably on " The Great Pumpkin Waltz "—Vince Guaraldi's tune from the 1966 Halloween television special It's The Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown —here delivered with harmonic sophistication and passionate lyricism. On soprano saxophone, Blake exudes clarity of technique and natural phrasing, switching to tenor on the following tune, " Transylvanian Lullaby ", the main haunting theme from Mel Brooks's 1974 comedy Young Frankenstein . Allison and Sarin build tension at the outset, and the piece becomes gently brushed after brief, well-devised staccato moves. The rhythm section compellingly swings in support of Blake's nimble solo. There's also a slow, rubato rendition of " Witchcraft ", Cy Coleman's tune popularized by Frank Sinatra and the Bill Evans Trio, where brooding melodicism comes to the fore. The chemistry between Blake and his rhythm team is undeniable throughout, even when the energy dips a bit after the first couple of tracks. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Halloween ► 02 - Stalking Monster ► 04 - Transylvanian Lullaby

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以万圣节为主题，萨克斯手 Michael Blake 召集长期合作的钢琴、贝斯与鼓手组成四重奏，将九首与万圣节相关的经典曲目重新演绎，包括 Ellington 的《Stalking Monster》与《Anatomy of a Murder》、Guaraldi 的《The Great Pumpkin Waltz》、Mel Brooks 电影主题曲《Transylvanian Lullaby》以及 Sinatra 翻唱的《Witchcraft》，外加 Blake 原创的《The Creep》收尾。编曲上融合 5/4 拍、慢速 rubato、华尔兹等多种节拍形态，乐器编制以原声爵士为核心，强调旋律重塑与氛围营造，钢琴的高音区棱角和弦与低音区的律动交替推进，萨克斯在高音与中音之间切换以贴合曲目情绪。整体呈现的是主题鲜明的原声爵士合奏，虽带有一定的实验编曲意识，但风格仍扎根于传统爵士语汇之内，对于偏好学院派即兴与前卫爵士的听众而言，跨界融合的深度有限。

items._cn_summary: 本文为Touching Extremes近期发布的两张实验音乐唱片合辑式介绍。第一张专辑由Eamon Sprod创作，将四年来在被忽视的室内空间与城市基础设施中采集的录音素材汇编为两部声音学组曲，属于典型的具体音乐与场域录音美学范畴。第二张专辑由Robert Piotrowicz创作，运用合成器、非对称节拍、微分音变化，并融合对东欧舞曲传统的想象重构，在六首电子作品中探索非西方音乐语汇与电子手法的对话。两张专辑均来自独立小厂牌，制作思路偏向声音艺术与装置化聆听。原文为乐评转载摘要，篇幅较短，对作品细节描述有限，但所涉及的音乐方向与听众关注的实验电子、声学艺术领域高度契合。

items.body: The album was originally released during the formative years of Kompakt's long-running Pop Ambient series Photo by David Westlake Markus Guentner's ambient and dub techno classic LP In Moll is being reissued to mark its 25th anniversary. The record has been newly remastered by composer and mastering engineer Rafael Anton Irisarri for its new edition. Markus showed me entirely new possibilities for what electronic music could communicate." The updated release takes in fresh visual elements created by Guentner himself as he revisited the album 25 years on, while the track 'In Moll 4' will appear on vinyl for the first time as part of... items._cn_summary: Markus Guentner的专辑《In Moll》发行于Kompakt厂牌Pop Ambient系列早期，融合氛围音乐与dub techno的质感。这张作品在2011年由Kompakt发行，25周年再版经过Rafael Anton Irisarri重新母带处理。Guentner亲自为新版创作了视觉元素，其中曲目'In Moll 4'首次以黑胶形式发行。Irisarri在采访中表示，这张专辑曾为他打开了一扇通往未知电子音乐世界的门，展示了电子音乐表达情感的可能性。作为Kompakt早期Pop Ambient美学的代表作品，它以沉稳的音色层次和空间感氛围成为该系列里程碑之一，再版让更多听众得以接触这一经典。

items._cn_summary: 本文是对英国实验电子乐队 Globo 的访谈报道。乐队于1993年在诺里奇成立，首张专辑《Pro War》于1995年发行，仅使用 Akai 采样器、鼓机和成员的个人智慧创作。他们从未真正融入当时的音乐场景，既不同于 Underworld 之类的电子组合，也与伦敦为中心的英伦摇滚潮流背道而驰。乐队的核心成员包括曾任《Melody Maker》记者的 Mark Wernham（笔名 Mark Roland）、插画师 Steve Appleton、电影制作人 Paul Thompson 以及前成员 Ian McGregor。文章提及他们近期翻唱了 The Fall 的整张专辑，展现了对后朋克经典与电子实验融合的探索。作为一篇访谈，内容偏向人物背景介绍而非音乐深度分析，信息量有限。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Over its near-20 years of existence, Utah's Rylee McDonald has seen his high school musical project turn into a kind of family affair, now adding his partner and wife and their two children to the mix. Still, the Rush- and Led Zeppelin-inspired artist has emerged as his own musical force.1. "In A Lone and Dreary World" (19:03) a djenty low end does not deter this prog extravaganza from taking us on a journey that reminds me of the music of 21st Century projects like LIFESIGNS and NUMEN and even COSMOGRAF and DAVE BRONS . . . (if a little metal edge were applied). Though I am not a fan of this kind of "plastic" drum sound, I very much appreciate the skills and creativity of the performance on the batterie exhibited here by Mike Lofgreen (though it is also mixed into the soundscape as a kind of anomaly of isolated individually-distinguished sterility; that is, the rest of the sounds are given those standard effects we now associate automatically with prog, i.e. reverbs, distortions, gates, sustains, compressions, etc.) Oh! really love the voice of Kristen McDonald. The collective sound of the band's vocal palette reminds me of short-lived band from Naughties, THE REASONING as well as second- and third- album PURE REASON REVOLUTION (2009's Amor Vincit Omnia and 2010's Hammer and Anvil). Paired up with those syncopated djenty guitar chords and we have quite a cool sound and mix. Then you have to take into consideration the common human plight being expressed in the song lyrics: dissatisfaction and distrust of all we've been raised to believe and value, all we've been told--including that coming from parents and family--learning to listen to and trust one's own inner voice and inner truths and beliefs--the awakening to the power of a spiritual perspective (perhaps even a Christian rebirth): "No enemies" and "saved and sound." Though the length taken to deliver the message/story is a bit over-protracted, it is effective and well-rendered with little or no fluff and appropriate nuance and theatrics. Nice work. (36.5/40) 2. "Faiths Window" (5:20) with industrial horn humming in the background a dirty-distorted electric guitar's two-chord strum repeats itself, occasionally moving between subtly different chords as Rylee McDonald sing/talks over the top, turning into singing as the rest of the band's sound cascades into the mix. It's heavy but it's symphonic with the layers of instruments easy to distinguish from each other. In the fourth minute the lyrics are delivered through growl-screams before the McDonald family choir takes over. A metal instrumental passage takes over with searing electric guitar, etc. but then Kristen emerges as the lead vocalist, taking us to the song's (rather sudden) end. (8.875/10)3. "Patience" (4:53) a normal rock sound palette over which Rylee's single male voice leads the way gradually turns heavy metal with the chorus, playing out as such into the final fadeout of electronic keyboards. A solid song but there is nothing very new or innovative here. (8.75/10)4. "Past Life Parable" (5:03) more solid heavy prog steering toward the more sophisticated hair band sounds and music of the 1970s and 1980s, the big difference here is the use of djenty guitar chords and some more-modern sounds as well as an admirable level of sophistication in the construct/composition. (8.875/10)5. "Gravity I" (2:35) nice Spanish acoustic guitar play surrounded by proggy drum 'n' bass and textural synth washes and other keyboard and, eventually, electric guitar effects. Impressive drum play toward the end--just before the transition/bridge to "Gravity II." (4.625/5) 6. "Gravity II" (4:49) bleeding over from the previous "introductory" song, Rylee's voice in the lead position is backed/doubled by Kristen. Nice use of organ bass pedals and harpsichord sound in the third minute, but then we are quickly back into the metal, even djenty music long before the minute's end. I really like the guitar djent-play in this section (as well as the more subdued vocal performance), but then we shift back into hyperdrive with the machine gun bass pedal play for a few bars before cutting out for a near-a cappella passage, but then we nearly as quickly and suddenly find ourselves back in the fray of machine gun beats and rapid-fire beat-down low end guitar chords. Still, I like and respect it overall. (9/10)7. "Animals" (5:34) Rylee's single male voice is singing while only accompanied by lone acoustic guitar picking. After one time through a round of the verse and chorus the keys, bass pedals, and stark drum play join in the now split (R & L) two-acoustic guitar picking foundation. I wish I could pick out who Rylee's voice reminds me of: it's definitely one of STYX's lead vocalists: either Tommy Shaw or Dennis DeYoung. The McDonald family choir is cited for this song but their role is, sadly, rather quiet, minor. Still, this is a pretty cool song--one that only lacks for seriously brainworm melodies. (9.125/10) Total Time 47:17The McDonald family's sound and style cannot help but be compared to the bands mentioned above--especially THE REASONING and early PURE REASON REVOLUTION but also bands like RUSH, STYX, INTROITUS and MEER. From its Led Zeppelin inspiration and Rush fueling and modeling, the band seems to have come into its own: into something that sounds like . . . but is really their own thing--which is really nice.A-/five stars; though this kind of Classic Rock and sophisticated 80s Metal blend of prog is not really among my high preferences, I do appreciate the creative and complex song structures built here as well as the wonderful vocal work rendered by the collective members of the McDonald family (really, Rylee and Kristen).
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是犹他州音乐人Rylee McDonald主导的家庭项目，由其妻子和两个子女共同参与录制，灵感源自Rush和Led Zeppelin等经典乐队。首曲长达近二十分钟，融合了djent金属的低频底鼓与前卫摇滚的宏大叙事，配以女主唱Kristen McDonald的声线，既有金属的重量感也有交响化的层次铺陈。歌词聚焦于对既有信仰体系的怀疑与个体精神觉醒的主题，宗教色彩隐含其中。短曲方面加入了工业嗡鸣、growl-scream死腔与合唱交织的处理手段，键盘收尾增添电子色彩。整体制作在重型与抒情之间寻找平衡，乐评对鼓音色和混音细节有所批评，但对创作真诚度和家庭协作的独特形式给予了肯定。

items.body: Review by Neuroprog — Octobre is one of the first progressive rock albums from Quebec, released in 1973. The wonderful compositions on this album allow Pierre Flynn to showcase his full talent. He is truly one of Quebec's finest singers, a real hidden gem. Overall, the songs are built around powerful and catchy riffs. This is therefore not the most progressive album out there: it does not particularly seek to push musical boundaries or necessarily build toward epic moments. It is instead one of the great Quebec rock albums, with clear influences from the progressive rock movement of the time. It was only after this album that the band would go on to develop and complicate its compositions further. It is unfortunate that this excellent album and band are not nearly as well known as Harmonium, Robert Charlebois, Beau Dommage, Offenbach, Paul Pich�, and others.More specifically, the album features a lot of changes in rhythm despite containing only eight tracks and running for less than 30 minutes. We go from songs like Si on partait, a more straightforward rock song with a frantic pace, to much more nuanced and slower pieces featuring melancholic lyrics sung beautifully by Pierre Flynn. Flynn also shines on several tracks with his expressive organ and piano solos.To fully appreciate this album, it is essential to understand French, and especially "joual", as well as the Quebec specific references of the period. Dans ma ville is a perfect example of a song built around two completely different tempos. You can feel the musical crescendo throughout the verses before everything comes back down for a gentle chorus, conveying the feelings of anger and nostalgia that run through the song. This combination of emotion and rhythm is present throughout the album, reinforcing the power of Flynn's vocals.The closing track, La maudite machine, is an anthem in which the importance of the lyrics takes precedence over the melody. Strangely enough, it is the best-known song on the album, although it is not necessarily the most musically interesting one.4/5

items._cn_summary: 1973年发行的魁北克前卫摇滚专辑，篇幅不长但节奏变化频繁，歌曲在强劲有力的摇滚节奏与缓慢忧郁段落之间不断切换。皮埃尔·弗林的人声是核心亮点，配合管风琴与钢琴独奏呈现出充沛情感，歌词需结合魁北克方言与地域文化背景方能完全领会。专辑并未刻意追求宏大叙事或音乐边界的突破，而是以鲜明的旋律钩子和情绪对比取胜，兼具摇滚的感染力与前卫的细腻编排。作为魁北克早期前卫摇滚的代表之一，其历史价值与艺术质量值得肯定。

items.body: Suzanne Perry, the vocalist of 1990s dream pop duo Love Spirals Downwards, released the three-track EP “There’ll Be No More Promises” on Projekt Records on September 18, 2026. The EP is available as a name-your-price digital release on Bandcamp and through streaming and download platforms, and is described on its release page as dream pop, ethereal and darkwave. Perry recorded the EP with multi-instrumentalist Cris Miller of the solo dream-pop project Silver Screen. The lead and title track, “There’ll Be No More Promises,” is new material; the second track is a re-recording of the Love Spirals Downwards song “Ladonna Dissima,” originally released on the duo’s 1994 debut album “Idylls”; the third is a cover of Danny Elfman’s “Sally’s Song” from “The Nightmare Before Christmas.” Perry describes her songwriting process as “instinctively formed as an escape. I find myself captivated within the experience of honest expressionistic music brought into being from a deep introspective place.” Miller, discussing his approach to the collaboration, says he “pay[s] special attention to detail and pursue[s] a holistic approach: envisioning the entire sound first, allowing free experimentation during the process, knowing the direction of the song will be uncovered.” There’ll Be No More Promises (ep) by Suzanne Perry Perry is scheduled to perform live at Brickbat Mansion in Portland, Oregon, on Saturday, October 24, 2026. About Suzanne Perry Suzanne Perry is the vocalist of Love Spirals Downwards, the dream pop duo she formed with guitarist and producer Ryan Lum in Orange County, California, in the early 1990s. The project released its debut album, “Idylls,” in 1994, followed by “Flux” (1995), “Ardor” (1996) and “Ever” (1999), largely on Projekt Records, building a reputation within the American dream pop and ethereal scenes alongside labels including Projekt Records. Love Spirals Downwards has been inactive as a group for extended periods since, with Perry periodically re-emerging with new recordings. “There’ll Be No More Promises,” released September 18, 2026, reunites Perry with Projekt Records and pairs her with Cris Miller of Silver Screen. Alongside the new title track, the EP revisits Love Spirals Downwards’ own catalogue with a redesigned version of “Ladonna Dissima” and adds a cover of “Sally’s Song,” continuing the ethereal, harmony-driven sound Perry first established three decades ago.
items._cn_summary: Suzanne Perry 是九十年代梦幻流行二人组 Love Spirals Downwards 的主唱，此次发行三曲 EP《There'll Be No More Promises》，由 Projekt Records 于 2026 年 9 月 18 日以自定价数字形式发行。整张作品定位于梦幻流行、以太与暗潮三种气质之间，标题曲为全新原创，第二首是对 1994 年首张专辑《Idylls》中《Ladonna Dissima》的重新录制，第三首翻唱了 Danny Elfman 为《圣诞夜惊魂》所作的《Sally's Song》。制作由 Silver Screen 主创、多乐器演奏者 Cris Miller 操刀，他强调先在脑中构想整体声响再进入自由实验的流程。Perry 自述创作源于本能与逃避，文字表达偏向内心独白而非技巧展示。整体而言是一张延续三十年一贯风格的回归作，重访旧作并补以新曲与翻唱，面向梦幻流行与暗潮场景内的固定受众，融合度有限但氛围连贯。

items.body: Projekt Records releases Norwegian ambient musician Erik Wøllo‘s new album Earthshine on 18 September 2026. The album is available as a Pay What You Can digital release and as a CD limited to 300 copies, packaged in a 4-panel digipak. Earthshine by Erik Wøllo The title refers to earthshine, the sunlight reflected from the earth’s surface that faintly illuminates the part of the moon not directly lit by the sun. Across 20 short tracks that crossfade into one another, “Earthshine” moves through abstract electronic soundscapes built from processed drones and sequencer pulses, alternating between expressive passages and sparser, hushed sections. The CD edition also includes a 21st, gapless version of the full album as a single continuous piece. Wøllo recorded the album to analog 4-track and 8-track tape machines before transferring the material to computer for further arranging and mixing, a return to the recording approach he used in the 1980s. Explaining why he went back to tape for “Earthshine”, Wøllo said: “When the tape is running, something affects me, I descend into myself, realizing music completely in the moment. I wanted to go back to the way of recording I was into in the 1980s, using old analog tape recorders. How would it affect my compositional process? Would it take me in other compositional directions? Compare it to writing a novel with a pencil instead of a computer. The unhurried measured approach was more time-consuming and led me to make different creative choices. It turned out that the music became more fluid and open-ended.” Beyond the Projekt Records Bandcamp page, “Earthshine” is also available through Projekt’s distribution partners deejaydead.de, littleuniversemusic.co.uk and audioglobe.it. About Erik Wøllo Erik Wøllo was born on 6 January 1961 in Hemsedal, Norway. He started playing guitar at age 11 and began his professional career in 1980, touring Norway in jazz, rock and fusion bands before turning to a full-time solo career in 1984, when he built his own studio, Wintergarden. His third album, “Traces” (1985, Cicada Records), marked a turning point toward the guitar-and-synthesizer-based ambient and space music style that has defined his solo work since. Wøllo has released more than 50 solo albums, moving through labels including Origo Sound, Monumental Records and Spotted Peccary Music before settling with Projekt Records, which has issued his work since “Gateway” (2010) and remains his current label. His catalog includes “Silent Currents” (2011), “Different Spaces” (2017), “Recurrence” (2021), “Sojourns” (2022) and “Snow Tides” (2026), among others. He has also released collaborative albums with Steve Roach (“Stream of Thought”, 2009, and “The Road Eternal”, 2011), Michael Stearns (“Convergence”, 2020), Ian Boddy (“Frontiers”, 2012, “Meridian”, 2018, and “Revolve”, 2023), and Byron Metcalf (“Earth Luminous”, 2016), among others. “Revolve”, made with Ian Boddy, won the Schallwelle Award for best ambient album in 2023. Wøllo contributed a rework to Apoptygma Berzerk’s 25th-anniversary album “SDGXXV”, having worked with the band in the studio during the making of their 1993 debut “Soli Deo Gloria”. He has also performed at Chuck van Zyl’s Star’s End “Gatherings” concert series in Philadelphia, alongside artists including Steve Roach and Robert Rich. “Earthshine” extends his ongoing run of releases on Projekt Records into a new recording method rooted in his earliest analog tape work.
items._cn_summary: 挪威氛围音乐人Erik Wøllo新作《Earthshine》收录20首短曲，曲目之间无缝交叉淡入，构建出抽象电子音景，以处理过的持续音和序列器脉冲交替穿梭于表现力段落与稀疏低语章节之间。创作过程回归1980年代的模拟磁带录音方式，使用4轨和8轨开盘机录制后再转入电脑进行编曲与混音，这种慢速权衡的方式影响了作曲选择，使音乐更为流动开放。CD版本额外包含第21首无间隙连贯版本，将整张专辑作为单一连续作品呈现。专辑通过独立厂牌Projekt Records发行，提供数字与限量300张实体两种格式。整体风格延续作者自1985年以来以吉他与合成器为基础的氛围与太空音乐路线。

items.body: Swedish goth pioneers The Bizarre Orkeztra have reissued “Land” as a 2026 remaster, out now through COMEDIA in collaboration with Ambush Records. The track is the first release in a new series of remastered singles drawn from the band’s catalog. “Land” was written by Sonny Jansson and originally released in 1984 as a 12″ single on Ambush Records, the band’s own indie label. The original tracklist, “Land,” “Korridor,” “Justice” and “Travelling Man,” was recorded by Christer Björklund at The Bizarre Orkeztra’s headquarters, with vocals recorded by Jomma Sundström at Gävle Ljudstudio and production by Bob Boxkopf. Copies of the 12″ came with an eight-page comic booklet, “The No! COMIX No.2,” made specifically for the release. For the 2026 edition, the title track has been remastered by Håkan Nilsson, with Richard Solstjärna serving as executive producer and providing the new cover art. The single is available digitally, including on Spotify, with a release date of 16 September 2026. COMEDIA describes the campaign as presenting “carefully selected highlights drawn from the band’s impressive back catalog.” It is not the first time “Land” has reached digital platforms: the track was previously issued as a remastered digital reissue in 2020, at the time as part of a monthly reissue project with a companion schedule that also covered “Visions On The Wall,” “Midnight Show,” “A Beautiful Place,” “Hunger For Pleasure” and “She’s Got.” The 2026 edition relaunches that catalog campaign as a new series of remastered singles. About The Bizarre Orkeztra The Bizarre Orkeztra formed in Gävle, Sweden, in the early 1980s, emerging from the punk rock band PF Commando and the avant-garde post-punk band Modaern Art. The band was among the first goth acts in Sweden. Its original lineup was Sonny Jansson on vocals and guitars, Richard Sandberg on drums and guitar, and Ola Claesson on bass and backing vocals; Håkan Nilsson later joined on synthesizer for the group’s later recordings. “Land” was the band’s debut release under The Bizarre Orkeztra name, following the 1981 recording “Ingen kärlek, Inget hat,” released under the group’s earlier name, Bizarre Sex. Two studio albums followed on Ambush Records: “Visions On The Wall” in 1985 and “A Beautiful Place” in 1987, along with the singles “Midnight Show” in 1986 and “She’s Got” in 1989. The album “Hunger For Pleasures,” released in 1988, featured Joakim Lindgren on saxophone alongside Nilsson’s synthesizer work. The band released three albums and several singles in total before disbanding in the late 1980s. Bass player Ola “Toli” Claesson, who died in 2009, created cover art for several of the band’s albums and singles, including the comic strip made for “Land,” which was handed out to the audience at the band’s first concert in Gävle. COMEDIA’s new remastered singles series revisits that catalog, beginning again with the track that first introduced The Bizarre Orkeztra to record buyers in 1984.
items._cn_summary: 本文报道了瑞典哥特先驱乐队 The Bizarre Orkeztra 于2026年通过 COMEDIA 厂牌重新发行1984年单曲《Land》的2026年新版remaster版本。原文详述了单曲的录制背景、制作人员信息及历史沿革，包括原始12寸单曲附带八页漫画册的特殊发行形式，以及2020年曾进行过的数字化重发项目。文章以事实陈述为主，涵盖了乐队从 PF Commando 和 Modaern Art 等前身乐队演变而来的历史脉络，列出了乐队在 Ambush Records 旗下发行的两张专辑和多张单曲。该报道偏向新闻信息整理，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评析或声音美学方面的探讨。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

Weird and wonderful, it sounds
items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body: Belgian electronica pop act 808 Dot Pop has posted four videos since 14 August 2026, each pairing a track from an ongoing “-ism” naming series with a 20th-century building, ahead of two albums, “Minimalism” and “Maximalism,” due at the end of November 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The most recent, “Collectionism,” was posted on the artist’s official website on 17 September 2026. The four videos “Internationalism (Seagram)” was posted around 28 August 2026 and pairs the track with the Seagram Building in New York, an example of the International Style. The track itself is not available on the video’s own release: it appears exclusively on the various-artists compilation “Sounds From The Matrix 26” and will not be issued elsewhere. “Brutalism (Habitat 67)” followed on 6 September 2026, built around Moshe Safdie’s Habitat 67 in Montreal. The visual is as a digital reinterpretation of the building via “The Hillside Project” by NeoScape, rather than footage of the original structure. “Contextualism (Fallingwater)” was posted on 11 September 2026, pairing the track with Frank Lloyd Wright’s Fallingwater house. The version of “Contextualism” heard in this video appears on the “Minimalism” album, while a separate version of the same track, tied to the AT&T Long Lines Building, features on the lead single “Minimalism,” due 26 September 2026. “Collectionism” was posted on 17 September 2026. Unlike the previous three entries in this video 808 Dot Pop gives more info on a few upcoming fan packages. The ‘Minimalism’ and ‘Maximalism’ project 808 Dot Pop announced “Minimalism” (a white-sleeve album) and “Maximalism” (a black-sleeve album) on its website on 14 August 2026, describing them as “two completely different albums in content.” The lead single, “Minimalism,” is scheduled for 26 September 2026. Two further items are tied to the same releases. “Foundationalism,” a six-track EP featuring exclusive versions, is planned as a fan-shop exclusive on an NFC-equipped “phygital” card format. A 72-page fan book titled “Essentialism,” covering the architectural sites referenced across the campaign, was announced on 11 September 2026, with further details promised but not yet published as of this writing. A full tracklist and confirmed formats for “Minimalism” and “Maximalism” have not been published. About 808 Dot Pop 808 Dot Pop is the solo electronica pop project of Belgian musician Passenger S, also known for his work in Metroland. Side-Line reported his debut under the 808 Dot Pop name on 27 March 2020, in “Metroland’s Passenger S launches debut album under 808 DOT POP moniker”, ahead of the album “The Colour Temperature,” released on download and CD on 5 June 2020 on Alfa Matrix. Further singles followed the same year: “Incandescent,” the second single from “The Colour Temperature,” on 19 June 2020; a tribute cover of D.A.F.’s “El Que” for Alfa Matrix’s “Wir Sind DAF” compilation, released 2 October 2020; and “Kelvin (4200),” the third and final single from the debut album, on 13 November 2020, alongside a bundled triple 7-inch vinyl set covered by Side-Line in “Electro pop act 808 Dot Pop releases triple 7 inch vinyl singles in one bundle + 2 new download only singles” (6 November 2020). Side-Line also ran a ‘Click Interview’ with 808 Dot Pop in July 2020. The project continued with the “Ultraviolet” single campaign (February 2021) ahead of the album “The Cubic Temperature,” the “SunCatcher” EP (early March 2022) and a single dedicated to Guglielmo Marconi (January 2023), the latter featuring lyrics by Gary Hunter (Kraftman) and vocals by Lis Van Den Akker. Side-Line covered the act’s return with three simultaneous albums plus two EPs in “Belgian electronica act 808 Dot Pop back with 3 albums in one go + 2 singles” (27 March 2023) and a further double-EP release in “Electronica pop act 808 DOT POP returns with double EP” (5 June 2023). Most recently, fellow Alfa Matrix artist Cubic issued a rework album built on 808 Dot Pop material, covered by Side-Line in “Cubic drops 808 Dot Pop rework album ‘Back To 808’ on Alfa Matrix” (12 December 2025). The four-video architecture series and the wider “Minimalism”/”Maximalism” campaign mark the act’s first new album cycle since 2023.

items.body: UK synthpop and dark disco project KN/GHTS released the single “Light The Fuse” on 17 September 2026 via Specchio Uomo. The B-side carries a remix of “Supernatural Lover”, from KN/GHTS’s second studio album of the same name, by Berlin-based artist Daniel Knutz. Light The Fuse by KN/GHTS Specchio Uomo describes “Light The Fuse” as a pulsating and emotionally charged song about loss, recovery and finding yourself again. The track mixes synth pop, dark disco and italo disco elements with classic synth sounds. Daniel Knutz, whose own work draws on darkwave, coldwave, post-punk and minimal electronic, reworks “Supernatural Lover” as the release’s second track. An official video for “Light The Fuse” is out now, directed and edited by independent filmmaker Dirk Roche. It was filmed during the “Supernatural Lover Tour”, with additional footage from KN/GHTS’s live performances in Germany. About KN/GHTS KN/GHTS is the solo project of UK vocalist and songwriter James Knights, previously a singer of electronic pioneers Boytronic and known from his time in Scarlet Soho. Knights launched the project under the name Knight$, releasing the EPs “What’s Your Poison?” (2016) and “Alligator” (2017) before his debut album “Dollar$ & Cent$” came out on Cargo Records in 2019. Side-Line spoke to him about that album in a 2019 interview, in which he described the project as a faster-moving continuation of the sound he built with Scarlet Soho and Boytronic. The project later restyled its name as KN/GHTS and released its second studio album, “Supernatural Lover”, building an audience particularly in Germany, Sweden and Mexico. KN/GHTS combines synth pop, dark disco, electronic music and theatrical performance, and has performed live alongside Drab Majesty and Andy Bell of Erasure. “Light The Fuse”, released via Specchio Uomo, continues the project’s work following the “Supernatural Lover” album and tour.

items.body: Charlotte, North Carolina synthpop project Midniter, the solo vehicle of Nic Pugh, released the single and video “I Could Love You” on September 15, 2026, via Bandcamp and YouTube. It is the fourth and final promotional single ahead of Midniter’s debut album, “Xeno”, due October 27 on SugarTank! Records, the Charlotte label Pugh co-founded. The release coincides with the opening of vinyl LP pre-orders for “Xeno” through the label’s own store. Midniter describes “I Could Love You” as a ballad about unrequited love Pugh traced the song back to an unfinished piano piece: “‘I Could Love You’ came from an old piano tune that I never finished. The bookends of the song are directly from that idea, with the middle evolving into a more synthpop direction for Midniter. To me, it’s a pretty standard ballad about unrequited love – a tale as old as time that everyone can understand.” I Could Love You by Midniter The video for “I Could Love You” favors mood over narrative Pugh said the video leaves its meaning open: “The video is more ambiguous, playing with the question, ‘Is this about desire, obsession, or both?’ It’s ultimately your call to make. Our goal with this video was to focus more on mood than narrative. It was more important to live in these feelings of distance and longing than explain why they linger. The dancers, our friends from Baran Dance, were instrumental in carrying those moods throughout the video with their choreography. Our main actress Dustie Bayer was also incredible in her debut.” Paul Jahn of Yawn Productions filmed and edited the video, co-directing it with Pugh. Choreography comes from Baran Dance members Audrey Baran, Faith Centa and Donovan Granville, with Dustie Bayer in the lead acting role. For the silhouette performance scenes, Midniter expands to a trio with Joe Boyland and Dan Hitzelberger joining Pugh. Filming took place at Petra’s, the Charlotte venue where Pugh works and where Midniter’s 2025 debut single video, “Shoot the Moon”, was also shot, alongside a University of North Carolina dance studio and locations around Charlotte. About Midniter Midniter is the solo indie-electronic project of Charlotte, North Carolina musician Nic Pugh, launched in 2024 after roughly two decades in punk and rock’n’roll bands, including Paint Fumes and Jaggermouth. As Midniter, Pugh mixes synthpop songwriting with indie-electronic production, citing Radiohead, Justice, The Knife, LCD Soundsystem, Aphex Twin, Squarepusher and M83 as reference points alongside an “Indie Sleaze” visual style. Pugh co-founded Charlotte label SugarTank! Records with fellow musician Nic Holman; the label supports LGBTQ+ artists and allies. Midniter’s debut single, “Shoot the Moon”, arrived with a video shot at Petra’s in 2025, and Side-Line covered the project’s “Alarmist” video single that October. “I Could Love You” is the fourth and last of the promotional singles released ahead of Midniter’s debut album, “Xeno”, due October 27 on SugarTank! Records, with vinyl LP pre-orders now open through the label.

items.body: Los Angeles club Das Bunker marks its 30th anniversary this October with three events: a Catch One show headlined by Combichrist on October 2, a Nine Inch Nails-themed boat cruise called Nine Inch Sails on October 10, and a Halloween dance party on October 31. Combichrist headlines Das Bunker’s 30th anniversary at Catch One Combichrist returns to Das Bunker for the first time since 2009 to headline the club’s official 30th anniversary show at Catch One on October 2. The set draws on the band’s first three albums, “The Joy of Gunz” (2003), “Everybody Hates You” (2005) and “What The Fuck Is Wrong With You People?” (2007). Richmond, Virginia’s The Treasury, whose sound mixes EBM, synth-punk, post-punk and 1990s techno, opens. Das Bunker resident DJs Mimi Cry, IHX, Franck H Bomb and The Operative play the rest of the 21+ night, which runs from 9pm to 3am. A Nine Inch Nails boat cruise and a Halloween party close out the month On October 10, Nine Inch Sails departs from Long Beach, California, the port city where Das Bunker started as a club. Das Bunker offshoot 90s Goth Klub and Depeche Boat present the 21+, three-hour, two-room cruise: DJ Bractune plays Nine Inch Nails on the outdoor deck while DJ Eser covers goth, darkwave and new wave on the second room. The anniversary month closes on October 31 with a Halloween party at Catch One, presented by 90s Goth Klub and Body Rhythm across two rooms of goth, darkwave and new wave. DJs J Bractune, Rev.John and Angel Tears play the 21+ event. About Das Bunker Das Bunker was founded in Long Beach, California on October 22, 1996, to spotlight industrial and related genres that other Los Angeles clubs overlooked before relocating its regular night to Catch One. Over three decades the club has hosted Front 242 and other established industrial and EBM acts alongside emerging names, and has run recurring nights including History of Industrial, Summer Massive and Das Bunker Star Wars Night. Its coverage has included the Los Angeles Times, Vice and Post Punk. Side-Line covered Das Bunker’s 29th anniversary last October, when Unter Null headlined at Catch One. This year’s 30th anniversary run adds Combichrist, a Nine Inch Nails cruise and a Halloween party to that annual tradition.

items.body: At sundown, even a familiar landscape can begin to feel strange, its ordinary landmarks suggesting places you might once have visited in a dream. On Western, The Church gives that feeling an easy, unhurried shape. A shuffling drumbeat keeps moving with quiet resolve while gentle guitar chimes and a bed of breezy synths suggest the tall shadows cast by the last light spreading across the desert. Beneath them, the bass holds a deep, rounded groove, giving Steve Kilbey room to sing with the calm of someone who has already heard every objection. Recorded in Austin, Texas, Western offers another look at Lacuna, the Australian band’s 28th album, due October 30, 2026 via Cooking Vinyl. The 17-track record follows their recent singles-celebrating world tour, with this latest release picking up after Sacred Echoes Part II. Kilbey’s matter-of-fact yet nostalgic delivery gives the song its peculiar comfort. You could picture him singing from the corner of a dim saloon, entertaining a few gamblers with a story whose details become stranger with each telling. His voice carries a trace of resignation and a dry amusement, taking each improbable turn in stride. Around him, the guitars leave space for the rhythm to breathe, their wistful and twangy post-punk melodies carrying a dusky bittersweetness that seems perfectly at ease with itself. The lyrics seem to wander from men rolling dice to strange encounters, glimpses of another world, and eventually outer space. Those abrupt changes of scene suit the music’s steady momentum, with Kilbey following each detour as casually as he might describe the route home. Across three minutes, Western makes a rambling, faintly dangerous adventure feel as easy as watching the sun go down. “Well, we were in Texas, weren’t we?” laughs Kilbey. “As a kid, all there was on TV were Westerns, so I let it all soak in and this is what came out. Some nice six-string bass counter riffs going, and the song is basically a shaggy dog story that just jumps all over the place… breezy and uncomplicated.” Listen to Western below: Formed in 1980, The Church have spent 46 years exploring the meeting points of post-punk, psychedelia, and dream pop, with songs including The Unguarded Moment, Almost With You, Under the Milky Way, and Reptile marking different stages of that history. Their current six-piece lineup brings Kilbey together with longtime drummer and producer Tim Powles, guitarists Ian Haug and Ashley Naylor, multi-instrumentalist Jeffrey Cain, and newest member, drummer Nicholas Meredith. Lacuna is out October 30, 2026, through Cooking Vinyl. Pre-order the album here. Lacuna tracklist: Lumbini Grove Western Ferrari Sky River Winter Have You Been Here Before The Lemurian Everytime Sky and Hill Paladin Martian Skyline I Want It The Place of Eternal Spring Rapture Forever Lumbini Theme (Slight Return) Sacred Echoes Follow The Church: Website Instagram Facebook The post The Church Rides Again With Their Latest Single “Western” — New Album “Lacuna” Announced! appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: The Church 乐队即将发布第二十八张专辑《Lacuna》，先行单曲《Western》以悠闲的鼓点、轻柔的吉他钟鸣和微风般的合成器铺底，营造出沙漠日落时分的光影氛围。贝斯沉稳的低频律动为主唱 Steve Kilbey 提供了松弛的叙事空间，他用略带怀旧与玩世不恭的口吻，将赌博轶事、外星遭遇等跳跃意象串联成一段散漫的西部公路故事。吉他旋律在感伤与忧郁间游走，带有后朋克的荒凉质感却并不阴冷。整首歌曲仅三分钟便将漂泊、奇遇与黄昏的情绪凝为一体，制作上保持了乐队一贯的成熟稳练，但在实验性与声音创新方面并无显著突破，更偏向于其经典风格的延续与舒适区内的探索。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — The Roaring Waves by Hackett & Rothery sees 2 prog rock guitar legends coming together to create a very enjoyable if slightly tedious instrumental album. No one can take away the impact Steve Hackett & Steve Rothery have on the progressive rock world, with early Genesis & Marillion being a massive influence on the entire modern prog scene since the 70s & 80s, and their monumental playing is always an ace card. But while they bring such talent to these bands, they are the type of guitarists who contribute to a group more than themselves as solo instrumentalists. But the noticeable styles between the 2 are noticeable and they do compliment each other well. The tracks are very well composed and performed, but there isn't too much meat on the bone. It is overall very well mixed too. I'd give this a high 6 to low 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is The Roaring Waves.
items._cn_summary: 前Genesis吉他手Steve Hackett与Marillion吉他手Steve Rothery合作的器乐专辑，两位以乐队身份闻名的吉他手首次以纯器乐形式合作。曲目编制精细、混音优良，两位演奏者的风格差异在作品中形成互补。然而乐评指出，两位吉他手更适合在乐队框架中发挥，作为独奏器乐演奏者时个人特色不够突出，作品整体缺乏足够的深度与厚度，给人一种骨架完整但血肉不足的感觉。推荐曲目为同名曲The Roaring Waves。整体定位偏向怀旧向的前卫吉他合奏，面向老派前卫摇滚乐迷，对追求新声音的听众吸引力有限。

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 987"The Roaring Waves" is a collaborative album by two influential names in the European prog scene, Steve Hackett and Steve Rothery. As we know, Hackett was the main guitarist of Genesis and Rothery is the guitarist of Marillion. As we also know, Marillion was the band most close to Genesis of all British prog bands that appeared in the 80's. So, we can say that Rothery is, somehow, the heir of Hackett on guitars. So, we can not be surprised by this collaborative effort.Although the initial idea emerged around 2015, "The Roaring Waves" took nearly a decade to be written and recorded. The sessions were split between the Racket Club (Marillion's studio) and the home studios of both musicians. The strong connection between both solidified on stage when Rothery joined Hackett at the Royal Albert Hall in 2024 to play "Fly On A Windshield", one of the most famous tracks of the album "The Lamb Lies Down On Broadway" by Genesis.So, "The Roaring Waves" is the first instrumental collaborative project between two of the most iconic guitarists in progressive rock. The album is a profoundly cinematic, atmospheric and a melodic work, entirely inspired by the power, mysteries and nuances of the sea, beautifully paced conversation between two master guitarists. Instead of a flashy "speed trial" or shred-fest competition, the album prioritizes compositional patience, atmospheric depth, and melodic trade-offs. Hackett's angular, classical-tinged and experimental approach, merges seamlessly with Rothery's emotional soaring sustain. Having decided to completely forgo vocals and lyrics, the album gives the listener a true complete imaginative freedom through textures that blend progressive rock, classical music, ambient and electronic textures.The line up on "The Roaring Waves" is Steve Hackett (guitar and harmonica) and Steve Rothery (guitar, bass guitar and keyboards). "The Roaring Waves" also had the participation of Riccardo Romano (keyboards and bass guitar), Daniele Pomo and Leon Parr (drums)."The Storm" is the dramatic opening of the album. It begins by placing the listener in the midst of a storm, with the guitars intertwining to create the tension and force of a storm at sea. This is a beautiful, wild and cinematic piece that delights the listener, a track that serves more as an introduction to the album than in a particularly loud announcement. "Sandsend" is a more restful and contemplative track, where the tension eases, evoking a sense of isolation, a cool beauty and serene atmospheres. It veers a measured rhythm, toward elegant and melancholic atmospheres reminiscent of Pink Floyd, letting the guitars literally sing in unison. At under five minutes, the track is correspondingly compact. "Red Dragon" is the shortest track on the album where Hackett introduces the sitar guitar to give the composition a mystical and an oriental sound. It brings a touch of world music to the otherwise rather watertight soundscape with folkloric influences, bagpipes and sitar sounds. This is a more playful and less polished piece than its predecessors. The title track "The Roaring Waves" is probably the most compelling moment on the album. It begins with a beautiful flourish of classical guitar by Hackett. It's one of the album's highlights, the real swell. Slowly, the swelling dynamics, guitars giving each other space, and precisely that blend of melancholy and pathos for both Steves, a real classic prog moment. "K-129" is one of the most experimental and intriguing tracks on the album. Electronic soundscapes and dark guitars create a very own feeling. Once again, this rhythmic framework is layered over the two guitarists in a largely improvisational style. It stands out paying homage to the "Kosmische Musik" and the Berlin School of the 70's. It reminds me of "Gento", by Bisocope of last year, the project of Rothery and Thorsten Quaeschning of Tangerine Dream. For me, it's one of the strongest tracks on the album. "The Black Sea", described by the authors as a dark adventure, was chosen as the lead single of the album. It's one of the album's great melancholic beauties. Rothery's warm guitar meets Hackett's finely crafted timbres. This is precisely where it becomes clear why this collaboration makes any sense at all. "Pacific Coast Highway" departs from the gray and icy atmosphere of the previous tracks, an unexpected track. Here, the music gains rhythm and movement with Hackett playing harmonica and slide guitar, evoking a high-speed car trip along the sunny California coast. It's a lighthearted, road-movie-esque jam with plenty of vocals at the end of it.Conclusion: "The Roaring Waves" is a dialogue between two musicians who respect and listen to each other, and who have acquired the wisdom of guitarists who have nothing left to prove. It's, therefore, a mature, profound and extremely refined work. "The Roaring Waves" remains above all an album on which two guitarists thankfully dedicate themselves not to themselves, but to the respective piece and its shared concept. Hackett and Rothery harmonize superbly with each other, instead of getting lost in an endless competition for the more spectacular solo. Compared with the album "GTR" of Hackettt and Howe, this is a much better work. I know, those were the 80's. But I don't know if it's an excuse.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)
items._cn_summary: 《The Roaring Waves》是前Genesis吉他手Steve Hackett与Marillion吉他手Steve Rothery的首张纯器乐合作专辑，历时近十年完成。专辑以海洋为整体意象，从风暴的紧张张力展开，依次呈现沉思孤寂的海滨氛围，再到东方色彩的短篇小品。两位吉他手的风格形成互补对话：Hackett带来带有古典色彩和实验棱角的处理，Rothery则以情感丰沛的延音回应。整体制作强调电影感和氛围深度，融合了前卫摇滚、古典元素和环境电子音色，并加入了西塔吉他、口琴等乐器拓宽声景。乐评指出专辑刻意避免了炫技式竞速，更注重作曲耐心和旋律交接，但在声音语言上并未大幅突破传统前卫摇滚的范畴。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Although the Trans-Siberian Orchestra project was already well underway following the success of 1996's "Christmas Eve & Other Stories", Jon Oliva and Savatage still had a lot to offer as a band. Thus, in 1997, the American band released their tenth album, "The Wake of Magellan". A conceptual rock opera inspired by the reflections of an elderly and solitary former sailor, H�ctor Del-Fuego Magellan -a fictional character who claims to be a descendant of the famous Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan- whose story is intertwined with various contemporary events (the 1996 murder of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin for her investigations into drug trafficking, and the stowaways on the freighter Maersk Dubai, whose dramatic fate also unfolded that year).The sound of the sea in the instrumental and cinematic "The Ocean" and the festive, Broadway-esque track "Welcome" set the stage for H�ctor to begin a bitter retrospective on his life, ranging from the despondency reflected in dramatic power ballads like "Turns to Me" or "Morning Sun"-crowned by Al Pitrelli's superb and forceful guitar solos- to the seething helplessness and the decision to end his life out at sea, channeled through corrosive, heavy riffs in the '80s-style "Another Way" or the psychotic "Blackjack Guillotine" and "Paragons of Innocence," tracks that draw on influences spanning a wide spectrum from hard rock to metal.The atmosphere of mounting tension that pervades the album reaches its highest peaks in the progressive track "The Wake of Magellan" -an epic that stands as the album's crowning jewel, built upon the wall of sound created by Johnny Lee Middleton on bass, Jeff Plate on drums, and Oliva on piano, culminating in spirited polyphonic harmonies- and in the stormy instrumental "The Storm," featuring another great solo by Pitrelli. And it is only in the theatrical and epic "The Hourglass" that the conflicted character finally finds solace in redemption and a purpose for his life."The Wake of Magellan" is not only an ambitious rock opera but also one of Savatage's most conceptually rich works.Very good.3.5/4 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / rock opera / hard rock
items._cn_summary: Savatage 1997年概念专辑《The Wake of Magellan》以虚构人物——自称麦哲伦后裔的老水手Héctor Del-Fuego的回忆为主线，将其个人悲剧与1996年爱尔兰记者Veronica Guerin被谋杀、Maersk Dubai号偷渡客事件等真实新闻交织。开篇海洋音效与百老汇式序曲铺设戏剧舞台，随后展开从沉思抒情的力量金属到腐蚀重型riff的多元情绪，Al Pitrelli的吉他独奏贯穿始终。器乐段落'暴风'与同名标题曲构成史诗高潮，复调合唱层叠推进张力，最终在'Hourglass'中完成叙事闭环。整体编曲严谨、概念执行度高，但作为传统前卫金属作品，在声音设计、实验元素和跨类型融合方面对前卫/实验偏好听众而言缺乏足够的突破性。

items._cn_summary: 1962年8月，巴西制作人Aloysio de Oliveira促成了一次具有历史意义的音乐聚会，将Bossa Nova运动的奠基三人组——Antonio Carlos Jobim、Vinícius de Moraes与João Gilberto首次聚集于Au Bon Gourmet。这场为期六周的录音是巴西音乐史上的里程碑事件，记录了Bossa Nova从诞生到成熟的关键时刻。专辑还收录了Os Cariocas的和声与Miles Davis的小号参与，体现了巴西与北美爵士语汇的早期碰撞。作为世界音乐范畴的经典录音档案，其历史价值远大于声音设计的实验性，属于传统Bossa Nova的经典呈现而非先锋探索。

items.body: Fernando’s Eyes releases the single “Room On Fire” on 25 September via Aenaos Records, the project‘s first new material since last year’s album “Center Of Your World” and its accompanying “Bonus Tracks & Remixes”. A video accompanies the release on the same day. You can pre-save the single right now. Fernando’s Eyes is the solo project of Fernando Honorato, singer and co-founder of Stockholm post-punk band Principe Valiente. “Room On Fire” moves with more directness than the atmospheric material on “Center Of Your World”: Honorato produced the track himself, with co-production and mix by Hans Olsson, layering programmed drums against live toms he played personally. A saxophone part by Swedish jazz musician Lina Langendorf cuts through the arrangement without turning ornamental. Honorato describes “Room On Fire” as a song about leaving without looking back, a deliberate choice rather than a loss, with the production’s forward momentum matching that resolve. About Fernando’s Eyes Fernando Honorato is the lead vocalist and primary songwriter of Principe Valiente, the Swedish post-punk and darkwave band he founded in 2005. In 2025, he opened a more personal creative outlet through the solo project Fernando’s Eyes, starting with the single “A Million Times” and followed by the debut album “Center Of Your World”. “Room On Fire” is the project’s first new single since that album.
items._cn_summary: 这是Fernando's Eyes的单曲发布新闻，介绍其2025年9月发行的新单曲《Room On Fire》。Fernando Honorato作为斯德哥尔摩后朋克乐队Principe Valiente的主唱，将其个人项目定位为更具直接性的创作出口。制作上，Honorato本人担任制作人，Hans Olsson负责联合制作与混音，将编程鼓机与他亲自演奏的现场通鼓叠加在一起。瑞典爵士音乐家Lina Langendorf的萨克斯独奏穿透编曲层次，不流于装饰性点缀。Honorato将这首歌描述为关于果断离开而不回望，作品的前进动力与这种意志相呼应。整体来看，这是一篇信息发布性质的内容，侧重于发行背景与制作细节介绍，缺乏对音乐本体更深入的审美分析或评论性洞察。

The session will give an early listen to new music alongside an explanation of the concept behind the upcoming release, though Mesh have not yet detailed what format or title it will take. The duo spent much of 2026 touring behind the album “The Truth Doesn’t Matter”, released on Dependent Records and preceded by the singles “Exile”, “Hey Stranger” and “This World”. The band’s own description of the newly teased material as “unusual” sets it apart from that album cycle, though no release date has been confirmed for it. About Mesh Mesh are the British electronic duo of vocalist Mark Hockings and Richard Silverthorn, active since the mid-1990s and among the longer-running acts in the UK electropop and synth-driven alternative scene. The band’s catalogue includes the 1999 debut “The Point at Which It Falls Apart”, reissued in a 25th-anniversary edition in 2024, through to 2026’s “The Truth Doesn’t Matter” on Dependent Records. Hockings also records as Blackcarburning, releasing the album “Watching Sleepers” and the EP “Divide Us” alongside his work in the band.

items.body: 2026.09.16 海外クラシックNEWS～from ドイツ① 海外のクラシック界のニュースやコンサート、オペラ公演の様子を、現地在住の筆者がいちはやくお届け。今回は、ドイツの8月の音楽シーンから、意欲的なプログラムが展開されたベルリン・ムジークフェストのもようをレポートします。 中村真人 Masato Nakamura 音楽ジャーナリスト、フリーライター 1975年、神奈川県横須賀市生まれ。早稲田大学第一文学部卒業後、2000年よりベルリン在住。著書に『明子のピアノ』（岩波ブックレット）、監修を務めた『おとうさんのポス... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る 音楽シーズンと共に幕を開ける音楽祭、ベルリン・ムジークフェストが今年も始まった。前身のベルリン芸術週間を含めると今回が75回目という節目で、とりわけ意欲的なプログラムが組まれている。8月28日のオープニング公演が、ニコラス・コロン指揮フィンランド放送交響楽団による、リゲティのオペラ《ル・グラン・マカーブル》であることも、その表れといえるだろう。 20世紀後半を代表するオペラだが、ベルリンでは比較的上演の機会に恵まれている。2003年のコーミッシェ・オーパー（バリー・コスキー演出）、2017年のサイモン・ラトル指揮ベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団（ピーター・セラーズ演出）に続き、筆者にとっては3度目の実演となる。 「架空の国ブリューゲルランドの国歌が演奏されますのでご起立ください」とアナウンスされ、実際に聴衆が立ち上がってから鳴り響くのが、12個のクラクションによるけたたましい前奏曲。演奏会形式の上演かと思いきや、歌手は全員インパクトの強い衣裳を身につけ、舞台上演に比べて遜色がない。 客席に配したバンダや合唱、子役を使った秘密政治警察「ゲポポ」の登場など、フィルハーモニーの空間を存分に生かした舞台である。ヴィーナスと「ゲポポ」長官の二役を超絶技巧で歌うソプラノのサラ・アリスティドウを始め、歌手陣は総じてすばらしい。フィンランド放送響も、その精緻で美しい響きを生かした申し分のない演奏を聴かせてくれた。 一方、全体主義政治を生き抜いたリゲティが書いた、非人間性や腐敗をテーマにしたこのオペラが、かつてのような風刺性を持ちにくくなっている実情も感じた。現実の独裁政治や自然災害のほうが、はるかにグロテスクかつ巨大な範囲で私たちを襲い続けているということなのだろう。 ではこうした野心的なプロダクションが意味を失っているのかと言えば、そんなことは決してないはずだ。ロシアと国境を接したフィンランドとの共同制作により、このオペラがフィンランドで初演された数日後にベルリンで上演されたことには意義があった。こうした国際的な連携自体が、時に有効な政治批評性を持つこともありうる。 サバール指揮コンセール・デ・ナシオンのメンデルスゾーン～刺激的かつフレッシュな《イタリア》 サバール指揮のコンサートは、もはや一回一回に聴き逃せない重みがある © Fabian Schellhorn ムジークフェスト2日目（8月29日）には、ジョルディ・サバールが手兵のコンセール・デ・ナシオンと客演した。本コーナーで同じ顔ぶれによる今年3月のオール・モーツァルトのコンサートを紹介しているが、サバール指揮の公演はもはや一回一回が聴き逃せない重みを増している。今回のオール・メンデルスゾーンのプログラムも、フィルハーモニーはほぼ満席だった。 メンデルスゾーン「交響曲第3番《スコットランド》」と「第4番《イタリア》」、その間に「序曲《フィンガルの洞窟》」を挟む、一見何の変哲もないプログラムだが、泰斗サバールの手にかかると夢のような時間に変わる。 とくに面白かったのが《イタリア》で、一般的に知られる1833年版ではなく、作曲家がその後手を加えた1834年版がベルリン公演で用いられた。この版で聴くと、とくに第2楽章から第4楽章までの印象がガラリと変わるのだ。 バスのオスティナートで進行する第2楽章は深い祈りのようで、サバールが語るように「J.S.バッハのコラールのような」瞬間さえある（彼はこの楽章をアンコールでもう一度指揮した）。第4楽章のサルタレッロでは、1833年版にはないティンパニの強打が加わり、嵐のように始まる。中間部で弦楽器セクションが目まぐるしいテンポで奏でる音型のやり取りは、ピリオド楽器のコンセール・デ・ナシオンによっていっそう明晰に浮かび上がる。これほど刺激的かつフレッシュな《イタリア》体験は初めてだった。 前半の《スコットランド》では陰影の深さと共に、スコットランドの民族舞踊の生き生きとした表現が光った。ムジークフェストへのインタヴューで、サバールは「私はかつて17世紀の原典を用いて、スコットランド音楽の研究に4年間を費やした」と明かしているが、あらゆる時代と地域の音楽を吸収してきたサバール指揮の演奏には、人間の文化のなかで育まれてきた音楽の「養分」がぎっしり詰まっている。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items.body: Cocteau Twins released their sixth studio album, “Heaven or Las Vegas,” through 4AD on 17 September 1990, with Capitol Records distributing the album in the United States. The dream pop record turns 36 this year. The trio, vocalist Elizabeth Fraser, guitarist Robin Guthrie and bassist Simon Raymonde, wrote, recorded and produced “Heaven or Las Vegas” themselves at September Sound, the studio Guthrie set up inside Pete Townshend’s former Eel Pie Studios in Twickenham. The ten-track album opens with “Cherry-coloured Funk” and “Pitch the Baby” and also includes “Iceblink Luck,” “Fifty-fifty Clown,” the title track “Heaven or Las Vegas,” “I Wear Your Ring,” “Fotzepolitic,” “Wolf in the Breast,” “Road, River and Rail” and closer “Frou-frou Foxes in Midsummer Fires.” It followed 1988’s “Blue Bell Knoll” and reached number seven on the UK Albums Chart and number 99 on the US Billboard 200. “Heaven or Las Vegas” streams on Spotify. About Cocteau Twins Cocteau Twins formed in 1979 in Grangemouth, Scotland, when guitarist Robin Guthrie and bassist Will Heggie began writing songs together, taking their name from a song by fellow Scottish band Simple Minds. Guthrie met 17-year-old Elizabeth Fraser at a Falkirk disco in 1981 and invited her to sing; her wordless, high-register vocal style became the group’s signature. The trio signed to 4AD in 1982 and released their debut album, “Garlands,” the same year, followed by “Head over Heels” in 1983. Heggie left after “Head over Heels” and was replaced by multi-instrumentalist Simon Raymonde, who joined in time for 1984’s “Treasure,” the band’s first UK Top 40 album. Cocteau Twins released two albums in 1986, “Victorialand” and a collaboration with ambient composer Harold Budd titled “The Moon and the Melodies,” before “Blue Bell Knoll” (1988) became their first record to chart on the US Billboard 200. “Heaven or Las Vegas” followed on 17 September 1990, recorded and self-produced at the band’s own September Sound studio, and became the trio’s highest-charting UK album. Cocteau Twins left 4AD after the record and signed to Fontana, releasing “Four-Calendar Café” (1993) and “Milk & Kisses” (1996) before disbanding in 1997. Guthrie and Raymonde have continued releasing music individually since: Side-Line reported on Raymonde’s Bella Union label presenting the debut album by his project Lost Horizons in 2017, and on Guthrie’s ‘Riviera’ EP in 2021 and his 60th-birthday ‘Springtime’ EP in 2022. Fraser also returned to recording in 2022, her first new material in 13 years, as Side-Line reported. “Heaven or Las Vegas” turns 36 this year, still marking the commercial high point of the band’s decade-long run on 4AD.

items.body: María Dueñas partners with Gustavo Dudamel and the Simón Bolívar Symphony Orchestra of Venezuela to celebrate an artist she has long regarded as an inspiration. Jascha Heifetz’s vinyl recordings of the major works presented here—Lalo’s Symphonie espagnole and Korngold’s Violin Concerto—were ones she grew up with. She also had the opportunity to record three of the accompanying shorter works on his own 1731 ‘Heifetz, Piel’ Stradivarius. Homage to Heifetz Amazon Presto Apple Dueñas mentions that Heifetz’s soul and fire are what have shaped her own playing, and a work as striking as the Symphonie espagnole is a fitting vehicle for those qualities. The orchestra plays a part-and-parcel role in driving the extroverted, passionate spirit of the concerto, and their punchy entrance in the Allegro non troppo (track 1) commands undivided attention. Dueñas plays with plenty of verve (the opening is perhaps even more emphatic than her predecessor’s recording with William Steinberg and the RCA Victor Symphony Orchestra); there is, however, another, complementary persona that embraces lyricism and poignancy and ensures the melodiousness of Lalo’s writing is never lost. Where Dueñas and Heifetz sound most similar is perhaps in the middle register, as both lean into the strings with their bows to draw a warm, resonant presence. The Scherzando exudes playful charm as Dueñas adds a coy innocence that contrasts with the smoldering tempestuousness of the previous movement. The Bolívar players evoke a delightful levity in their neat pizzicatos and trills, upon which the soloist builds an improvisatory feel in her part. The Intermezzo (track 3) shares the vibrant character heard in the Allegro non troppo, but it is the Andante (track 4) that captures the deepest sense of pathos. The ensemble’s thick sostenuto gives Dueñas a rich background texture to work with, and her wide expressive range doesn’t disappoint: some sections express sadness at barely above a whisper, while others powerfully evoke a more tragic presence. I found Dueñas’ reading of this movement perhaps the most different from Heifetz’s, which is in some ways less outwardly intense but speaks more soulfully and profoundly to the listener. Korngold’s Violin Concerto possesses intensity, but in a manner different from the melodrama of the Lalo: its harmonic language is more adventurous and its phrasal architecture more expansive. The Moderato nobile (track 6) draws its intensity from anticipation. Dueñas shows plenty of staying power in the held notes of the high register and, together with sparkling fingerwork, reveals the composer’s lush language. The comparison with Heifetz’s recording reveals some interesting distinctions, though both capture Korngold’s cinematic essence. I found Dueñas’ tone headier and at times angular (owing partly to the bright timbre of her instrument), going hand in hand with her rhapsodic treatment of the virtuosic passages. Heifetz’s sound, meanwhile, is generally smoother yet resonant, evoking nostalgia in choice moments. The Romance (track 7) is gorgeous, capturing the tender and dreamy side of the work. Dueñas’ ability to switch to a more gossamer sound is impressive, showing that she is as much at ease with nuance as with sensation. The orchestra is highly responsive to the soloist, meeting her at every turn in its color changes and phrase contouring. The intricacies of the swashbuckling Finale (track 8) are expertly synchronized between the forces, and despite all that is going on texturally and tonally, passages are approached with clarity and ease. I was curious to hear how the switch of instrument in three of the shorter works would influence the readings. Dueñas performs Léon Roques’ arrangement of Debussy’s La plus que lente (track 10) on the Piel, and we immediately hear the violin speak in a way that recalls Heifetz’s recordings of the two concertos. The timbre is subtler yet more complex in its husky, vocal profile. Combined with her lithe phrasing and lovely soft dynamics, the result is limpid and otherworldly. Heifetz’s arrangement of La chevelure from the Chansons de Bilitis (track 11) sounds deeply intimate, with Dueñas channeling the instrument’s throatiness to create enigma and suspense. Pianist Itamar Golan proves equally receptive to the dark, almost sinister undertones. Dueñas and her collaborators give top-notch performances that do justice to a heartfelt homage. items.body: Industrial rock band Engines of Aggression release the single Wargames on September 28, 2026, through Phoenix, Arizona outfit Sonic 9 Entertainment. A private pre-release preview of the track is available now on the band’s official site. “Wargames” follows the 2025 singles “Start a War” and “Nightmare in Pain Town.” Engines of Aggression describe “Wargames” as mixing mechanized industrial rhythms with a hard-rock edge in the vein of Rob Zombie and Static-X. The current lineup is Tripp on vocals, Ríos on guitar, Sterling on bass and Deech on drums. The band’s own materials state that Engines of Aggression headlined the Whisky a Go Go on the mid-1990s Los Angeles club circuit, with Korn and System of a Down opening for them at the time, and that the band shared bills with Danzig and Henry Rollins. About Engines of Aggression Engines of Aggression formed in Los Angeles in the early 1990s around frontman Tripp Holland, who recruited guitarist Rik Schaffer, drummer Craig Dollinger and bassist Douglas Van Dyck. The band released the “Speak” EP in 1993 on Priority Records and the debut album “Inhuman Nature” in 1994, issued by Priority Records in the US and Virgin in Europe. “Inhuman Nature” was produced by Lamar Lowder, mixed and engineered by Brian Jenkens and mastered by Tom Baker. The band built a following on the Sunset Strip club circuit through the mid-1990s before a collapsed record deal and internal conflict ended that run of activity. Engines of Aggression returned in the 2020s, relocating to Phoenix, Arizona under Sonic 9 Entertainment. The band released “The Black E.P.,” originally issued only in Japan, on June 14, 2024, produced by Steve Duda, whose credits include Nine Inch Nails, Deadmau5 and Rob Zombie. The EP’s four tracks are “New Shanghai,” “Let U Down,” “Moto Psycho” and “Go Fanatic.” The comeback continued through 2025 with the singles “Start a War” and “Nightmare in Pain Town,” both produced with longtime collaborator Lamar Lowder. The current lineup comprises Tripp (vocals), Ríos (guitar), Sterling (bass) and Deech (drums). “Wargames,” due September 28, 2026, is the band’s next single following that 2025 run.

items.body: On October 2, 2026, Arsine Tibé releases the instrumental EP “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode III)”. The German project is the solo work of Manfred Thomaser, known from the synthpop duo !Distain, and the new EP continues the Lounge Noire Sessions series that began earlier in 2026. ‘The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode III)’ continues the series “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode III)” follows “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode I)” and “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode II)”, which Arsine Tibé released on June 19, 2026. Unlike “Reclaimed”, the concept mini-album Thomaser released in August 2026 with vocalist Suzanne Letting, Episode III returns to the instrumental format of the first two Lounge Noire Sessions EPs. No streaming or purchase links for the EP have gone live yet ahead of the October 2 release date. About Arsine Tibé Arsine Tibé is the Lounge Noire and electronic pop solo project of Manfred Thomaser, based in Munich, Germany. Thomaser describes the project’s sound as drawing on lounge, soundtrack, ambient, new wave, electro and pop elements. He is best known as one half of !Distain, the German synthpop duo he shares with Alexander Braun, and has also worked on the projects Demokratie and The Independent Seasons. Side-Line first covered Arsine Tibé in February 2016, when Thomaser launched a mini-album under the project name, led by the track “Obligation”. The Arsine Tibé discography grew through releases such as “We Came To Fail”, “Good Evening, The Mountain Said” and “The Copy”, issued through the area db imprint, alongside collaborations with Suzanne Letting including “Beyond the Point (feat. Suzanne Letting)”. In 2026 Thomaser opened the Lounge Noire Sessions series with “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode I)”, followed by “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode II)” on June 19. Arsine Tibé and Letting then released the four-track concept mini-album “Reclaimed” on August 7, 2026, with proceeds tied to a Refuge fundraiser. “The Lounge Noire Sessions (Episode III)”, out October 2, 2026, continues the instrumental EP series alongside that ongoing collaborative work.
