items.excerpt: Metropolis Records presses 16Volt‘s “LetDownCrush” on yellow vinyl for the first time, marking 30 years since the industrial rock album’s original release with a limited edition of 300 copies out 9 October 2026. LetDownCrush by 16volt “LetDownCrush” first appeared on 7 August 1996 through Cargo and Re-Constriction Records, the third 16Volt studio album after “Wisdom” (1993) and “Skin” (1994) and the last the band released on Re-Constric
items.body: Metropolis Records presses 16Volt‘s “LetDownCrush” on yellow vinyl for the first time, marking 30 years since the industrial rock album’s original release with a limited edition of 300 copies out 9 October 2026. LetDownCrush by 16volt “LetDownCrush” first appeared on 7 August 1996 through Cargo and Re-Constriction Records, the third 16Volt studio album after “Wisdom” (1993) and “Skin” (1994) and the last the band released on Re-Constriction before signing to Metropolis. The album stayed out of print for 15 years until Metropolis remastered and reissued it on CD in 2012, adding a cover of Cypress Hill’s “We Ain’t Goin’ Out Like That” as a bonus track. The new vinyl edition carries the original ten-track sequence plus that bonus cut. 16Volt is the project of Portland-formed vocalist, guitarist and producer Eric Powell, who wrote or co-wrote every song on “LetDownCrush” with guitarist Marc LaCorte, credited on four tracks. Guest vocalist Stella “Soleil” Katsoudas features on opener “Swarm,” Dan Pred plays live drums on “A Cloth Like Gauze,” and the late guitarist William Tucker contributes additional and lead guitar. Jeff “Critter” Newell produced and engineered alongside Powell. Tracks “The Dreams That Rot in Your Heart” and “The Cut Collector” have remained fixtures of the band’s live sets since the album’s release. 16Volt’s release history since ‘LetDownCrush’ 16Volt followed “LetDownCrush” with “SuperCoolNothing” (1998, Re-Constriction) before moving to Metropolis Records for “FullBlackHabit” (2007), “American Porn Songs” (2009) and “Beating Dead Horses” (2011). Side-Line previously covered the band’s remastered reissue of its debut album “Wisdom” and its 2024 return with “NegativeOnArrivals,” a compilation drawing on the self-released “The Negative Space” (2016) and “Dead on Arrivals” (2017), which Metropolis also reissued that same year. 16Volt’s most recent studio album, “More of Less,” arrived on Metropolis on 25 July 2025. About 16Volt 16Volt was formed in Portland, Oregon, by vocalist, guitarist and producer Eric Powell in 1988. Powell recruited drummer Joel Bornzin, guitarist Jon Fell and Jeff Taylor to record “Motorskill,” which appeared on the “Cyberflesh Conspiracy” various-artists compilation on If It Moves. The band signed to Re-Constriction Records and released its debut album, “Wisdom,” on 25 May 1993, followed by “Skin” in 1994 and “LetDownCrush” in 1996. 16Volt closed out its run on Re-Constriction with “SuperCoolNothing” in 1998. The band later contributed nine tracks, three written specifically for the game, to the soundtrack of the video game “Primal.” 16Volt signed to Metropolis Records for “FullBlackHabit” (2007), “American Porn Songs” (2009) and “Beating Dead Horses” (2011). Powell self-released “The Negative Space” (2016) and “Dead on Arrivals” (2017) on his own Murder Creek label before the band went on hiatus. Powell reactivated 16Volt in 2024 with “NegativeOnArrivals,” combining material from those two self-released records for wider distribution, and followed it with the new studio album “More of Less” on Metropolis in July 2025. The current lineup is Powell on vocals, John “Servo” DeSalvo on drums, “Mindcage” Rick Furr on guitars and Jim Semonik on keyboards. The 30th-anniversary yellow vinyl pressing of “LetDownCrush” places the band’s first Metropolis-era physical reissue of the album alongside its recent run of new and archival releases on the label.

The track pairs electronic rhythms with a synthpop hook built around themes of nostalgia and longing, and arrives with an animated video the duo produced themselves. Hipster Slaves release ‘Fine Young Hands’ on Bald Freak Music Hipster Slaves pairs Pennie, also known for his work with Cohe
items.body: Dillinger Escape Plan co-founder and drummer Chris Pennie’s electronic duo Hipster Slaves releases the new single “Fine Young Hands” on 25 September 2026 through Bald Freak Music. The track pairs electronic rhythms with a synthpop hook built around themes of nostalgia and longing, and arrives with an animated video the duo produced themselves. Hipster Slaves release ‘Fine Young Hands’ on Bald Freak Music Hipster Slaves pairs Pennie, also known for his work with Coheed and Cambria, with singer, synth and piano player Ron Scalzo, the founder of Bald Freak Music. Scalzo sings and plays synths from Nashville while Pennie handles drums, synths and guitars from New York City. “Fine Young Hands” follows the project’s self-titled 2019 debut EP, and Bald Freak Music has a full-length Hipster Slaves album planned for 2027. The single is available to pre-save ahead of release through a DistroKid hyperfollow page, which links to a Spotify pre-save and to the duo’s Bandcamp page. The official video for “Fine Young Hands” is out now on YouTube. About Hipster Slaves Hipster Slaves is the electronic duo of Ron Scalzo and Chris Pennie. Scalzo founded Bald Freak Music, an independent record label and production house, in 2005, releasing his own work in the electronic project Q*Ball alongside guitarist Ron “Bumblefoot” Thal, as well as albums from Bumblefoot, Black Pig and Swashbuckle. In 2006, Scalzo joined guitarist Brett Aveni and Dillinger Escape Plan drummer Chris Pennie to form the alternative rock band Return To Earth, whose debut album, “Captains of Industry,” followed that year. Return To Earth signed to Metal Blade Records and released its second album, “Automata,” in 2010, reunited in 2020, and released “Oblivion” through Bald Freak Music in 2022, followed by the four-song release “Octavius” in 2024. Pennie co-founded the mathcore band The Dillinger Escape Plan with guitarist Ben Weinman in 1997 and remained its drummer through the band’s early catalog before later serving as the drummer for Coheed and Cambria between 2007 and 2011. He also contributed drums to releases by Idiot Pilot, The Armed and Greg Puciato. Hipster Slaves released its self-titled three-track debut EP, featuring the songs “Pitchforks,” “Hipster Slaves” and “Near Dark,” on Bandcamp on 11 November 2019. Scalzo also hosts the Independent Minded podcast and The Joy of Bob Ross podcast, both produced through Bald Freak Music. “Fine Young Hands,” out 25 September 2026, is the first new Hipster Slaves single since that debut and precedes a full-length album the duo has planned for 2027.

items.body: Catherine Ringer, vocalist, songwriter, and co-founder of French new wave duo Les Rita Mitsouko, has died at age 68. Her children announced her death in a statement to AFP, confirming that she died from cancer on the night of September 14, 2026. With her partner in music and life, Fred Chichin, Ringer made pop music feel large enough to accommodate almost anything: punk impatience, funk, cabaret, electronic experimentation, and the expressive possibilities of French chanson. A song could be funny, sensual, disconcerting, and profoundly sad within the same few minutes. Ringer gave each feeling its own physical presence, singing with a freedom that made conventional ideas of good taste seem rather timid. Born on October 18, 1957, in Suresnes, near Paris, she was the daughter of painter Sam Ringer, a Polish-born Jewish Holocaust survivor, and an architect mother. She left school at 15 and pursued an artistic education through theatre, music, and dance. Among the formative figures in her life was Argentine dancer and choreographer Marcia Moretto, who became her teacher and collaborator. Those years onstage helped establish the connection between movement and voice that would distinguish her work with Les Rita Mitsouko. Nostalgie’s biography documents her early performances and work with Moretto. Ringer met Chichin in 1979, beginning a partnership that would carry them from the Paris underground to international recognition. Their self-titled 1984 debut, recorded with Conny Plank, introduced a group whose appetite for experiment came with a formidable instinct for melody. As Coilhouse’s retrospective observed, Ringer’s background in avant-garde theatre remained visible in the duo’s performances and videos. Marcia Baïla became their breakthrough. Written in remembrance of Moretto following her death from cancer, it joined the exhilaration of dance to the shock of losing someone whose life had been devoted to movement. Its popularity carried that private grief into public celebration. The song offers an especially poignant way to remember Ringer now: affection, anger, and delight sharing the same space, with no easy separation between them. Directed by Philippe Gautier, the music video for Marcia Baïla gave the song an equally extravagant visual life, with costumes by Jean Paul Gaultier and Thierry Mugler. Watch the video below. The duo’s collaboration with Tony Visconti on The No Comprendo in 1986 brought Andy, C’est comme ça, and Les Histoires d’A. The album won at the 1987 Victoires de la Musique, as did Jean-Baptiste Mondino’s video for C’est comme ça. These songs remain an excellent introduction to Ringer’s range: the teasing insistence of Andy, the sharp attack of C’est comme ça, and the ease with which she could make a repeated phrase feel like an argument, an invitation, or a joke. Their creative world extended well beyond records. Jean-Luc Godard included the duo at work in his 1987 film Soigne ta droite, while collaborations brought them together with fellow musical eccentrics. Sparks joined them for Singing in the Shower, from 1988’s Marc & Robert, a meeting of artists who understood how much pleasure could be found in pop’s peculiar corners. Later, Iggy Pop appeared on My Love Is Bad, preserved alongside their other collaborations in the band’s collected catalogue. The apparent playfulness could also carry terrible knowledge. Le Petit Train addressed the deportation trains of the Holocaust, a history bound closely to her father’s survival. Its video, filmed in Bombay, placed Ringer amid exuberant dancing while the words described people being carried toward their deaths. The tension between the music’s invitation and the lyric’s meaning remains deeply unsettling. She understood how a familiar pleasure could open an audience to something painful. Chichin died from cancer in 2007, aged 53, the year Les Rita Mitsouko released Variéty. Ringer continued performing their songs while building a solo catalogue that included Ring n’ Roll in 2011 and Chroniques et fantaisies in 2017. With Plaza Francia, alongside Gotan Project’s Eduardo Makaroff and Christoph H. Müller, she explored tango on 2014’s A New Tango Song Book. Her later work also returned to the intimacy of spoken language. In L’Érotisme de vivre, she performed the poetry of Alice Mendelson, accompanied by pianist Grégoire Hetzel under the direction of Mauro Gioia. The scale had changed, but the curiosity remained: another writer, another setting, another way to give words a body. Ringer leaves music full of appetite and contradiction, open to beauty without becoming polite about it. She made eccentricity feel generous, something an audience could participate in. Our thoughts are with her family, friends, collaborators, and everyone who found freedom in her voice. Follow Catherine Ringer: Instagram Facebook Follow Les Rita Mitsouko Instagram YouTube Bandcamp The post Catherine Ringer, the Extraordinary Voice of Les Rita Mitsouko, Has Passed Away at 68 appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

シーズンプログラムは、厳しい状況下においても音楽的探求とオーケストラの成長を止めてはならない、という強い意志と意義が込められている。 沼尻 神奈川フィルにとっての初演作品や大編成曲にも積極的に取り組んでいきたいと思っています。就任時からの念願であったラヴェル《ダフニスとクロエ》（全曲）や、名曲でありながら大編成ゆえ演奏機会の少ないシャブリエ《楽しい行進曲》、決して演奏機会は多くなく他の楽団も取り上げることの珍しいシェーンベルク《ペレアスとメリザンド》などを意欲的に取り入れています。 上野理事長は、主要な会場である横浜みなとみらいホールが2028年4月から1年間の改修休館に入ることへの危惧を表明。さらに同時期に休館・長期休館のミューザ川崎シンフォニーホール（2028年度後半〜29年のうち約1年間）や神奈川県民ホール（2025年4月1日～期間は未定）にも触れ、楽団を挙げて全力で乗り切る意向を示した。 沼尻音楽監督は、「劇場問題などで日本で本格的なオペラを上演することが難しくなりつつある中、オーケストラが主体となって質の高い上演を継続することは、日本のオペラ文化のレベルをキープするためにも非常に重要」と、オーケストラが担うべき文化継承の役割を訴えた。 2027-2028シーズンは、神奈川フィルにとって初演となる作品の多いプログラム。まさに「挑戦の年」となる。拠点ホールの改修休館という課題を控えつつも、作品の真髄を突くプログラミングで挑む神奈川フィルの新シーズンに期待したい。 2027-2028シーズンプログラム みなとみらいシリーズ 会場：横浜みなとみらいホール 第422回 2027年4月24日（土）14:00 指揮：沼尻竜典（音楽監督） items.body:
Yung Raja has been announced as the REP for ComplexCon Asia’s SHOW UP 001, the first edition of the new live music platform celebrating homegrown communities and cultures across Asia. The event will take place on 8 October at Capitol Theatre in Singapore.

As the inaugural REP, the Singaporean rapper and songwriter has curated a lineup bringing together different generations of the city’s hip-hop scene alongside artists from across the region.

“I’ve been working relentlessly over the last decade to put Singapore on the map,” shared Yung Raja. “It means a lot to be given the opportunity by ComplexCon Asia to represent the country at large.”

Joining Yung Raja on the Singapore front are Akeem Jahat, Mary Sue, and BDK NIP, bringing together established and emerging voices in local rap.

The programme will also extend beyond the mic. DJ KoFlow will bring his turntable wizardry to the decks, while LI.A will shift the focus to Singapore’s dance community with a cypher featuring poppers, lockers, and freestyle dancers. DJ Zai and street-dance studio AK.Kreates are also part of the lineup.

SHOW UP 001 will welcome a slate of regional names as well, including Chinese-American rapper Bohan Phoenix and Indonesian rapper Ramengvrl. Japan’s DJ Koco, aka SHIMOKITA, and Yeti Out co-founder Tom Yeti will also take over the decks, bringing sounds spanning hip-hop, funk, soul, disco, jazz, and more to the night.

For Yung Raja, the event is ultimately about creating space for the communities that have built Singapore’s hip-hop culture.

“Singapore has so much talent, but sometimes you need someone to open the door and give you the stage. SHOW UP is our way of doing that,” he said. “It’s about putting artists in a room, giving them a real platform, and letting them in the most literal terms show up for themselves, their community and what they believe in.”

SHOW UP is a new live music platform by ComplexCon Asia that aims to connect artists, cities, and audiences around the region, building towards ComplexCon Hong Kong in 2027. Each edition will be developed alongside a local REP, who will curate a lineup representing their city and its wider regional community.

Early-bird tickets are on sale here.

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets
